review_title: Very small salt crystals, but smells good!
review_text:
The best way to describe the scent of this exfoliating scrub is to say it smells like you just walked into a day spa. It's a truly lovely smell, light, fresh, salty, and luxurious. I've actually tried using it as a lotion instead because the fragrance is so nice, but it didn't really work out. It's very creamy, though, and when you put a dollop in your hand, it might seem like there aren't any salt crystals in it, because the cream is thick like lotion.
There was quite a bit of settling in the packaging when I opened the jar, and since I ended up using quite a bit in the shower, I don't think it'll last very long--perhaps a month. The salt crystals are very small, and when I tried to vigorously scrub, it washed away before I could properly exfoliate.
How I recommend using it, in order to get the best use out of the Himalayan salt is to wet your leg before you step unto the shower, so it's a little more than damp. Then take a dollop and scrub your leg, and when you're done with whatever appendages you wanted to exfoliate, hop in the shower and rinse it off. Somehow, when my legs and arms were really drenched, the scrub just slid right off. Less moisture helped it adhere better. The smell really is great and refreshing, and once I've figured out how to use it, I've started enjoying it more.

review_title: Flower very nice, but birdcage veil difficult to handle
review_text:
I purchased this for my upcoming wedding. The flower (called a "fascinator" in the bridal industry, I'm learning) is very nice, and I will definitely wear it. I may cut the wires with the bling off, but that's just me. I'm having a simple summer picnic wedding with a white, cotton halter dress, and the bling might be a bit too much. I am going to ask my best friend before making this decision. Either way, it's a nice piece.

The birdcage veil, though, wasn't really how it's pictured. In the photo it seems to have a lot more conformity to a human head than the actual piece that showed up in my mailbox. The real thing starts out unruly, and popped up in weird places on my head. I tried calming the thing down with bobby pins, but it still looked unshapely. Finally, though, after watching the company's videos (they give you a piece of paper with a link to some instructional videos) and keeping it near the shower for a few days to get it to calm down, it did actually look good. I have a large head with puffy hair, and I found that if I put the comb towards the back of my head on the right, and allow the veil to come up over top my head from the back right, hanging down around my face, that the veil's large size is actually an asset, because it covers my puffy hair without flattening it.

I was so worried about the veil that I ordered a separate, handmade birdcage veil from etsy for $30 (see it at pompandplumage.com) that I hoped would be more what I'm looking for. When it arrived, though, it was too small to wear without wearing my puffy hairstyle slicked back, which isn't how I plan to wear my hair. I actually went back to the cheaper veil I bought here on amazon.

Whatever you end up doing with the veil portion, the flower/fascinator is nice enough, and cheap enough, that it's still worth the purchase. The flower/fascinators on the same site on etsy where I purchase the other birdcage veil, pompandplumage.com, are $60-$70, and look similar, so even without the veil, this was a good deal.

review_title: Good product but quantity misleading: Only one pen included!
review_text:
Is it just me? I have purchased this exact product several times--happily--in dark brown, grey brown, and chestnut (red brown). My eyebrows are, like my natural hair, about a level 4 or 5 dark brown, and the grey brown is probably the closest, though the other colors are handy for changes of color to hair and makeup. My brows are thinning, but a little filling in does the trick, and these pens are my favorite tool for the job, as they both color in where you need solid filling and can be used to make feathery strokes for a more natural brow look. This pen came with a useless little razor and three eyebrow "templates," only one of which I might consider useful (if you are new to shaping your brows).
The problem:
In the past I have received (I see now from other sellers) at least two or three pens for $6.99 to $8.99. I can't believe I paid over $8 for just one pen from this seller "Generies." Going back over the seller page, I see that indeed, by the pictures it appears that one will receive two pens. A sneaky little trick, showing the same photos as the sellers with better deals, but neglecting to include the "2 CT." If you are busy or distracted in the least, you might fall for it, as did I--and doubtless, as have many customers.
I really dislike writing negative comments, but am doing this to save others the trouble and disappointment of feeling ripped off. Needless to say, I will be buying this product from other sellers in future--the ones with the more reasonable--and honest--deals.

review_title: Needs Some Work to Make it work!
review_text: This was my first experience with a wig that wasn’t from Spirit Halloween and I can’t say it was much better. After trying this wig I decided to learn a little more about wigs and I found a ton of info out there about them and how to do a little work on the less expensive ones to make them look better. (ie: thinning them out, plucking the part and hairline, etc.) I also learned about the features of a wig that make it look more realistic, such as synthetic vs human hair/human hair blend, pre-plucked and lace front. Now that I know a bit about wigs I feel more optimistic that I’ll be able to find ones that are affordable yet look more realistic and/or that I’ll be able to work on them a bit to make them look more so. In summary: The part and thickness on this wig are what I think need the most work. There’s virtually no part and the hair on the top is much too dense and puffy. This could be rectified by plucking but the wig is just not worth the work, IMO. The style of it is cute—The length and the waviness of it were exactly what I was looking for. I can’t say the same about the bangs but that’s the part of the wig that would benefit from some plucking and thinning out. The softness is pretty good for a synthetic wig.  I can’t comment on tangling because I didn’t keep the wig long enough to see how it holds up. The color is hard to comment on because it looks so different depending on the light—It can look like an ashy light brown with subtle highlights, a darker, less ashy light brown with no dimension to it, and in others it appears to have a mauve-like tinge to it. (You can see the differences in the pics.) In the end I returned this wig and after doing more research I decided I wouldn’t buy another inexpensive synthetic hair wig and instead look for a human hair blend that may be a little more expensive but looks more realistic. The bottom line: I recommend not buying this wig unless you know how to work on a wig to make it look more realistic.

review_title: Nice kit for beginners/parent child activity
review_text:
I purchased this for my 7 year olds birthday. We got around to doing it tonite, finally. Overall, we were very pleased with this kit. Make sure the water temp and oil temps are spot on, add them and mix. Let sit, mix, let sit, mix, let sit, mix, etc. I was surprised how simple it was. It's nice how they combine oils and make everything into convenient packets of mixtures. Not having to measure really helps you focus on making the actual product while still keeping my daughters attention. She enjoyed this very much and was so eager for us to be able to stop mixing it and bottling it up.
My only gripe is the amount of lotion. We wanted to play with scents, so we used flavor oils we found in our cupboards. But, because they are tiny 2 oz jars, it was difficult to experiment with different scents. We did end up just taking out 2 oz of lotion, scenting, bottling, repeat. But, it was kind of annoying. For double the price of this kit, I saw another kit that makes 4x this amount of lotion. But, I believe ingredient wise, this kit is better. I love that this company chooses a natural preservative and that they use essential oils for scent. (It only comes with 1 scent - lavender) To make this kit better, they should increase the amount of lotion this makes and maybe offer a variety of essential oils to make a few different scents. I also wasn't quite clear on if they used unrefined or refined mango butter, but considering the small amount, it's not a huge deal. For the first timer, this is a great intro to DIY AND THE BEST PART: the lotion is lovely!! Makes my hands so soft and isn't greasy. I'm going to try making more lotions on my own :) My daughter was so proud and just loved labeling her lotions and giving one to her brothers.

This is a very thin, clear oil. It isn’t as thick as baby oil and runs almost like water. I would never put oil or an oil-based product on my skin because it clogs the pores. What I did use this for is my hair, which is very thick and very dry. After shampooing, I poured a little bit of the oil into my hand and rubbed my hands together. Then I ran my hands through my hair, keeping the oil away from the scalp area. Afterwards, I blew my hair dry then applied more oil. Usually, I apply a gel in the same manner that calms the frizz and leaves my hair with a nice shine to it. However, the oil did not produce the same results. My hair still had flyaway ends with no gloss to it. My newly washed and dried hair always looks better the next morning after the hair product has had a chance to calm the frizzy hair shafts, but the morning after I used the oil, the results were no different than the night before.

I’ll stick to my gel product to end the frizziness of dry hair.

Disappointed. The scents include a "musk", florals (Jasmine, Lily, Honeysuckle) and a "vanilla", which should be a warning. High-end designer scents may be derived or contain some of these "notes", but do not stop there. The "musk" referred to as "amber musk" is the most subtle and acceptable of these; it is somewhat "softer" than the old, familiar drugstore variety that had its heyday in the '80s. The florals smell cheap; very few fragrances use essence of living flowers and that is necessary to distill a true floral scent. The jasmine has a "brassy" top note as does the honeysuckle. No one should do "vanilla" anymore; it is a cloying and overwhelming smell (not scent), rather than a complex "caramel", and this one is no different. (Acqua di Parma is the only line that includes "vanilla" notes in its scents that have class and understatement.) These scents are nicely packaged in glass bottles and a laminated cardboard box with the brand name stenciled on it. But not nearly worth the price.

review_title: The good, the bad and the ugly...
review_text:
My review consists of the good, the bad and the ugly. First,
the good - I finally found a curler that 'fits' my eyelid. Huh, you say? Well, it appears that most of the manufacturers believe I have golf balls instead of human eyes. The tool's shape is long and shallow enough of a curve to catch most of the eyelashes. It is comfortable to use, but takes a bit of practice. Once you are comfortable with the scissor motion (sorry, no other way to describe it) used to make the curl, you are rewarded with a nice, non-crimpy curl. The pad in this one is the best I have used. This tool also opens wide enough that even the most nearsighted or lush lashed amoungst us can get it close to the base of the upper lashes. The design over all is very well thought out. I recommend using an magnifying mirror if you have to use bifocals (I do). All that said, now...
the bad - there is no replacement pad and I am questioning how sanitary this is going to be in the long run. I agree completely with folks here who advise to REMOVE ALL EYE MAKEUP before use. Ain't nothing pretty about an eye infection. I am wondering out loud how to properly clean this curler to be certain it remains safe. If you are prone to sties and other types of infection, I would be asking the same questions. Which leads to...
the ugly - until you practice and are used to it (won't take long) the results are a bit odd looking. The black pad is plushier and looks to be made of silicone and not the usual hard rubber. I have found that the hard rubber pads are chiefly responsible for that weird ugly crimp you can get. Not so with this one. I mentioned before the squeezy scissor action your thumb and index finger have to use can be tricky. If you have coordination issues, well - things could get ugly.
SUGGESTIONS for use...wash your hands before use. I keep the little plastic clip to keep the tool closed. You could follow the advise of one person here to heat the tool with a dryer, but I think I may skip that. Use a makeup mirror to assist you. Practice when you have some time. Enjoy, Ladies - get out there and be lovely.

review_title: works well, but has a minor design flaw
review_text:
I have used ionizing brushes for over 30 years—since they were first sold by Sharper Image. The negative ions work very well to flatten the surface of the cuticle of each hair, making the hair less likely to break or split, and also softer.

This particular brush works well, but the one I received has a minor design flaw: the brush part pops off so easily that I have to hold it tight with my thumb, making it less ergonomic than it might be... not an issue for me. As for the vibrating part, I couldn't tell, but that's not what I bought it for. This brush generates NO heat, which is exactly what I wanted. Unlike some similar products, there are NO seams that could catch the hair.

TIPS FOR ALL IONIZING BRUSHES:
(1) if they don't need electricity (cord or batteries), they're not the real deal
(2) heating elements, just like heated blow-drying, tend to dry out your hair and make it more brittle: even oily hair can get dried out
(3) brush your hair SLOWLY to get the best result
(4) if your hair is flatter after using it, and you don't like that, bend over and brush it upside down to get more volume

review_title: It's not what I thought it would be
review_text:
I gave this 3 stars for "Softness" because the brush is average to a bit firmer than what would be ideal and comfortable to use on your back, while the loofah strap is average. The brush bristles are kind of scratchy and not the "good exfoliating" kind of scratchy. They're more like the "ouch, that's scratching me" kind of scratchy. Overall, though, it's acceptable and average.

Next, I gave this 2 stars for "Easy to use" because I don't find this easy to use. The brush is separate from the stick that extends it to reach your back; you slide the oval-shaped brush onto the stick by inserting the stick into a cut out section on the back side brush. The problem here is that it doesn't stay on firmly at all. I ended up with 2 options: either not on firmly enough, so it kept popping off, or pushed on so much that it's very difficult to get off of the stick to use separately. The loofah strap is really easy to use, though. It's nice and long so there's plenty of length to comfortably hold each end and move it back and forth at most angles, no matter how thin or thick your arms or body may be. That's a real plus! But I still couldn't give more stars if only half of the set is easily usable.

Finally, I gave this 4 stars for sturdiness because there's no doubt, it seems pretty sturdy. The bristles on the brush have stayed intact. The loofah strap is firm and sewn solidly -- but it may be too firm. It's hard to get flexibility out of it. The elastic strap handle on the brush is flimsy, but overall, it's a solid set. The wood is a good, solid, well-finished wood without splits or cracks. It doesn't seem like a cheap product that's going to warp and break easily if you keep it away from hanging to be soaked when it's not needed for use. Putting it somewhere nearby where it stays dry is best.

I usually get packs of cheapola showercaps from the dollar store (like a six pack of plastic bags with a rubberband, you know?) but they don't last long... So I had a vinyl one that lasted longer, but was really just that same old design that was just plastic tied to your head with elastic...

This shower cap is... well, frankly, after the other ones I've used... luxurious. The material is not plastic, but more like the soft nylon on my windbreaker jacket. It's much quieter when I'm in the shower, which makes for a more peaceful bathing experience. It is also more comfortable, as the headband is more fitted. It's especially comfortable if you wear it over your ears... there's no pressure anywhere, but it still keeps your hair dry. I, personally, like to have my ears "out," so there is some pressure to the top of my ears where the headband sits, but I don't mind it.

The headband does stretch a bit for head size, but not as much as you might be used to if you've used shower caps with elastic bands. I kind of liked this... It makes it easier to get all my hair in it. I flip my head upside down over the shower cap, and the cap just kind of catches my hair like a bucket, and I can just tuck in any stragglers before flipping my head back up. If you need to tighten the headband just a little bit, you can re-tie the bow for a slight adjustment.

No shower cap is going to be completely, perfectly water tight. You're always going to get a little bit of water around the edges unless you're really careful in the shower and take pains to avoid direct spray. I use a shower cap when I take a shower before bed and don't want to go to sleep with wet hair... a little bit of moisture doesn't bother me, as I'm not trying to protect a hairstyle or anything. I really just like the comfort and feel of this cap a lot!

So, after being chemo eyebrow bald (and everywhere else bald too) for almost a year due to breast cancer chemotherapy treatments, when my eye brows finally grew back they were mostly white instead of my natural dark brown. Augh!! Since I am a second time breast cancer warrior with bigger fish to fry — I ignored my mostly white eye brows for about nine months — hoping they would eventually recover their natural dark brown color after my body recovered from all the chemo poison. Nope. Not happening. No such luck.

The mostly white eyebrows bothered me even more than the flat chest double mastectomy— because well a flat chest can be padded but having invisible brows left me feeling washed out and old. So, I decided to fix my brows because that seemed like a doable relatively easy DIY thing. I read lots of articles on home dying eye brows. Then, based on article recommendations, I found this Godfey product on Amazon and after much research and watching DIY “dye your eyebrows at home” videos, I gave it a go and dyed my eyebrows at home exactly one week ago. The results: Yay!!!! As everyone suggested, I put vaseline around my eyebrows to protect my skin. I did one eyebrow at a time rather than both at once. Also, due to my super sensitive skin, I only left the dye on for two minutes per brow. Still, it worked perfectly. My eyebrow hairs are still dark brown — one week after I dyed them. Success!!!

I love having my dark eyebrows back, and sort of feel like me again.

review_title: Beautiful Oil For A Splurge- But Not Worth The Hype
review_text: This is a beautiful oil to treat yourself, but the bottle is misleading. If you look carefully, you can see that the liquid does not reach the bottom, that there is another glass bottom a ways up, making the bottle appear more full than it is. I took a star off for that because that's just not cool. They could make it in a smaller bottle & people would still pay $48 for it. It's a nice product. I wish, however, that it didn't have the olive oil in it, because that's what I think is causing acne in a lot of girls skin. For those with acne or if you just don't want to pay this much, you can get the same "velvet" results with rosehip oil. The Ordinary has one for 10 bucks. Rosehip oil can help reduce your inflammatory acne, get rid of acne scars, and clear your skin. Rosehip oil is an anti-inflammatory, able to reduce swelling and fluid buildup. Rosehip oil has a low rating of 1-2 on the comedogenic scale (a.k.a. not likely to clog dem pores). Plus, the linoleic fatty acids in rosehip oil have been shown to reduce oil production in oily skin types which can help prevent future acne. I received this Velvet Skin Drink as a sample & like others, I was impressed, but I found it for brand new & sealed for $24 on Mercari. Personally, because of the olive oil filler and the bottle deception, I wasn't willing to pay $48. They do some great marketing, evidently, as it's out of stock all the time. They make it sound like it's made of purely grapes, which it's not & the bottle deception just isn't worth the hype. Yes, the product is beautiful & makes your skin very soft, but is it softer than my Ordinary Rosehip oil? Nah. This is something nice to splurge on if I find a good deal, because of the of Sarantoni grapes, Resveratrol and lactic acid. But there are no studies on the benefits of these grapes over other grapes & they don't say how much Resvertal and lactic acid they use. I wouldn't consider this an active of any of those products. The Ordinary has both for cheap.

Hyaluronic Acid? I never knew what it was until recently :) sounds like something you use in the brakes on your car. hyaluronic acid (also known as hyaluronan) is a glycosaminoglycan, a type of molecule composed partly of sugars. Hyaluronic acid is actually a natural structural component of skin, and, in fact, is present in connective tissue throughout the human body.

The awesome thing about Hydrolic Acid is its ability to retain moisture; it’s considered to have a greater capacity to hold moisture than any other natural or synthetic polymer. In fact, one gram of hyaluronic acid is able to hold up to six liters of water. The hallmarks of youthful skin is its moisture content. A dried up face will age you quicker then anything.

Hyaluronic acid can improve your skin’s moisture content and at the same time strengthen skin’s barrier; that is, the outer layers of your skin. A healthy barrier looks and feels softer, smoother, and plumper. This does all of that. Sense menopause I have suffered from dry skin. This has made a big difference in how my face looks and feels. review_title: Great product. Pretty color purple. Good price. Great for nail art!!!
review_text:
I got this to try as a cheaper alternative for liquid Latex nail protector. It arrived quickly. It IS absolutely a much more cost effective alternative for buying the tiny bottles individually. And this company has lots of color options too.

What I did:
I received it and immediately painted it around a nail bed to test it's effectiveness. And since, I've compared it's coverage/ease of use/removability to a product that is intended for nail use (a liquid palisade product).
Results are:
it works EXACTLY the same. No harder or easier to use. So, if someone uses liquid Latex for nail art protection already, this IS absolutely a great alternative!!! Once I knew it would work great, I got out an empty nail polish bottle and used a little mini funnel and poured it in. I also decided to spice it up with glitter, like some of the more popular liquid Latex for nails companies have done...and it works perfectly still, and looks more exciting, and is amazing!
Verdict:
I will continue to buy this as my nail art protection. The other items (that are intended for nail art) work great for the same thing, but this is a cheaper and much more customizable option... which I like!
Keep in mind, you can use any empty polish bottles... just clean them out thoroughly first. The glitter is completely optional...but if you do use it, I recommend ONLY using the cosmetic grade glitters...craft glitters are just too cheap and they bleed and curl and ruin the stuff they get submerged in. And any tiny funnel would help you get it into a different container.

I attached photos.
The pics include:
The actual product. What I used to "make" it easily applicable for nails. What it looks like when immediately applied, once dried (which dries to a darker shade), and how easy it is to remove with no residue!

So, I say, this is a great option for nail art enthusiasts like me, and this product would probably also work for other latex uses (like it is shown on the bottle). So, for my liquid latex needs, I'll go to this product from now on.

I purchased this product in a store, but I am such a fan I had to write a review. Ever since I purchased this palette, it has been my go-to for everyday makeup. I am fair-skinned with dark hair and hazel eyes, and the colors are perfect. I don't always use every color in a palette and I don't always place the colors as directed, but in this case, Stila knows what they are talking about!

The large color on the left is your all-over base, and I apply that first. Next, I go to the top right corner and apply this grayish color from crease to browbone. Third, I take the darkest color and place it quite heavily (but narrowly) in the crease and a little in the corner and lash line. Next, I put the highlight (lightest) color just under the brow and also outside the inner corner of the eye. Finally, I put the shimmery gold-like color in the middle across the lid and blend all the colors with a blending brush. I use the darker blush normally, but use the light one as a highlight if I want the added effect. I love that when I am doing my makeup on the run, I only have to grab this one container and my makeup brushes (I have the EcoTools Eye Enhancing Duo Brush set with four tips on two brushes, so even there you don't have to take as much with you).

The quality of the product is excellent and it blends well. Other than the darkest brown, the eyeshadow pigments are not super intense, so you can go light or apply more for a deeper intensity.

** This is copy of my review from same product but bought different times and vendors***

This a great price for 20 polishes. Buying them in the store would be like $6 or $7. I have to admit this is my favorite guilty pleasure. It is like gambling lol. For around $1 a polish this is such a fun way to try new colors!

I absolutely love this polish. I have used it for years. The nice thing about these polishes is that even after years they still perform as well as the new ones. I love how easy it is to apply. If I am in a hurry, one coat is fine. I like to take my time with my nails so I have steps (below). I like to change my polish every week so chipping isn’t a problem for me. Also I wear gloves when I do dishes or clean to extend the life of my nails.
I love that this polish dries fairly quickly if you don’t put it on too thick. I mean, put on a coat while watching TV or on the PC. Careful not to touch anything! But let it dry thoroughly.
Then if you need a little more tint slap a little thin layer to make it pop. Also here are couple tips I learned through my years of doing my nails:

1. Use the SH Complete Care 7in1 or 170 Clear'd for takeoff as a base coat. (I am pretty sure that is why it’s called that... It makes sense to me) I know they say you don’t need one with this polish, but really it is for easier removal. It makes your life so much easier! Especially with darker colors that seem to get in the creases and under your nail that are a pain to remove.

2. Use a white polish (121 let’s snow for example) under any color to make that color really pop. You don’t need a really thick coat of white either. Just enough to give a canvas for the bright color to pop.

3. This polish is a little thick so mind that when you apply it. Put one streak down the middle of your nail (your first application to each nail) this will be a little thicker then go to each side and touching the outskirts of the middle line to grab some of the excess there to spread to the sides.

4. I use Sally Hansen Salon Manicure Top Coat as well to seal the color in if I am not using a Salon Manicure Glitter Overcoat. I think they both help preserve the color.

4b. I know glitter can be intimidating because it’s such a pain to get off. Don’t let that deter you. If you like the look of glitter go for it! There are polish removers designed for that now. As well as the polish remover in the jar that you put your finger in to remove color. There is one that has little ridges (or brushes) inside the center wall that help strip the glitter. Can’t tell you where or who. But I can say you probably have one in your town.

5. For those of you that like a little shiny nail but not necessarily color. I use the 170 Clear’d for takeoff and add some drops of any sheer color (Arm Candy, Sheer Ecstasy, Sweet Talker, Shell We Dance, Pink Slip) it just looks like a natural nail with clear polish only it hides blemishes! And your nails look super awesome! I get compliments all the time about how healthy my nails look when I do that.

I hope these tips help. These are things I have learned over the years. I love doing nails and I am glad to share the things I have discovered to save someone else some frustration or time.

Since I was born with a tremor, the shaking of my hands would cause me to burn myself often whenever I straightened my hair. Thanks to this straightening brush and it's super cool bristle tips, I haven't burned myself once when using it. On days that my hands are extra shaky, I use the gloves that were provided with this brush, so can be extra careful not to burn myself. The design of this brush is beautiful. It takes only seconds for it to reach the temperature you set it on. Another pro about this brush is the negatively charged ions. When using a hair tool that emits negatively charged ions, they cause bunches of H2O molecules to break down into small ones, which helps the device to work better and faster. This is SO much better on your hair. It also seals the hair's cuticle which calms frizz and flyaways. The brush comes with a pair of heat resistant gloves, 2 hair clips, a cleaning brush, all in a nice box. I keep the brush and all of the parts stored, conveniently, in the box. I have no regrets about getting this brush. I included  pictures without me wearing any makeup nor did I put ANY hair products on my hair. I ONLY used the brush. I highly recommend it. review_title: I like this heated eye mask
review_text:
I like this heated eye mask, for the most part, I especially like that it exists in the first place! I was searching Amazon up and down for a heated eye mask that can be worn like a sleeping eye mask to relax my eye muscles after sitting at a computer all day when I finally came across this one. I don't care for the color or the kitty design, but the purple material is velvety soft which I do like.

The mask easily covers my head, though I do have a small head, and the strap fits around the back of my head pretty well. I do choose to wear my hair up at night when I use this heating mask otherwise the strap slides up my straight fine hair slowly if I move my head from side to side. And I somehow never wake up with it on, though I'm thinking that has much more to do with me removing it during the middle of the night vs a product error.

The power cord is composed of two pieces, the first has one end with a USB and the other as a round female piece. Connected to the mask on the right side is the other piece of the cord. This piece has a male round piece and connects perfectly to the female piece. I imagine this design is intended to allow the cord connected to the mask to easily be pulled out if the person moves during sleep.

I plug the cord right into my USB-hub with my phone charger and it works perfectly well.

The controls on this are odd, and you are provided zero instructions. There are two buttons I believe one is a (-) that is indented and the other is a (+) that is raised if my memory serves me right. You have to keep one side pressed down until the unit turns on, then I press the indented button because the numbers go up to 60 on this side. The numbers displaced are bizarre and I have no idea what unit of measurement they are - though degrees Celcius makes the most sense.

The one thing I wish this product had was sewn in contours for the nose and eye sockets so it was able to lay more flush with your eyes. This would allow your eyes to feel a more direct heat. Usually, to counterbalance this I place one of my arms over the heating mask to apply weight and increase the intensity of the heat.

review_title: Well made, leak-free bottles for a healthier, greener lifestyle
review_text:
Since becoming a mom, I've been trying to live a greener, less toxic lifestyle. I've started cloth diapering & using un-paper towels. I've switched to natural body & laundry products. However, for some reason, I had been holding out on switching to chemical free cleaning and fabric/air fresheners. I'm not exactly sure why I was so hesitant. These bottles made making the switch fun and easy!

These bottles have both a mist and a stream spray option, as well as an option to turn off the spraying mechanism. Currently, I have one bottle filled with a 1:1 ratio of water to vinegar for use as glass cleaner. The mist option works well on my mirrors and shower doors. The mist option also works very well for both my homemade room/linen spray and my pest repellent spray. (Peppermint essential oil diluted with water and sprayed on the baseboards/around door and windows.) I use the direct stream option for my tub and tile cleaner. It works very well for spraying directly onto the grout.

At 16oz, the bottles are substantial but are not heavy in hand. The trigger is easy to squeeze, yet not flimsy. The glass itself is a gorgeous, deep cobalt blue. I keep my homemade air freshener in one of these bottles on the bathroom counter and have been asked multiple times about where I got it. They really are just so very pretty. Too pretty to be hidden under the sink like most other air freshener or cleaning supply bottles.

Often times, when you purchase cleaners from the store in inexpensive plastic bottles with these same mechanisms, the spray head tends to leak after a week or two of use. It never fails. These, however, are sturdy and seem to be much more heavy duty. I've used these bottles nearly daily and have not had any leaks whatsoever. As beautiful as these bottles are, this is what impressed me most. I'm extremely happy with this product and would highly recommend them!

I’ve been single-blade shaving for about 5 years. I enjoy trying out different blades and soaps. This is one of my stand-byes so I can recommend this soap.

1. SHAVE: EXCELLENT. Mitchell’s is very slick and leaves very little tendency to cut or scrape. It results in a close, smooth shave in two passes. Most premium soaps result in a good-to-excellent shave.

2. SKIN: EXCELLENT. This product contains lanolin and results in the very best and softest after-shave experience of any soap I’ve tried. Most premium soaps result in a fair-to-good experience for me.

3. VERSATILITY: GOOD. Some soaps seem to shave very well with one brand of blade and not others. Mitchell’s doesn’t seem to mind. I use ASTRA and generally sharp blades.

4. LATHER: FAIR. This soap deposits easily onto a wet badger brush, sufficient to lather onto the skin and shave well. It does not whip into a full thick lather if that is important to you. It is also reputed (I have no direct experience) to be difficult to lather at all if you have hard water.

5. LATHER DURABILITY: GOOD. The lather on the brush lasts OK during the shave. Easily enough for two passes.

6. PUCK DURABILITY: EXCELLENT. I tend to rotate among several brands of soap, and most milled soaps collect enough water from the brush to decay and dry out somewhat before the puck is finished. Mitchell’s lasts to the end.

8. VALUE: FAIR. Mitchell’s is priced about the same as other premium milled soaps. However, if it is sold as a bare replacement puck so you will need a shaving bowel or other container.

review_title: We'll see how long this lasts...
review_text:
Provides a decent shave, particularly after the beard has been moistened as it is immediately after a shower. The question is, for how long, considering the flimsy construction of some components and the already below-specified battery life.

Things they don't describe in the mostly worthless manual:

The charging indicator is a steady red AC plug symbol.

The LCD indication at full charge is 99. A RED (not a far more intuitive GREEN) battery full symbol is shown at when the charge reaches 99.

A low battery is indicated by a flashing red AC plug symbol when the charge number on the LCD reaches 10.

Charge time was tested and found to be 82 minutes. The manual claims 60 to 90 minutes, so they got that right.

Use time is specified in the manual as 50 to 60 minutes. The run time was tested and found to be only 30 minutes in 5 minute on, five minute off intervals, just free running and not being used to shave which should further reduce the run time slightly.

The charge indicator was at 52 after 25 minutes and then rapidly dropped from that to 10 only five minutes later causing the low battery indicator to flash, so I would definitely NOT trust the charge indicator to be an accurate indication of how much shaving time you have left. They are apparently not calculating percent charge remaining and displaying it on the LCD, they are simply and far less usefully displaying percent battery VOLTAGE which drops off rapidly at what is called the battery's discharge "knee." A cheap route to take revealing that the LCD display is nothing more useful than a gimmick.

The manual states that the razor should be unplugged from the charger (this razor package does not come with an AC to USB charge adapter) when the charge number reaches 99, so I suspect this charger might not have an intelligent charger which stops the battery charge process at full charge to avoid battery damage over the long term. So, I will not put this razor on charge and just forget about it until my next shave like I can with my Norelco with its intelligent charge system.

Other information:

The space under the heads which catches the beard shavings is very small. Cleaning often will be a must. We'll see how the hinge and head locking mechanism hold up.

When opening the shaving head to clean, put a finger on it to slow its opening, otherwise it will rapidly flip open and if a razor element isn't locked into its place by its flimsy and not very intuitive to correctly replace locking ring, as it wasn't in my case, the razor element and its parts will be vigorously projected into an alternate universe. Luckily, I found all of the parts. Had I been standing over a sink, some could easily have gone down the drain. We'll see how the razor element locking rings hold up.

review_title: Don’t love it but don’t hate it
review_text:
This foundation is a tricky one. There are things I really like about it and things that I don’t.
I bought it in the shade 04 Honey. In the bottle it looks like an almost exact match to my skin, but when I put it on it’s much paler with a decidedly pink undertone, yet it doesn’t look orange or too pink in my skin. I prefer a neutral undertone though since my skin can be both yellow and pink.

I love the bottle and packaging. It comes in a frosted glass bottle with a pink pump and pink cap that snaps on tightly.

The coverage is much higher than I expected and it is heavier than expected for a luminous foundation.

It covers blue tones better than redness. I have typically had to build it up in areas I have more redness (and we’re talking average redness, not anything extreme) and doing this makes it look much heavier so I end up using a concealer instead. The problem with this lies in the finish.

So this foundation’s finish is very confusing and hard to describe. It is very glowy and luminous without being shimmery but it has the heaviness of a matte. I know, confusing.
Areas can look too greasy or too dry. It settles into fine lines and creases around the eyes and nostrils. For this reason this is not a foundation I choose for the daytime. It’s much too heavy and shiny for the day, which is a shame because I enjoy it’s longevity. Once I set it with some powder around the eyes and my nostrils I really enjoy it for a night out.

I should also mention it is heavily perfumed with a floral scent so those sensitive to scented foundations will likely want to give this a pass. It’s not bothersome to me personally but fragrance can irritate really sensitive skin.

All in all I don’t use it as much as I hoped I would and probably won’t repurchase based on that and how heavy it is. At 36 I want a foundation with decent coverage but a lighter feel. It’s also not the easiest foundation to completely remove and when I wear it I have to use a cleaning oil and a cleanser both AND a miceller solution.

I have combo skin that can be prone to breakouts with certain brands but I haven’t broken out from this foundation.

I enjoy Holika Holika’s BB cream which is why I gave this a shot (and I like a luminous foundation) but I’ll probably stick with the BB cream in the future since it’s lighter.

First, I want to say I bought this at full price....period!

I've been very lax over years, at any kind of skin care routine. My skin isn't really showing any effects of bad skin care, because I was blessed with really good skin, but....I'm 52 now and decided I really shouldn't push it any longer. So; I purchased Tree of Life Beauty Vitamin C wash first. I was very impressed with the ingredient list, the amount used to wash my face (neck, chest, and shoulders as well), and the way my skin felt afterwards.

So when I saw the toner was 93% organic, I decided buy the Tree of life Beauty Toner, to go along with the wash. First of all, I really am impressed with the ingredients this company uses. I grow all organics herbs, berries, vegetables, etc. and use as many organic ingredients that I can. I would love to be a purist, but my budget says "NO!" This company doesn't use a lot of needless filler ingredients to stretch the product. So when you think of the product being only 8 oz, you can be assured that 8 oz (when used properly), is a good amount of product that will last. I can't say how long yet, as I've only been using it a week.

Secondly, being an herbalist has taught me that your skin is your largest organ! You should be careful what you put on it. Your pores soak up every last drop of whatever you put on your skin. Parabens are absolute poison and should be avoided like the plague! (Sorry all of you Vicks and vasaline lovers out there) From what I've read about Tree of life Beauty, we're on the same page and I don't feel I need to be concerned about them hiding any in their products.

And finally, Vitamin C is essential to your body in too many ways to go into. But I take a vitamin C daily to help with the absorption of Collagen 1&3 (Which is important for hair, skin, nails, bones, joints, etc). I had not realized the benefits of vitamin C for your face. I absolutely love the way my skin feels after using the cleanser and toner. I let it dry well, then follow up with moisturizer both morning and evening.

So far, I'm quite happy with Tree of Life Beauty products and will probably transition to more of their products as I use up what I already have. We'll see how it goes after using these items for 30 days.

First off, the jar is pretty sturdy, I’m not going to dispute that and it’s amber, which is always good in helping keep out UV rays. The ONLY seal is the Amazon barcode label (One of the photos shows the label, but I cut through it, it was intact when it arrived - so that was not the issue). There was no shrink wrap seal, neither was there an inner seal, nor one of those inner lid liners. This jar also does not have ANY other labeling except for that Amazon barcode and the top label with their website URL. This was a standalone jar, no box. There is no product information on the jar, no ingredient list, no product name, no manufacture or expiration dates. This brings up heavy red flags for me – quality control especially.

The product description sounds rather amazing, right? Ok, keep in mind what I previously mentioned about quality control. In their description they advertise that you can EAT it. I’d recommend against it because of the lack of quality sealing. It would be one thing if this were given to me by someone who I knew personally that had made the product, but since this is coming from a company that I don’t know and that doesn’t have anything other than the description on Amazon, I’m not sticking this product in my mouth. I know the anti-bacterial properties of honey, however, that doesn’t mean that it can’t be contaminated by anything else -1) it’s not pure honey, there are other ingredients within, 2) who knows the health/sanitation practices of this company, right?, 3) with there just being the barcode label as a seal, who’s to say that someone couldn’t have tampered with it in the warehouse?, and 4) their only label – the one I mentioned with their website URL – if you go to the URL, it comes up with:

“This webpage is not available

ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED”

I don’t know about you, but without anything reputable to back up the product or company, I find it very hard for me to trust this.

ALL of that aside, if you can look past those packaging and trust issues, getting to the actual product…

When you open the cover, it does have that very rich strong scent of honey. The brown sugar and other ingredients have settled to the bottom, so some stirring was necessary — the honey is also pretty solid, so a cosmetic spatula (not included) was not adequate enough to stir it. Once you do stir it, the scent of the brown sugar comes through. Because it’s honey, it’s really sticky, and like any sugar scrub, it has that gritty sugar texture which is great for exfoliation. If your skin is dry when you apply, you may have a tough time spreading it, to avoid this, moisten your skin prior to smoothing this along.

It does its job at exfoliating, removing a layer of dead skin, but I didn’t expect that it wouldn’t. The product itself is good, leaves the skin smooth and smells good – I used it on my leg.

It’s not proprietary though, since there are a ton of DIY tutorials on how to make sugar scrubs out on the web nowadays. But if you’re not into making your own and if they change the packaging and labeling and get a working website up, then this would be the way to go.

I really hope that they get the concerns I mentioned in the beginning straightened out. It would have been a decent product all around if not for those issues. If they do, then I'd be more than happy to bump the rating to a 4. This product was given to me complimentary in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

review_text: Have trouble holding this great floss? Try this: cut a piece about 14 inches long. Double it over then tie a simple overhand knot four to five inches down to form a loop slightly wider than your hand. Gently try to floss a tooth. Adjust the knot to an ideal size for you. The magic is that the knot is easily moved by separately pulling the ends. Once it's optimal tie a second knot and tease it until it sits on the first knot. They will now be locked into position. At first I had trouble getting anything at all out of the tube. There was a problem with my cap that prevented anything from coming out. But after taking the cap off the product flowed out. By reading other reviews I learned that the tube must be submerged in hot water for some time to liquify the mixture of oil. Otherwise you get a pebbly mixture. And unless you live in a subtropical climate, one of the oils in the mixture comes out in a semi-solid state and must be rolled between your palms to liquify it as well. Once that is done, your hands will be pretty thoroughly coated on both sides and between the fingers. Then you must work it into your beard. It did a pretty good job of softening my scruffy beard. But now its time to clean the oils off my hands using the sink full of hot water I soaked the tube in. An oily film can be seen in the water, but my hands still feel oily. No worries. The remaining oil get absorbed into my hands.

review_title: Sharp Shears for Healthy Looking Hair
review_text:
I learned some things when I was looking for hair cutting shears. Mostly that you can pay around $200 for the best ones,used by professionals,and,that you need very sharp scissors or shears to cut or trim hair.

I've been trimming and shaping my own hair for a long time and am usually happy with the results,considering too many times,when I would go to a salon to have it cut or shaped or trimmed,they did a job I was almost always disappointed with. I decided a long time ago,if someone was going to screw up my hair,it might as well be me. At least I have a good idea on when to stop cutting it and I actually care what the final result looks like.

I also have fine,wavy hair. Not the easiest to cut.

I have noticed,and maybe it was from using whatever scissors were around at the time,that sometimes the ends do look a bit frazzled;and in researching shears,I found out that unless the blades are very sharp,the ends can break,or result in split ends. I don't have split ends and never noticed them,except for a long,long time ago when I was a teenager;but,I have used these once to do some light trimming and shaping;with wavy hair you are always shaping,cutting with the wave and not cutting against the wave. And,these shears have produced a nice result. And I don't see the somewhat frazzled or lightningbolt effect at the ends of my hair,that I sometimes get.

I've used these just once,I only trim my hair to maintain healthy looking ends,and I did it a few weeks ago,and I like these and I'm glad I looked for something better than "any old scissors" that I have on hand.

review_title: Comprehensive review of robusta coffee scrub
review_text:
I recently used this scrub and felt inspired to write a review about it for those that aren't sure if they should get this scrub or not.

Before buying this scrub, I was aware coffee scrubs have been trending for a year or so. As others, I was very skeptical about it and wasn't sure how I felt about this beauty trend. The only way I was going to find out was to give it a try.

Here's what I learned after using it that I think will help others should you decide to try it:

1) Prepare your environment and set aside time before using it - Prior to using the scrub, decide where you are going to use it (shower, bath, fenced backyard, etc.) because I'm warning you now, it's gonna get messy. I have a regular sized shower/bath, so if I plan on using this again, I would get myself completely wet, sit in the tub, use the scrub all over my body, rinse off (still sitting), then finally stand up to complete washing off. If you have a private fenced off backyard where you are near a hose, that's a good setting too. The whole process took approximately 40-50 minutes (I like to take my time). I used the whole pack because I literally used it all over my body, but you can use whatever amount you want. Just know that you will need time to really work it into your skin and let it set for a few minutes before washing it off.

2) Be honest with yourself about your skin regimen - What I mean is, if you are not disciplined about your skin regimen or don't want to take time to use this scrub, then honestly I don't know this product is going to work for you. Personally, I'm committed to a regular and consistent skin regimen and set aside time to use this product to get optimal results. I am just saying this isn't like a typical scrub and takes more time to work it in to your skin.

3) You'll likely need soap to get the rest of it off - Even after a rinse, it will stain, just like coffee will do, so I used some shea butter body wash and a body brush to get the rest of it off. Once I was completely clean, I dried off and used body shop cocoa butter all over my body (it's what I usually use anyway).

4) For people with very oily skin be aware - Since this product has coconut oil and you are highly prone to breaking out, I'm not sure if this is a good idea; the amount of coconut oil is definitely noticeable so just be aware.

The verdict: I will say, this made me feel amazing afterwards. My skin felt very smooth and soft. That being said, I bought it without having any expectations. I tried it mainly out of curiosity. As there are advances in beauty products, I am naturally going to want to try new things. I have heard that coffee scrubs reduce cellulite or supports regeneration of new skin cells. Honestly I don't know if that's true and frankly find that doubtful. However, I can say it is better than most scrubs I've used in the past, and it's a wonderful treat for the skin from time to time. I would buy and use it again for occasional use.

I understand the metal was likely placed there to protect the blade and prevent unnecessary dulling and the build up of gunk. Most razors on the market today have a strip of lotion or emollient along the top of the blade. Unfortunately, the metal from the pod kept fusing to the strip causing both the strip to come off and the plastic of the pod to pull free - resulting in both a broken pod and a damaged and unusable razor. review_title: A Thick and Rich Eye Cream.
review_text:
EDITED REVIEW as of 9/25/21.

I came back to edit this review and to lower my rating from 4 stars to 3 stars. Here's why:

After a few weeks of using this cream, I started to develop some sensitivity to it. When I say sensitivity, here's what I mean: 1) The scent bothered me more than it did when I first used the cream. In fact, I started to sneeze most evening after applying it. 2) I'd used the cream on other areas of my face, and noticed minor breakouts in those areas.

Basically, I think the cream was just too oily for my skin. Even around the eye area, which has virtually no oil glands, the non-absorbency of the cream left me feeling sticky and greasy even though I gave the cream plenty of time to absorb.

End of Edit.

***************************************************************************************************************************

Everything else I said in my original review still stands. But the above edit may help you decide if this is the right eye cream for you.

If you're looking for a natural, plant-based eye cream that is ultra-thick and rich, you'll find it in this 2 oz. jar.

The jar will last a VERY long time, because you only need a tiny amount of this cream to cover the undereye area and the corners where crows feet form.

I'd advise putting the cream on a couple of hours before bed, since it takes quite a while to absorb into the skin. (If you don't wait, you'll end up depositing most of the cream on your pillowcase.)

I've also used a small amount of this cream on other areas of my face (nose to mouth lines) and the results were the same as around my eye area.

So what were the results? The skin around my eye area looked smoother and brighter after one night of use.
The results on other parts of my face were less noticeable, but I believe continued use of the cream will improve the results in both the eye area and on the face.

I'm rating the cream 4 stars instead of 5, because of one major issue I have with it, which is: THE SCENT.
The cream has a rather strong minty (?), menthol (?) medicinal smell that takes some time to fade away.
Since I prefer NO SCENT in eye/facial products, I deducted one star from my rating.

That aside, if scented products don't bother you, and you want a thick, rich eye cream you will probably enjoy using this one.

I've tried many brands of purple shampoos/conditioners in the never-ending battle against brassy tones.
This is one of the better brands.

First of all, I love the scent. It is vaguely floral, definitely a feminine scent. It smells wonderful in the shower, but I like the fact that it fades quickly once you rinse it away. It doesn't linger all day, meaning it won't compete with any other fragrance you are wearing.

Second, I like the fact that this set is gentle, and non-drying. (Some other brands have left me with straw-like hair after a few uses.) This combo cleans gently, and leaves the hair feeling silky.

Third, the toning is effective. There is a visible difference after just a couple of uses. I saw the yellow/orange tones had faded after the first use, and after the second, my hair was shiny and showed highlights, but there was a marked difference in the amount of brassiness.

Fourth, I like the fact that the shampoo is natural (made with botanicals) and is sulfate and paraben free. It is also cruelty free, another big plus. The pump bottles are also great, making the shampoo and conditioner easy to use in the shower. They are plastic, so no breakage issues.

Finally, the price is right. The shampoo and conditioner bottles each contain 16.9 fl. oz of product. A good buy.

Bottom line, this is a solid 5 star set. Recommended!

All four fragrances are pleasant, clean, and crisp. My partner likes Oxford Bleu and Riviera the most. He says these have a "fresh" smell to him. (I agree!. The Oxford Bleu is my favorite.)

If you're not familiar with English Laundry scents, this set is a great way to try several of their offerings. If you already love English Laundry, here's a chance to enjoy some of your favorites.

When you need a little extra cleaning down there, this is gentle and effective. It's also easier to dispose of and potentially less wasteful then feminine or other wipes because you put a dab on toilet paper to use, and then flush the toilet paper as usual.

I just got my first Norelco model 8825 XL, after 7 years using a Braun 4501. I considered these two brands the top in the electrical shaving industry. In some aspects I founded the Norelco reigning over the Braun and in other aspects the Braun is much better. So, the question you should ask yourself is what type of hair are you trying to shave?
Let first look at the Norelco series:
The different between the Norelco's Spectra (8000 series), Quadra (7000 series), Advantage (6000 series), and the Reflex (5000 series) is one major feature added to each series. The Reflex sports the basic "Lift & Cut" system. The Advantage is the same but include a lotion dispenser. The Quadra's "Lift and Cut" system has two types of head with a slot and hole. The Spectra series has what the Quadra does, but include a comfort control. Both the Quadra and Spectra don't have lotion dispenser. There are also more special features that can be found in each series by looking at the 2nd digit. For example the Spectra 8894 have a digital screen where the bare-bone lower number Spectra 8825 have just a green light.
The performances, Norelco vs. Braun:
I have soft hair in the beard area and thicker hair around the lips (mustache and chin area). The Norelco does a superior job in the beard area; it cut it clean with a couple of strokes. When using the Braun (older model 4501), I sometime have to use a long trimmer and then go back over with the coil. The Norelco three individual heads move over the sides of the face a lot better. Braun does do a superior job over the mustache area. It coils has more and bigger holes then Norelco. The Spectra with it dual slot and hole head is good but takes longer time to cut down the thicker stub. The old Braun battery (NH-) is dying on me. Norelco battery (NiCd) is replaceable and you use it charged or just plug and play, which the Braun could not do. Overall, I prefer the Norelco's design.
The features I like:
I am still playing with the Personal Comfort Control and am not sure if it is necessary. The more sensitive the level is the long it takes to cut so far. The long hair trimmer is great, but that is almost standard in most models, but not the Advantage's Series. Plug and play is great, since I don't travel every day. Cleaning is simple; just rinse it in the sink. I like the solid construction the Norelco's design is, the rotating machine is fun to use and is very smooth.

review_title: The All Natural way to remove nail polish!
review_text:
I'm puzzled by this product. I loved the idea of having a natural, non-toxic nail polish remover. I paint my own nails quite often, skipping the nail salon to save money and time. I've been giving myself manicures and pedicures since 6th grade, so I'm pretty good at it (if I do say so myself) and am well-versed in many of the products out there. I typically use a 100% acetone remover, which is AWESOME, but I hate that there are so many harmful chemicals, not only on my nails, but also in the fumes I'm breathing in every time I use it. So, when I saw this product, I was excited and motivated to try it and like it.

When it arrived, I was also pleased with the size. I had assumed it would be pretty small because of the way the dropper looks next to it in the picture, but it's actually a good sized bottle. Before using any product, I read the directions and particularly with a new type of product like this non-toxic, all-natural nail polish remover. That's when I saw that you have to leave the product on the nail for 2-5 minutes. I don't understand this because once you use the dropper to apply the product to the nail polish that's on the nail, it immediately starts dripping down the sides of the nails onto your hands and makes a bit of a mess. It's also pretty inconvenient to sit there for 5 minutes when I could use my regular nail polish remover and would have clean nails in 30 seconds to a minute. I decided instead to try pouring the product into a shallow bowl and soaking my nails in it instead. This did make it much easier and created less of a mess, but it also requires you to use a lot more of the product than you would just using the dropper.

I waited 2 minutes and took a cotton ball to swipe the nail to see if the polish would come off. It started to, but just the top layer. I re-soaked them in the product for 3 more minutes, and I was able to remove the polish from my nails. I should also mention that I use Orly bonding base coat, which helps the polish adhere to the nail. I also had 3 coats of polish, and a top coat, so that might be why the polish was so stubborn to come off. Plus, it was a deep red, which is difficult to remove no matter what you are using, and it usually dyes my nail beds a bit when I'm removing the polish anyway. As a positive, I did notice that this product was MUCH less harmful on my nails. My acetone remover immediately dries out my nails and strips all the healthy oils from the nails and nail beds. This did not do that. My nails had a nice, healthy shine to them and the nail beds retained their moisture, which is nice.

So, in summary, I love that this product is natural and non-toxic, but it's just not practical for me to spend 5 minutes soaking my nails to wait for the polish to come off. However, if you are super green and more willing to commit to being patient in order to be able to use something that has no chemicals and is good for your body and those around you (which I commend you for!), then this is a great substitute for chemical nail polish removers.

review_title: Ever wanted to know what you will look like with grey hair?
review_text:
The colour of this wig is very attractive. It's a beautiful silver but there's black subtly peppered in here too. It's not that obvious at all until you get up close.
The hair is on the shiny side, but IMO that goes with the grey.
The tresses are loosely curled and the side area of the hair is cut much shorter--below my ears so this could do with some styling.
The biggest issue is the hairline. I can see the cap and the very center part of the hairline cap does not want to sit flat. So it needs work.
Very attractive overall--I'm going to have to work on the hairline....

Of the three wigs here, the purple is the best. I would give that wig 5 stars. The colour is fantastic; it's not the same purple all over; it's got different shades and the hairline is fantastic.
The black wig is bad. I'd give that 2 stars. It's super shiny but the worst thing is that there is NO way I can hide my hairline unless I pull the wig farther down on my forehead. It's also not cut that well, but that's possible to fix. The hairline issue is not fixable.
The grey wig---I love that one too. My second favourite. It's got those great dark roots. It is very long so tangling may be an issue depending on use. But it looks great, fits well etc. So.. 2 out of 3 ain't bad.
Overall a great deal as long as I accept that one wig is fairly useless for me.

The best thing about this wig is the colours: fantastic fantasy cosplay colours: it's just beautiful. The 'hair' is soft and not too shiny. Too shiny would really spoil this IMO.
The hair is REALLY full, so it's going to either look The Shining scary, or else, you are going to need a crown or something to keep the hair off your face. You can also style it off your face too.
The hair is cut in a long shag style, with some bits in the back much shorter. This gives it the full look. The hairline section is the wig's weak point and it looks fake--well it looks fake anyway with the colours, but it's hard to make the wig look GOOD. Again back to styling, crown, or some type of headband to smooth over the hairline section.

My head measures about 22 1/2 around. On me the wig seemed to be on the small side. The hair is obviously fake as it is meant to be so so problem there, and it's a nice quality nylon or nylon type material. I love the colours.
It comes with a hair net, 2 wig caps, a pearl-type clip and a pair of druzy post earrings. The latter were a surprise and a pleasant one.
I had a hard time getting the wig to cover the very front section of my hair. I think anyone who has masses of hair, or really long hair may find this wig doesn't cover easily.
The hair hangs awkwardly. It falls forward into the face. I trimmed it a bit.
IMO this is a great wig for costuming and/or teens, but those with masses of long hair may find it problematic.

I just recently started using purple shampoo. I have grey hair, btw. I liked the results I had with another brand so was eager to try this brand. First, at least at the time of this review, the price is decent.
The purple shampoo is a deep violet. I applied it to my wet hair and worked it in. Loved the purple lather. Then applied the conditioner which is more of a deep inky blue. The instructions said to leave it in for a few minutes. When I wash it out, my hair feels differently--it feels as though there's still something there on my hair, but deeply mixed in. It feels differently than when I use regular shampoo.
Anyway, I love what this does for my hair. It seems to brighten the light silver and darken the darker grey. At least that's what it seems like. No frizzies either and that's important for me.

I wasn't sure what to expect from this product, but it is really fun. Who thought that pink eyelashes would look great?
I am not a make up expert and I don't think I am that good at it either, so I have no problem admitting that MY end result did not look like the pictures. And I will also admit that this may be my fault.
The pictures show eyelashes that look solidly pink (or whatever colour you buy); mine did not come out like that. The brush tends to carry a lot of mascara so I got some clumping.
My eyelashes, which are black, ended up pinkish over the black near the base but with pink tips and I actually think it looks better than the professional pics. The only way I could get solid pink eyelashes ended up with too much clumping. So it was possible to get solid pink eyelashes and I did, but then I had to gently wipe off all the excess mascara and that left me with pink tips.
Honestly, I liked it that way, I think it looks more subtle and not so obvious. The pink mascara goes great with mauve or nude eyeshadow IMO.
This needed a couple of minutes to dry but after that it didn't smudge. And it really does lengthen and thicken lashes. I'm happy with the look and like it more than the professional photos on site.

If you look at the ingredients listed, there are a lot of oils: coconut oil, Jojoba oil, Clary Sage essential oil, organic Ylang Ylang essential oil, neroli essential oil, geranium essenatil oil, sunflower seed oil, lavender oil, rose absolute, Jasmine absolute and a vitamin E oil blend. The box is the best thing here. I had high hopes for the mascara. It's string, so it doesn't go on easily. It clumps. And I also found it very difficult to remove, Of course it is waterproof and that feature works. It took many swipes with oil to start to break this up and off the lashes.

This great set is a larger square and two small circles. The material is so soft, you want to rub your face all over it. Each piece comes with a handle for easy storage/drying. Instructions say these can be machine washed and dried but I hand washed mine and they came out just as lovely as before.
The seams are very well sewn with some type of lightly corded material.
Very nice indeed. The colour is purple but it's a heliotrope purple. Quite beautiful.

I liked this clay mask a lot. The mask cream is very thick indeed, and it takes a squeeze to get it out of the tube. It goes a long way, but at the same time, this is a small tube (3 oz). It dries quickly. And it's the type of mask that makes your face feel TIGHT. The type where you can't smile.
After about 20 mins, I washed this off. It was easy to remove. After using a few times, I think it does indeed have a brightening effect on the skin. It doesn't moisturize. At least it didn't for me, and I had to lather on cream afterwards as my skin felt a bit dry after the mask.
Overall I liked this. I like how it worked but it is on the pricey side.

review_title: Nifty idea but I'd worry about it holding mask in place
review_text:
What's that saying about necessity being the mother of invention? Well here we are in a pandemic wearing face masks. Someone came up with the idea of a head band with buttons to hold the mask mask in place.

This is a thin material. Think very thin t shirt type material. The headband measures about 18 inches and just over 3 inches wide. I like the material for a headband. However, its use as a mask holder is iffy. Many people complain that the elastic that holds the masks in place makes their ears pop out. That is definitely true of some masks. They can also be wearying on the ears, having that elastic against your ears all day, so this headband is a great concept.
I put the headband on and as I stretched it over my head, I heard a pop, so some stitching gave somewhere.

I attached two types of masks, one at a time. First, it was a bit fiddly to get the elastic over the button. Once it just sprang off.

One mask using the buttons fit well. Another did not. The latter mask opened up on the sides.

I would hesitate to wear this out thinking that everything would stay put for hours. I like the headband as a headband. It's nice material. A sort of light grey merle, but if you are looking at this for long-term safety, I would say no.

It feels more like soft plastic than leather, and it does not smell bad. Overall I am pleased with the design and features of this bag and plan to keep it. review_title: I have fine hair but a lot of it
review_text:
I’ve had numerous extensions in my life. I bought these as a cheaper alternative to the Bellami volumizing weft, which is expensive (definitely an investment). I have fine hair but a lot of it. The problem I have with many extension companies is blending the extensions with my own hair, since most of them are so thin my hair peaks through. I also have shoulder length hair, which adds another level of difficulty when trying to blend extensions.

Pros
• The hair is soft
• The hair doesn’t tangle easily
• The color is nice
• The clips are amazing. Once I clip them in they stay.
• They are convenient. One weft and you’re done (usually)
• They are cheap, and a good quality for the price
• Good starting off extensions

Cons
• The hair is thin; it is heavier on top and thins out to a v-point. As expected my hair peaked though. I ended up tying up my bottom layer and putting the extensions on top. It solved the problem of the hair poking though.
• For these extensions to work for me I would need to buy at least two more packs of hair. Having 3, five clip wefts wouldn’t fit around my head comfortably.
• These will not give you volume; they are too thin to give you any thickness
• If you have a lot of hair these will not look very natural

This hair is best suited for someone with thin, medium length hair who is looking for some length. Also, if you have layers in your hair it could help blend the hair. I got my own hair thinned out a little at the hair salon and it made a huge difference.

This hair will not work well with short hair or thick hair unless you are willing to work hard to blend it.

I will be buying one more weft in order to see how that works out for me. I will update this post once I receive my new weft.

My experience wearing 2- five clip wefts

I am very impressed with this razor. I have used electric razors most of my 35+ years of shaving. I was skeptical using it for the first time, I thought it wasn't working because it is so soft to the face and so quiet. It didn't sound "agressive" like my other razors did. WRONG!!! The shave was close, my skin was not irritated at all, and it cut smooth basically in the first pass. This unit is first class.

Other nice features are it can be cleaned under the faucet, it charges quickly and maintains that charge for a long time, and it provides what I consider one of the best shaves I've had in a long time. May, 2012 - I can't believe I wrote the original review almost seven years ago. I'm still using this razor and it still works just as I expressed back then. The battery still keeps a great charge, and the shave is still excellant. I went on a 10 day vacation last year and the charge held for the whole trip. This is truly a great product.

I've been using this razor since it arrived, approximately 2 weeks ago, and thinking long and hard about the score I'd give it. I actually intended to give it 4/5, the reason being that, while it's an excellent razor, the price point is rather high. In the end, though, I'm so impressed that I really need to give it a full five stars in spite of the price, with the caveat that you may want to take a look at one of the less expensive, stripped-down models; this one is the flagship, but all the models should be similarly excellent (please bear in mind this is the only one I've used).

And excellent it is. While my feelings have already been summed up in the opening paragraph, read on for similarly styled (but moderate) hyperbole.

I've never gotten such a good shave with an electric razor. Norelco does recommend that you give the razor a full 21 days of your time exclusively (i.e. not shaving with anything else) before making a judgment. I haven't had the luxury of giving it a full 21 days, as I need to get my review in; however, I've already adjusted to it so well that I can't imagine going back to my old razors. It will only get better as I get more used to it, although I'm perfectly satisfied at this point and unsure if it could get any better.

Not only do I use it to shave my face (which is obviously what it was designed for, and it does a great job), I use it to shave my head. It's not going to give you as close a shave as a traditional razor, but it's also not going to scrape against your skin like a traditional razor. You'll also save money on shaving cream (the only extra expense is buying a new razor "head" for it yearly, the price of which I am uninformed of). It works "dry". This is nice for me, as it takes a lot of cream to shave both my face and my scalp, and it does, in fact, do a decent job on my head. It's a little stubbly, even right after shaving, but honestly the only thing that would do a better job would be a blade, and that's a difficult way to shave (I was previously using a Headblade). If it can shave a head, where my hair was very thick, I imagine it would be adequate for even the bushiest of beards, and, again, it's designed for faces, not heads.

If you look at the features list, you'll see that this model is full of bells and whistles. Truthfully, they are mostly extras you could live without; the lower-end models would likely be just fine, so I strongly suggest examining them as a money-saving alternative. The meter that shows you how many minutes of the charge are remaining is sort of handy, the icon that lights to remind you to clean it is somewhat useful, but to say they're necessary would be a grave overstatement. In fact, the "wash me" icon lights up after basically every use, so its necessity is particularly dubious. (As a side note, it's marvelously easy to clean.)

In the end, the product does receive my highest recommendation. I think if you tried it out, you'd be pleased, and even if you had to send it back and didn't like it after three weeks via their guarantee (it does take time for your skin to adjust), there would be little time/money wasted. I would, however, encourage you to check out the lower-end models. Ultimately, even the high price point wasn't enough for me to downgrade to four stars. I'm normally quite critical.
