I love this flat iron despite the one problem I have with it. I wish that the flat iron was skinnier. It’s difficult to get close to my head at certain angles due the flat iron size. If my hair was longer, this would not be a problem. I almost returned the product because of the iron size. But I made some changes to the way that I iron my hair & I think it will work despite the iron size.
The features I like about it:
-steam feature - makes my frizzy hair smoother than a normal flat iron does
-high temperature adjustable heat - makes it so I can iron my hair with less passes from the iron, even if my hair is wet when I’m ironing it - my hair is thick and usually requires more passes, even from a high heat iron, and I have never been able to dry my wet hair by ironing it with any other flat iron in the past
-setting buttons are on the inside handle - I was annoyed with this feature at first, but I realized that this makes it safer to leave plugged in when not in use, when you have small children - I have not had the problems I have had in the past with my kids trying to play with the buttons because of their location
-comes with quite a few extra tools including an extra steam compartment and an easy way to fill the steam compartment - the holes for the filling the steam compartment are really small and would be impossible to fill without provided bottle
-comes with chord Velcro strap - this makes it easy to keep organized despite having a long chord in a small bathroom

Despite my problem with the short hair, I decided to keep it because it works so well. I will also say that I don’t believe the steam feature is protective to hair damage. It just makes the flat iron way more affective with less passes.

Luckily I have clip ins to help here when I dont want to clip the shorter hairs out of my face. If you have anything beyond thin, fine hair get 2 - 3 packs.

My only complaint is that they dont offer smaller packs. I wish they offered a half pack, so you arent faced with another $50 for a few more strands.

Aside from that the hair is very soft and I've been able to style it how I want without issue. I haven't washed my hair yet, but I'll update if I experience any issues there.

[[VIDEOID:b7a26be60316cb3ca697412c040cd1b1]] We have 3 cats: different ages (17, 8, 5), hair lengths (short, medium, long), hair types (silky soft fine, coarse, in-between), temperaments (laid back, shy/skittish, impatient/trouble-maker).

My interest in this brush was specifically for our oldest cat. He had spent much of his life outdoors, but we recently shifted him to being an indoor cat due to age, health and inclement weather.

He was a mess and we had to cut out much of the mats and debris.

Since I spend much of my time in the basement he stays there with me and I created a bed for him next to my sewing area and desk. He likes to sleep there and when I need a break, I like to brush him. He has adapted very nicely to being an indoor cat as long as I brush him at least 6-8x's/day. I kid you not.

However, I noticed as we finally got him cleaned up, that certain areas were bothering him when brushed. Careful inspection revealed external skin growths (like moles) and if our old slicker brush happened to hit them, he would let us know it hurt.

I purchased 2 brushes to try on him. One was a silicone brush and this one. While he liked the feel of the silicone brush (as did the other cats), it wasn't effective at actually grooming.

On the other hand, this brush does a remarkably decent job. It's not as efficient as our old style slicker -- and I think that's due to the fact that it has considerably fewer bristles and they are spaced further apart.

It is necessary, though, to wait for the brush to have a considerable amount of hair in it before cleaning by pushing the button. If you try to remove it before it's relatively full, it doesn't do a very good job of removing the hair from the bristles.

When I also tried it on the other cats, my husband's shy/skittish female cat, who has always avoided me like the plague, couldn't get enough of the brush and was actually purring. Of course, as soon as I stood up (I had been on the floor with her), she ran back to him as if to escape from an ogre!

Mr trouble-maker tolerated the brush but was too impatient to stick around for long. Point is, he didn't object to it, he just wasn't in the mood and would rather run around and play. (8-year old Siamese).

My only request was that the next version of this brush have more bristles, closer together. Meanwhile, I will keep my old slicker for cleaning furniture. It does a remarkably good job.

Forgot to mention: my arthritic hands absolutely adore the soft squishy silicone-like handle.

I wanted to give this sunscreen a rating of 5 stars but I don't think that would be honest. The description sounds so appealing, gentle and pure, but there are several things that really bother me. First of all, this is definitely NOT a natural product. There are tons of ingredients in here that don't pass that test at all (read the label!).  Secondly, the two sunscreens that are listed as active ingredients don't protect against UVA rays, only UVB. Titanium dioxide which protects against UVA rays also is in here but not labeled as an active ingredient, and it doesn't give a percentage. Thirdly, if you research ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate you will see that it is not considered to be an entirely safe ingredient. With all that said, I do like the texture. I think the description of this is misleading though, and although I don't hate it, it wouldn't be my first choice for a pure, natural, and entirely safe sunscreen. review_title: Great Anti-Aging Product-Leaves Smooth Skin-Tips for Application and Use Information!
review_text:
I am very pleased so far with the InterSight Naturals Hyaluronic Acid so far. It comes in a 1 oz bottle but a little goes a long way. I will explain in my review.

There are a lot of benefits in general to your body with Hyaluronic Acid, including your skin and face. The major benefit is that it is an anti-aging agent. We already have this in our skin. As we age, we lose some along with collagen. Hyaluronic Acid in this Serum allows your skin to retain more moisture, whether you have oily skin or not. It has a lightweight texture and works for oily or dry skin and sensitive skin too. That's great because I personally have all of that going on with my face.

There are other serums out there similar to this. I like InterSight's Hyaluronic Acid because it is free of fragrance/scent and drying agents like alcohol. It's ingredients include (of course) hyaluronic acid, witch hazel, green tea, jojoba oil, vitamins c and e and aloe. So, if you are familiar with any of these you will know that these are elements are soothing to the skin and each have their own benefits. I like products that have natural ingredients versus a lot of chemicals that I don't know how to pronounce.

This product is advertised to activate collagen production, which is what the h. acid does. It goes beneath the skin's surface when applied correctly and retains moisture, plumping it up like youthful skin. When I use this, I notice that my skin appearance is very youthful and fresh. You can use your own moisturizer afterwards (I switch it up personally but mainly use Vanicream Light Lotion, not cream, because it's "Dye free, perfume/fragrance free, lanolin free, paraben free, formaldehyde free." Also, it isn't greasy.)

This bottle comes with a dropper in it. I have a few tips if it will help anyone for use.

1. The product directions are teeny tiny but it says to wash and dry your face, neck and décolletage area first.
2. Apply the product. I found that it's easier and less waste to put three drops on my left 3 finger pads - ring, middle and pointer finger, share some with the same fingers on the right hand and apply with an upward direction starting with the décolletage and neck area.
*Note - a little goes a long way. I used less than half a dropperful for 1 treatment.
*The drops I put on my left finger pads initially are maybe the circumference of or slightly less than a notebook paper hole that is punched out.
*Don't put any in your eye socket including eyebrows.
*Get close to your hairline but not in it, especially if you color your hair or are hiding gray hairs. Washing your hairline and putting products like this on it will fade the color quicker, at least when you are trying to cover up random stray gray or white hairs.
3. Let the product dry before adding moisturizer and then makeup (if any). It doesn't take too long. If you are really in a rush, I have a tip. I keep the mini, battery operated personal fans around for facial stuff. It will help it dry faster.
4. Personal tip - Use a moisturizer with SPF 30 or greater during the day when using this (and when not using it too!) I use Elta MD UV Shield Broad Spectrum SPF 45, the transparent version for a lot of reasons. Product is great, non-greasy, soaks in, is for the face and body, cost is reasonable, no scent and it protects my skin! I want to share this because I love products but have some I stick because of how affective it is.

This product is not sticky, greasy, and leaves zero residue on your hands, but I recommend washing them anyhow afterwards. Who knows if you may rub your eye, etc.

One last tip in case you don't know why you should use it on your décolletage, neck in addition to the face. Guess where aging shows the most? The neck and, not listed prior, your hands! Neck wise-look at people and their necks. The age usually shows up sooner. So, it's important to include it. I include those areas when getting facial peels too - glycolic or salicylic acid - in the fall and winter only. When you put sunscreen on, consider putting it on your hands too, or for that matter, your arms, especially the side that faces the window when you ride in a car.

I hope this helps. I have tried different hyaluronic products and really like this one for previous reasons - no scent, a little goes a long way, natural ingredients, leaves my skin very smooth and doesn't irritate at all plus all the benefits of it.

I am very happy with it and plan on buying another retail on Amazon when this one runs out, whenever that is! Thanks for reading my review and please, please use sunscreen if you decide to purchase and use this product!

review_title: Very helpful for plucking eyebrows and seeking imperfections in your skin!
review_text:
I ordered this Hampstead Home Vanity Mirror because when I'm getting ready for 'date night' with the hubby, I like to take my time putting on my face (applying my makeup). That usually means I'm sitting down and listening to the TV while trying to make sure my makeup is as flawless as possible. It helps tremendously to have a lighted mirror that has magnification so that I can make sure that my eyebrows are properly groomed and that I've managed to hide / blend any and all imperfections in my skin tone. On the flip side, you ONLY get the magnification with this mirror so if you want the overall effect, you better stand WAY back or go to another mirror.

In order to utilize the lighted feature of this mirror, you need to install 3 AA batteries (not included). The lighting is pretty awesome though and much better than the lighting I've experienced with another type of mirror. The suction cup is a nice feature, although not one that I personally need to use. This isn't a mirror that I will leave on my countertop and it's a very stable mirror so I don't see the need to suction it down. I think the price of this mirror is very reasonable and I've paid more than this for similar products.

review_text:

After a few trial and error rounds of doing glue-on nails, I learned to choose the nail that is the size smaller than the size you think is right (it spreads flat after it’s glued and then this also saves your cuticles). Also use a very small amount of glue. Even if you think it’s too little, it’s probably too much. It’s much easier to glue a nail back on than to deal with dried glue all over your cuticles and between your nail and finger skin. Also rubbing alcohol takes the excess glue off if you do have issues.

Also! Big tip - start with your pinky nails first. Do both pinkies, both rings, both middles, etc. Your thumbs are very useful in the application process so it’s best to do them last.

review_text:
These are wonderful hair drying wraps--by far the nicest that I've tried (I've been using these types of wraps for years.) These are so plush and soft, but also very absorbent. I love the bright colors. My absolute favorite thing about them is that they are large enough to fit all my hair. My hair isn't terribly long--three inches or so past my shoulders, and it's of medium thickness, I would say. Generally, my hair is too long for the typical hair wrap and an inch or so peaks out at the end of the twist. Not with these! These hold all my hair and there is maybe an extra inch of material, so they can hold even longer hair! And because they are so much bigger than the typical ones I use, they don't pull my hair so tight, which can result in a weird kink in the hair around my face, especially my bangs.

These don't completely dry your hair, but they do suck up a lot of the water. The longer you leave them on, the more they absorb. I usually only leave them on for ten minutes out of habit (see the weird kink in my hair the other kind leave). They are really nice!

I've been experimenting with glue-free and magnetic-free lashes and I really enjoyed using this product! Is it my absolute favorite? At the time of writing this review, so far, yes!

I really like the formula of the eyeliner, it has been one of the smoothest I have tried so far. As for the strength of the adhesiveness of the eyeliner with the lashes, it is super strong! Even the slightest touch of the lash to the eyeliner will have it STUCK! The eyeliner also is very water and smudge proof!

I have only taken one star off because the lash band itself can be a little bit irritating for people with small eyelids/monolids. While wearing these lashes, the inner corner of my eyes were feeling a bit irritated because the band was poking the skin. Eventually this made my eye water, and the inner corners of the eyelash were beginning to peel up. I feel that if I readjusted these lashes, or cut some portion off, it would help with the issue.

I've never used magnetic lashes before, but was very intrigued! These magnetic lashes + the eyeliner are STRONG! I've attached photos of the lashes after wearing them for 10 hours at my workplace. The magnetic lashes and the liner are so strong in fact, that I actually ripped out a lash because I accidentally had the magnetic liner on my lash!

I'm very impressed by how well it stuck onto my eye throughout the day. I am also VERY surprised of the formula of the eyeliner. I have tried many, many waterproof, smudgeproof eyeliners, but this eyeliner is by far THE MOST waterproof and smudgeproof! I have oily eyelids and my original waterproof eyeliner would still smear on my lower lids (I bought a waterproof Missha eyeliner for $27 and it still smudges!)

Not only that, the liner will also remove very easily with micellar water or makeup removing face wash -- it washes off so clean that I don't have to follow up with another makeup wipe after the shower. This is amazing!

I only really took off 1 star for three reasons:
1) The formula of the eyeliner has a scent that is very perfume-y/chemical-y. This doesn't bother me too much, but I do think that some customers may be bothered by it.
2) The brush of the eyeliner is very flimsy -- it is difficult to get a sharp line, because the brush is so thin.
3) the inner corners of my lashes began to curl up and off my lash line, pulling some eyeliner with it (leaving gaps in my liner).

Overall, I really like this small kit! It is VERY easy to apply and the lashes look so natural! I got very many compliments while wearing these!

review_title: What an amazing concept that is wonderfully executed!
review_text:
Boy, oh, boy! Not having to purchase bulk quantities of cotton swabs was the thing that pulled me towards this, both from an economic perspective and a consciously environmental one. I wasn't sure how the product would be in real life because I just kept imagining there is no way the swab won't fall off with use and cleaning.
But here are the great pros:
1) You get 4 swabs with 8 different ends that instantly multiplies how, where, and when you can use compared to the regular cotton swab. Used on the body, like ears, eyebrows, nails, etc. or even to clean tight spots in the kitchen, car, or keyboard!
2) You can disinfect them! Which is the best part! Cotton swabs are packed together and you are not sterile by any means. These can be disinfected because they seemingly withstand temperatures up to 230 C or 446 F. So I can easily boil them after use, apply alcohol, or use a multitude of methods to disinfect them safely.
3) Reusable over and over again
4) Highly effective. I have persistent unresolvable ear itching that started years ago because of the constant use of earplugs, and my dermatologist and I have tried all sorts of meds to resolve it to no avail. I use cotton swabs several times a day, and to me, they have never been entirely helpful. I have not tried all the tips for all the other things they could do, but I can say that for the hairy tip that it's the very best tool I have ever used that helped me with the itching. It does a perfect job, and I cannot recommend it highly enough.
They're very light, compact, come in a great case, super easy to clean and disinfect, if needed, highly effective, and will save money and storage space!

I have been searching for a really good mascara for a little while now. I have always been a fan of Maybelline's Colossal mascara, but they decided to change up the formula a while back and it's just not the same, especially the waterproof one.

Decided to give this one a shot and here is what I have found so far:

1. It's definitely not waterproof, so if you have any kind of allergies and watery eyes, beware, it will smudge all over the place.
2. It applies nicely. Gives even coverage on the lashes without weighing them down with too much product. I would say it is mostly true to the name of length and lift as it does do both, just don't be expecting to look like you have false lashes on.
3. The wand brush is a little more streamlined compared to that of the Colossal, which I think helps with the lifting and lengthening. Depending on how you like your lashes to look, a coat or two with this and you're good to go.
4. Durability - here is where I had somewhat of an issue. I apply my makeup in the morning before work (even with working from home I never know when I will have an impromptu video call, so I'm always prepared). This usually occurs shortly before 7am and I need my makeup to last me ALL DAY because I usually don't get around to washing it off until 10-11pm. What I have found with the Almay is that even though it goes on nice and evenly, half way through my day I start to find my lashes feeling weighed down and notice they start clumping together. I thought it was odd, so decided to try again the next day to see what happened and sure enough, same thing. I don't know if it's just due to the formula or what but that has been my experience.
5. Washes off very easily. I use coconut oil to remove my makeup and then use my cleanser to completely wash my face and I haven't had any issues with removal.

Since I do actually like the product aside from it's durability, I've decided to play around with it and see if I can get it to wear a little better. What I've been experimenting with is applying this first to add length and then apply my waterproof mascara to sort of set them both (and so it gives me the waterproof protection I need) and it seems to be holding up when used this way. Can't say what the real issue is with why this doesn't wear well all day.. is it me or is it the product itself..who knows? I don't hate it at all, just wish it would wear better.

Hope this helps!

review_title: not entirely convinced on how baby safe this is but maybe better for pre teens or adults
review_text:
I was curious about a perfume for baby because we've been taught not to use anything on the little ones except the gentlest of lotions and body wash. I decided to give this a try because I was curious about the scent and the execution of a product like this.

First thing I did was smell this, and while it is a pleasant smell, this particular scent isn't my favorite. It is too floral for me, almost artificial. I may have liked and felt more comfortable using a citrus and fruity type of scent on my little one. I also looked at the ingredients list and while they may be free of parabens, phthalates, synthetic colors, dyes, GMOs, and Gluten Free, there are some potentially irritating ingredients for the very sensitive of skins. Ingredients like Linalool, Citral, Citranellol, Limonene can be an allergen. It may have prebiotics which is good but one good ingredient does not negate a potentially irritating one. I'm all for someone coming up with a safe and good cologne for baby but I'm not entirely sold on this product just yet. I did read up on some additional information but I need more convincing for me to be on board with this perfume for infants. I do love the story of why the founder wanted to create these scents for little ones but I'm just not fully on board with some of the ingredients used.

I'm not sure I will be using this on my baby but I think a more appropriate age is pre-teen or teens. I may have been a little more open to a "cleaner" perfume for that age range as I'm sure there's a market for that. From what I read, the founder is going to be launching perfumes for that age group, so that might be more appropriate.

My baby actually smells nice from good hygiene so he doesn't need anything else but I understand the concept behind these scents. Fragrances do invoke certain memories, just like music. There are certain scents that I get a whiff of and it immediately transports me back to that day, the person, or the memories of that particular time period. All that said, I will be holding off using perfume on my baby and will be spritzing this stuff on myself. I think the concept is great but I would like to see even "better" and cleaner ingredients if I am to use it on my baby.

I didn't see the ingredients list posted on this Amazon page yet so here it is:
Ingredients:
Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance) Niacinamide, Glycerin, Lactitol, Xylitol, Linalool, Citral, Citranellol, Limonene, Hexyl Cinnamal, Gernaniol, Amyl Cinnamal, Limolene, Hydroxycitronellal.

review_title: you will see results if you commit to it
review_text:
I've been using this for 3 months now and I do think this works with longterm use. You obviously aren't going to see overnight results but if you keep at it you will notice a difference on your wrinkles. Luckily I don't have too many yet but I did use it on the little areas where I'm starting to see wrinkles. I noticed a tightening of the areas I used the laser on for the past 3 months. I really liked the hyaluronic acid serum that was included in the set - the serum felt gentle and has no smell (fragrance free). On some days where I didn't use the laser I would still use the serum to moisturize my face. I looked into purchasing just the serum, which they do have for sale, as I really like the product. The laser is easy to operate and charge (usb). I didn't use this daily as I wanted to give my skin a rest, but I think if you used this religiously then you would see results at a much faster rate. It isn't painful, but you feel a little zap. I would equate it to the same level of "pain" as a derma roller, that spikey/zappy feeling - not painful, not super uncomfortable. That of course, will depend on your skin sensitivity. I recommend using the lowest setting first then working your way up as your skin sensitivity will allow. Don't force your skin into what it cannot handle - listen to your body's reaction!

I've seen so many of these laser type products for the skin/body, and never tried it because I didn't trust it. Nira is the first at home laser product that I decided to give a chance to, as I trust it. Overall I am not disappointed but do know that you need to commit to it if you want to see results. If you are going to use it once every few weeks then it will be a while before you see results, if ever. I plan to keep using this to stimulate my skin.

review_title: a more natural approach for acne prone skin
review_text:
I am familiar with the Sibu brand as years ago I used to purchase the sea buckthorn oil supplements and was taking that religiously. I stopped just because I started to take other supplements (pre-natals, etc) and it was just getting to be too much I had to cut out some of the stuff. I still really like the Sibu brand and their sea buckthorn oil. I was pleasantly surprised to see that they now have skincare products. My favorite product in this set is still the sea buckthorn supplements (60 softgels). I am still nursing so I won't be taking this just yet but I am just about done nursing. The supplement is one thing I am looking forward to taking again. The expiration date is listed on the bottom of the bottle. I do like the smell of the anytime face wash, and it did a nice job of cleaning my face without drying it out. I do get little hormonal breakouts here and there so this is a good face wash for me. I've also tried the daily facial defense oil, a zit zapper, but it is too soon to tell if it works. It does a great job of moisturizing my face for sure as it is packed with different kinds of oils (argan, sea buckthorn, lavender, patchouli, etc). All these products are made in the USA, which I know is important for some people. This is a good set of skincare basics for acne prone skin. I like the more "natural" approach with the use of sea buckthorn oil and less harsh chemicals. This product came in a cardboard box (like a subscription style box) and placed inside a bubble foil zip loc style bag. Good packaging.

Some improvements ideas for this product:
- supplement does not say how many to take per day. The supplement facts says "serving size 2 vegan softgels", so I am assuming that means I should be taking 2 pills a day, making this a 1 month supply. There is no information pamphlet in the box or in this Amazon description page
- ingredients list for all 3 products should be listed on this Amazon page, I didn't see it listed yet
- brand name is confusing and made it hard for me to do more research on this product. Is the name of this product line "NOT OR" or "Not for him or her" or "NxO" or "NO"? It is just all very confusing. Either way, all of the names still made it hard to do a search because it sounds like it is a part of a sentence.

There are four products to try:
- restoring serum
- activating exfoliator
- softening hydra-wrap
- eye rejuvenating elixir

My favorite is the hydra wrap and exfoliator.
The hydra wrap is quite moisturizing and rich without feeling heavy, nor did it feel sticky/tacky after applying. I could slightly feel it on my skin after applying but it wasn't greasy or uncomfortable. The exfoliator has little shea nut powder beads in it to help exfoliate and scrub, and has a thick consistency. It is like your typical face exfoliator except it has great, good for your skin, quality ingredients.

The eye elixir is good and felt like a gentler/less rich moisturizer compared to the face cream.

I didn't like the serum because of the consistency - it is too liquid-y for me, and is almost like a toner than your typical serum. It felt fine on the face but I just didn't like how runny it was. The dropper style dispenser is great but it was like dispensing toner.

Overall, I really enjoyed AAVRANI's product line. I'm actually surprised at the quality of the packaging for a trial set like this. It is just as luxurious as the full sized products. That is still my mantra, but occasionally when I know I’ll be in the sun I put on a good Asian sunscreen - because they tend to uncheck all the boxes of the things I mentioned above. That said, this is another sunscreen I am adding to my collection. It did not feel uncomfortable on my skin and did not leave any white cast or blotches. It absorbed pretty quickly and my skin didn’t feel tacky. Also, this is SPF 50! All in all, this is another Asian facial sunscreen that I am adding to my “loves” list.

review_title: Has everything you need for skincare routine
review_text:

There’s a cleanser, toner, face cream, eye cream, etc. The packaging is beautiful and for some of the items, heavy (glass). There is a light scent but it is nothing overwhelming or offensive. The amount of product is also quite generous, especially given the affordable price tag for all of these items. If you were to purchase items like these separately (from a different brand) it would definitely be way over this price point. My favorite is the face cream. It is light, not too heavy or greasy, and just dries on your face with a nice moisturized feeling. Although I am using all these products myself, I could see this being a wonderful gift set. It makes a good gift for Mother’s Day or birthday. This also makes a good starter kit of basic skin care essentials. Not the most high end skin care but not bad.

Just a tip: Although the product labels are in Chinese, there is English on each of the bottles stating what the product is (eg: eye cream)
You can throw away the packaging with the English product description but you just have to remember how to use it.

Having previously been disappointed with another one of their product (spilled and dried out), I was half expecting this product to arrive the same way. While this one did not arrive dried out, it was disappointing to see the eye patches were not drenched in the solution like most eye patches I’ve tried. They looked almost dry. It applies fine but just would have been better soaked in more solution.

The patches also breaks too easily. I just put my fingernails on it and it split apart. I usually wear my glasses when I am using eye patches at night and have never experienced any that tore during use but these did. It tore near/underneath my eyeglass nose pad, which I had not touched with my fingers. When I went to remove them they broke apart in several pieces, which has never happened with any eye patches I have used. Overall these just did not leave a good impression on me.

review_title: Really liking the blessing of sprout products
review_text:
It took me a while to try this out and I finally was able to. When I opened it, at first I thought the cream went bad. The texture just looked different. Usually face creams look smooth but this had almost a goopy look before even putting my finger into it and testing it out. I came here and noticed that everyone pretty much had the same experience and it wasn’t that my jar that went bad - so I figured it was safe to put on my skin.

Upon applying, it is a bit tacky and sticky feeling but after rubbing it in to my skin and letting it settle, it fully absorbed into my skin. I loved the smell of this product. I thought it moisturized quite well without being too heavy or light. I wanted to try this cream because it uses lotus extract and other sprouts, which is just different from most of the western face cream products out there. I’m sure one day western products will catch up and do the same thing as Asian/Korean beauty products, as I have seen time and time again. I also paired this product with the serum from the same product line, and have been loving how my skin feels.

These bristles are SO soft! These will definitely not make you feel like you are scraping a layer of your skin off like most brushes do. This lathers very well which is great when I am trying to get my back. This brush is really so soft that I can use it on my baby as well. The wood handles are quite sturdy. Very good quality, dense brush.

review_title: Loving this product! It’s white, not blue, so don’t worry!
review_text:
I am starting to ramp up my mask use again and do them about 3 times a week. This week I gave these a try and really liked them. First of all, the smell was quite nice - very light but a very nice smell. I actually try to put all the serum that was stuck on the package onto the mask because I wanted more of the nice smell on my face. The mask is soaked in serum and had a little extra left which I scooped out and piled onto the mask on my face. The material of the mask is soft. After 20 minutes it was not dry yet (still damp) but I removed the mask to a very moisturized face. I was able to massage the rest of the serum into my skin and sort of wiped off some of the excess. I really enjoyed using this mask and I’m actually looking forward to the next one.

One thing I thought was that this mask is going to be blue colored, as it mentioned about a blue powder (copper peptide?). When I opened the package it was your standard white mask, white serum. It was a little confusing to me with the image of the blue cream in the front and the mention of a blue powder on the back of the packaging. Just know that this mask just looks like your typical face mask, soaked in white serum!

review_title: good for many things, sturdy yet biodegradable
review_text: I used these with my own liquid makeup remover to take the day off my face and it works great. Prior to this I was using cotton rounds and would have to use quite a few to get my whole face clean. With these I only used one towel. There are 50 in a box so it will last me more than a month. I like that these are biodegradable yet they are very sturdy and strong (I tried to rip them by stretching it but it would not rip!). These also have a good thickness to it - not too thick, not too thin. Good as makeup remover wipes or anything you want to use them for (cleaning, as a hand towel, as a towel to wash baby, etc).

review_title: no more lugging around a heavy bottle of perfume / body spray
review_text: Prior to these I had been carrying wet wipes in my bag for when I’m out and need a little refreshing / wipe down sweaty body parts. The wet wipes are not scented and I did not want to carry a bottle of perfume or scented spray with me because those are too heavy and bulky. I would be clean but I wanted to smell nice. These perfume wipes are the perfect solution for me. I now have these in my bag whenever I am out (to the park, grocery shopping, etc) and I don’t have to worry if I start to sweat or not smell as fresh as a bed of roses. What I’ll do is I wipe myself down with wet wipes first then I’ll swipe these on my neck and wrists. These are so convenient! I really like this scent as well. These would also be great for weekend getaways where you’ll have one less heavy thing (perfume bottle) to pack. The only issue is that it is not very cost effective - but you’ll have to weigh convenience with cost to see which is more important to you.

I just love the scent of this serum! Others are saying they smell vanilla but for some reason it smells like honey to me and I just love the scent. I am trying to phase out skin care that have added smells but I just could not resist this one! After applying the serum to my face and spreading it all over, it just seeps into my skin and moisturizes. It did not feel sticky or tacky at all. I really enjoyed using this serum at night before bed and letting it work its magic. Now that we are in colder weather my skin needs a thicker face cream like oils/serum so this is just perfect. I plan to use this every night because the scent just soothes and relaxes me. I can’t wait to try the other products in their line!

These wipes are great for when you are out and not want to lug around a huge bottle of hand sanitizer in your bag. They don’t really smell like alcohol or anything overwhelming at all, which I was surprised with. This would be a good wipe to bring with you to a restaurant where you can use it on your hands first then wipe down the table. I like this wipes but they can get a little pricey in comparison to pump gel/liquid sanitizers (per use).

review_text: I know scents are a personal thing and can be a hit or miss for most people. I didn’t mind the vanilla musk scent at all and thought it was pleasant. This is a good sized bottle and should last quite a while. For anyone who does not want to use this as a shower gel you can always use it as hand soap or as a refill for your hand soap. I already have plenty of shower gels I need to use up in my own shower so I am putting this in our guest bathroom, especially since the bottle has a nice floral design. My only complaint is this is a Korean product but they should have also included a list of ingredients in English in case it was a gift and the recipient needed to make sure they were not allergic to anything used in this shower gel.

review_title: a face cream for use in the colder seasons
review_text:
I like that this product uses oils like jojoba, cocoa, and coconut. This face cream is a little on the richer side (but not super rich and thick to where it is hard to soak into the skin). It is a little on the oily side but the thing is now that the colder/fall/winter season is coming, this is the perfect face cream for the season. I would not recommend this for use during the hot summer but your skin will drink this up in the cold. The scent was light and pleasant, but that always comes down to personal preference as some people are very sensitive to smell.

It says this cream has collagen and stem cells, but I’m not sure how much of those ingredients are used in the formulation. It would be nice to know because if there is too little then there is probably very little anti wrinkle benefits. As with all beauty/skin care products it takes time to see the results. Overall this is a good face cream if you just want something moisturizing for the face but I can’t say yet if this will help erase or prevent any wrinkles.

I love face oils and never worry about them being too oily because I only use them at night before bed - that way they have time to seep into the skin and work while I sleep. I just love the smell of this one - especially when the smells are from oils / essential oils, and nothing synthetic. This bottle is just chock full of good stuff, good ingredients, and herbs and things. As we get into the winter season this will be perfect to keep my skin moisturized so at the moment I am using it sparingly. After trying this face oil I am excited to explore other products from Laloirelle because their formulation and ingredients used are exactly the type of stuff I love and trust to use on my skin.

I am saving some of these for my next weekend getaway as they are super lightweight and I’ll have one less bulky product to bring (facial cleanser). My night time face routine usually consists of step one, using makeup remover wipes to get rid of all the makeup, and step two, washing everything off with a facial cleanser. These do a good job doing the second round of cleaning my face. Please know that these are not to replace makeup removers and will not get your mascara off. Overall this is a great product for washing your face (no makeup). My only concern is these are a bit pricey per use, understandably so as they are individually packaged, so I would probably save these for travel convenience and not so much a product I would use daily at home.

OMFG this brush is amazing! I have 3B style curls and I'm also biracial so my hair is really porous and a bit on the fragile side. In its curly state it's a pain to care for but the traditional blow dry and flat iron method is both tedious and damaging to my hair.

When wet to straight irons came out, I immediately hopped on board because it just made more sense that heating my hair while wet would be less damaging to it. Through this I got hooked lol. But even with that it is a bit tedious.... though it did help me figure out that I could flat iron my hair dry and skip the blow dryer.

My boyfriend has one of these brushes and I tried it as a quick way to straighten my hair in the am. I was SUPER impressed! But it had some design flaws that made me seek my own, and landed me here.

From what I've seen comparing this brush to the more popular Rinfy and his brush, they've reallly improved upon the original design concepts. Most notably, the buttons are on the front of the handle and not the sides, down near the cord instead of anywhere up near the head. This along with the way they're shaped to be concaved makes it highly unlikely they'll be pressed by accident. But even if you do press them by accident, the device automatically locks them about 30s after the temperature is set. If you want to change the temp or turn it off after that, you need to click the power button twice to unlock them.

The teeth are not only steep enough to accommodate my thick hair, but there's also way more of them packed more densely together. This seems to make this brush MUCH quicker at straightening my hair, and it can also get it board straight. The other brushes have only gotten it as close as a little wave.

Since my hair is so thick, I also have to place my hand on the bristles while I pull the brush through so it gets all my hair in it. This is the only model I've tried which hasn't burned me even once while using it so far. The teeth are so densely packed that there is no way for a finger or the side of my hand to slip down past the safety portion of it.

Quick heating? Honestly I don't know why anyone tries to claim that.... I've never seen any heated hair product heat up quickly. My stove doesn't even heat up quickly. I hardly expect my straightening iron or brush to defy the laws of physics so I don't have to wait a few minutes for it to heat up. That's why I turn it on BEFORE I'm ready to use it. 😉

All joking aside though, this really is a fantastic brush. It even FEELS high quality. Nice weight, premium plastics, slick design. It will fit right in with other hair devices no matter how pricey they are.

review_title: Not for long or thick hair
review_text:
This was my first time using hair chalk. After reading the reviews I was hopeful for good results with little mess. Well, the results were just under satisfying and the mess was exactly what I was worried about.
It’s chalk, I get it. But there were so many reviews saying the color stayed in and didn’t rub off onto white clothing! Thank goodness my daughter’s costume was black. Though we could still see blue/green on her shoulders and back. Her neck was blue/green for 3 days. And after 3 showers her hair still had color in it.
We used leave in conditioner and hairspray since I read many reviews advocating for them. I think if your hair is short, this could benefit you. My daughters hair is long and thick, and it was awful. I tried not to brush, but I inevitably had to comb horrible knots caused by the chalk being rubbed onto damp hair. (And a spray bottle is a must, chalk on dry hair is a joke.) This caused much of the color to fly away in clouds of chalk.
True, her hair was colored blue/green, but it was not the vibrant color that initially came off of the chalk. It was muted at best.

I strongly recommend doing this outside and with clothing on you don’t care about. Any tools you use in the process will subsequently get chalk all over it. Our flat and curling irons cleaned up easy enough.
I got some wet chalk on my light blue jeans and the color has stained.
When you iron your hair the chalk will dissipate in colorful clouds. And the remaining color will slowly work itself out on your clothes, chairs, couches, pillows, and eventually multiple showers.
I will say I chose chalk over dye for the benefit of no chemicals on my girl or in my house. But I think a mask would have helped, as we probably ended up inhaling tons of chalk!
Hope you have better luck than we did.

review_title: Look no further you found your brush
review_text:
I had been thinking about getting a new brush for a while. I have had an Oral-B Sonicare for about 4 years. It still works, but I had been thinking there may be something better with the advance of technology the last few years. The Sonicare brush vibrated from side to side, which I have always like much better than the brushes that rotate in a circle so I was very nervous about giving this brush a shot. All I can say is, WOW!

This brush is amazing. The Sonicare never seem to brush hard enough, whereas the top setting on this brush is exactly what I hoped it would be. I was also always a bit confused how firm I should hold the brush against my teeth and the 4000 series essentially makes that dummy proof as a giant red light comes on when you are pressing to firm.

The best comparison I can make is to describe this as the cordless version of the brush your dentist uses. It's that swirling brush that leaves your teeth feeling like you just left Dr. Dental's office each day. For folks that don't like as firm or rough a brush, there's enough settings to tone it down, but I have found that most brushes don't have a setting firm enough rather than delicate enough. This brush solves that problem.

I read some complaints about the handle, the charger, etc. I can't imagine why people could even complain as it's the last thing I would notice nor do I think either are a problem. The charging stand is nice and you can remove the holding case that attaches to it if you're worried about counter space. You also get a nice travel case, which is a huge plus because every time I took my sonicare on vacation, I would have to bring it with my carry on or else the on button would also get pushed in the suitcase and end up basically dead by the time I arrive.

I had a tough time justifying buying a new brush when I had one that worked fine. I couldn't be happier I took a chance as I firmly believe this brush will leave me much healthier teeth. I have to believe the Oral-B brand will last as my brush from 4 years ago is still going strong.

What a great buy.

review_title: Great on wavy/curly hair! Faster and more efficient!
review_text:
My youngest daughter is 7 and has very fine but very thick blonde hair that is curly in the back but not too curly on the top. She is always going to school looking crazy unless i put her hair up everyday or straighten it and with 3 other kids to get ready I don't have a lot of time for that so when I saw this product I knew I had to give it a try!
This brush straightener worked amazing on my daughters hair. I did her hair in sections because the back is very curly but it helped tone down the frizz in her hair as well as keep the curls under control. To use it all you do is section the hair and literally just brush through it with the product on, I did go underneath the hair as well at the bottom of the hair just to get out a lot of the curl that is close to her scalp.
The product doesn't get so hot that you can't use it but it does go up to 230 degrees which is a good temperature to use and is definitely hot enough to straighten your hair but not burn your hand. On the side is a digital display to tell you what the temperature is set at and is very easy to read.
The best part of this product though for me was honestly the ease in which it can be used and how much time it actually saved me rather than actually straightening her hair with a flat iron. I also loved that it didn't get as hot as my flat iron as my daughter moves too much and is always claiming she's getting burnt because the flat iron does produce heat when it's closed to your scalp (of course she really isn't but she's 7 so try explaining the difference, it's impossible). The one negative aspect I could potentially see is that if your root area was very kinky and curly I don't know how well this product would work on your roots, like I said though on my daughters wavy/curly type hair it worked great though! This is absolutely perfect for the people who want to take some waves of for people who have straight hair and just want that added silliness you get from a flat iron!

TLDR: GET THIS mask if you know you dont react to fragrance and simply like the smell of honey. DO NOT get this mask if you are looking for a mask with lots of honey and no added fragrance ingredients.

I almost returned this face mask because when I recieved it, one of them seemed to have leaked through the plastic package they were bundled in. Let me first say that this mask is the best smelling mask I have tried yet. I cant believe how lovely it smells, it took me back a bit. This concerned me of course as when something smells amazing it usually has fragrance added to it. When looking at the ingredients, I found that it does have "fragrance" in the ingredients, though it is farther down on the list of ingredients so it is not very much.

Near the bottom too, however, is propolis. Which is the only ingredient related to honey in this mask. Which was rather disappointing as this means this mask has hardly any honey in it.

I probably wont reorder this unless my skin somehow loves it.

Pros: Lightweight enough.
Bristles glide easily (I do brush out her hair first).

Cons: Takes FOREVER to heat up. They say 30 seconds up in the description, but like a full 5 minutes to reach 200C.
It's display is Celsius. I had to do some math to figure out what to set it on. Call me a dumb American or whatever, but every other hair tool I own is Fahrenheit.
You have to provide some real tension in the hair to get both the roots and the ends straight. This may work better with a glove when you get to the ends to hold them there, but I didn't have one handy and had to go over the ends several times.
So, I would pretty well recommend this for someone my daughter's age where she's going to be safe using it on her own. I don't think I would use it on my own hair unless for some reason I found myself without my other styling tools. It's a good way for her to learn how to take care of her hair though.

review_title: An adjustment but worth the money
review_text:
I really struggled with these lashes but I had to stop getting extensions so I really just forced myself to get comfortable with them. So I kind of played mad scientist and I'm gonna comfortable with them. I have some tips for anytime struggling.

1. If you HATE liquid eyeliner like me, do your eyeliner with whatever you use normally. I like my felt tip pens. So I did my eyeliner, then took the magnetic eyeliner, wiped the excess off the sides back into the tubs, and carefully just did a line thick enough on my eyelash base to get the magnetic property there. It was waaaay easier for me and therefore less messy and I didn't accidentally place them too high, they were truly down on my eyelashes.

2. I have very round eyes and they're big but not wide, so I cut them up! Instead of one long strip I have about 5 pieces of each lash to individually put on.
I found them easier to put on this way and I didn't have to shorten them to fit my eye, just space them out properly so I'm not just cutting up a good product unnecessarily that I paid full price for.

3. Decide if you like the applicator took they gave you or not. I put the lashes on with my fingers, but then use the applicator took to really squeeze them into my normal eyelashes so they blend flawlessly and you can't see an awkward gap between real and fake.

4. DO NOT TRY TO JUST RIP THEM OFF!!! You're going to rip your real eyelashes off. I would know, trust me I lost some soldiers the first time I took these off tipsy and just ripped them off 🥴
I get a towel and warm water and loosen the product, then an oil-free makeup remover on a soft towel and sat that on for a good minute to really get the magnetic properties off.

Overall worth the money but man it was an adjustment.

review_title: Great quality cases. Thin walls but can be poured from the bottom for a professional finished look.
review_text:
I got these for making my own deodorant because I'm tired of ones that don't work or have toxic fillers. It's very simple to do with some Coconut Oil, Bees Wax, Baking Soda and Essetial Oil. Just google and you can find many great recipes.

These are quality deodarant cases. The thickness of the walls is on the thin side, so it will hurt if you don't roll up the deodorant high enough and rub the thin edges on your bare skin. The roll mechanism works well. The one significant advantage I found in these when compared to others, is that you pour through the bottom. Most cases you must pour through the top and it has its problems. If your mix is very liquid, it can come spilling through the bottom, as well as sealing the moving mechanism tight. Having this unit upside down and pouring through the bottom makes for a more professional finished product. The top of the deodorant fills the cap below and takes it shape. When you open the hardened deodorant, it has the desired domed shape. Also you control how much you pour from the bottom, filing to the point where it doesn't effect the spinning mechanism.

Overall there are more expensive cases you can get that have a thicker wall, which will be more comfortable to the skin. However for this price point, these cases are the best as you can pour from the bottom.

I recently purchased a bunch of stampers to test, these included. These were among the worst I tested. All 3 of these are hard stampers with no squish to them. The green is the hardest, followed by white, then the red (the one I received was actually pink). When they're this hard, know that you need to roll the design on rather than press it on. Rolling, if not done carefully can lead to smudging. Also, hard stampers are not forgiving on curved nails. It will hit the highest part of your nail and miss the lower areas. I also found that the hard stampers do a bad job at filling in solid areas of designs, but only work well on designs with fine lines. The red (pink) one was the best of this bunch, very similar to the Konad double ended stamper. Although, I prefer the Konad because it is slightly larger. These have enough stability to them that you really can flick and get straight little lines that look just like hairs. They are thin and you have actual control. This formula also lasts forever! I definitely have to use makeup remover to get it off, so it is for sure waterproof. I also like that this color isn't pulling red on me. The only complaint I have is that when I open these there was a little bit of ink that had leaked out around the applicator at the top so it looked a little messy, but I love the way this works so much I don't care One thing to note is that it's best to put this on before you use any other wax or gels to keep your brow hairs in place. review_text: I've been in the market for a microneedling device for a while now, but I wasn't sure if I needed something super expensive or if I could get away with a more budget-friendly option. I decided to try two super inexpensive versions , both costing around $20 and see if this significantly more expensive option from GloPRO was really worth it. In short, yes. Both of the cheaper options were incredibly painful and flimsy feeling. One of them even felt kind of like getting a face tattoo. It was awful. The GloPRO option actually feels nice on the skin because of the vibration feature and the red light therapy is a huge benefit for those monthly breakouts. I do feel like my skin care is absorbing more effectively since I've been using this, but it's still an extremely expensive tool. If you really want a microneedling device, in my opinion this is worth the investment, however, I don't think it's a necessary item.

review_title: Falls apart quickly, fine mist spray, very small size
review_text:
I wanted a spray bottle to sparingly disperse a mild bleach-and-water solution onto counters and into my toilet bowls, but didn't want a full-size bottle. My experience with full-size bottles is that you never know what you're getting in terms of quality. Unfortunately, I should have applied the same logic to these bottles. Lesson learned.

These are really small. These are well-suited for misting hair, or misting plants, or spraying a solution into the air. That said, they also serve the purpose for which I needed such a bottle. There's no setting on these, and no way to turn them "off", if that is important to you.

The bottle is sturdy plastic. The screw-cap is sturdy and secures tightly with no leaks, allowing me to shake my solution before use. At first use, this worked great for the first three days. Sprays were consistent and never missed a beat.

Unfortunately, at some point on the third day, the top of the trigger popped up and out of place, and the whole trigger assembly came apart. I am fairly mechanically inclined, and figured out, after some effort, how to put the whole thing back together. However, the same fault kept occurring. It seems the whole assembly is merely held together by very light connections, where things click together. If the top of the trigger pops out of place, the whole thing comes apart.

My solution to this was to wrap an elastic hair-tie around the top of the trigger to the base of the trigger, just behind the actual trigger. This keeps the top from popping off and solves the problem. However, nobody should have to do that.

I am still able to use the one bottle in this fashion, and I really can't complain. I put the second bottle away for the inevitable failure of the first one. I can't really recommend these.

review_title: Great scent, good hold and volume, rinses poorly
review_text:
After having had a 1/4-inch buzzcut for about 15 years, about 18 months ago, I started growing out my hair, which is now quite long and sits around the bottom of my ear. As a result, I've been using different types of hair products to style it in different ways and keep it under control. Given a chance to try this pomade, I decided to give it a shot.

Packaging-wise, this is really simple: a glass jar with a metal lid. It has that old-timey barbershop feel, and would look nice on your counter or shelf, if you're into displaying your grooming products. Just remember it's glass, and an accidental drop on your counter or tiled floor is going to result in a disaster. The lid is a good quality and the seal seems to keep the product fresh.

As soon as you open this jar, you'll recognize that "barbershop scent". It has that minty-eucalyptus odor that's refreshing and eye-opening. There are days when I use this, when I'm sitting at my desk I wonder "what smells so good"...and I realize it's my hair. So if you're into good scents and smelling-good for yourself or others, you'll definitely like this.

The consistency of this product is quite interesting. It looks like vanilla pudding. However, it's definitely much thicker than vanilla pudding. It's not sticky. It feels and looks like a compound that would end up very oily in your hair, but that's not the result. Even given my hair's length, I don't have to use a lot of this, and typically on damp hair I only have to use about two fingertips' worth of this product in my hair.

While your mileage may vary, when I put this in my hair, it has an immediate effect. It provides immediate styling strength. It also helps to add a bit of volume, so that as I comb it through, I can easily prop-up the parts of my hair to give it a little volume and height. It dries well and doesn't get too stiff, leaving my hair with some movement, where I'm not afraid to run my fingers through it or adjust it. I'd say it's really good for my more "casual day" styles.

My only complaint, and for me this is really important, is that it doesn't rinse well in the shower. I only wash my hair every third day to maintain its health, and while nearly every other product I use rinses almost cleanly without leaving much of a residue, this particular product won't rinse cleanly. This becomes a problem if I use this on day two, but want to use a different product on day 3, for example. It definitely adds to residual build-up. I realize not every product rinses cleanly with just water, but this one is particularly problematic, forcing me to either wash my hair earlier or plan the days on which I use this so the build-up doesn't become an issue on consecutive days. So, if like me, you don't like washing your hair often, this may be a deal-breaker.

Overall, though, I'm quite impressed. The small jar is actually going to last me quite some time. It has a great scent and styling power. I'd probably use it every day if it weren't for the rinsing issue.

I have been using Bare Minerals for years now, and only recently stumbled across the IQ mineral foundation. From now on, I will be purchasing the IQ: Natural Eco-Smart Mineral Foundation. First of all, there is more product in the IQ container than the standard Bare Minerals container. I like the color of the IQ Medium Beige better than Bare Mineral's medium beige. The Bare Escentuals version would be too light during the summer, and too dark during the winter. The IQ seems to work better with my skin tone, and looks more natural on me. The foundation worked well with my existing kabuki brush, and I apply it in the same manner with which I used Bare Minerals. The product makes my skin look great, with natural looking and even coverage, and offers good coverage for acne scarring as well. It did not cause any irritation to my skin, nor did it break me out (which my acne-prone skin has a tendency to do with other products). It feels weightless on and lasts for hours and hours.

More product, lower price, and same great coverage.. IQ: Natural Eco-Smart Mineral Foundation is my new go-to foundation!

I put a ball in my glass mug and poured boiling water anyway. There is no "flowering" like you may get from flowering tea balls. It just sort of filled the entire mug with flowers - petals and flowers. Like the entire mug. It was the consistency of a thick stew. You might get a few sips for the space that is left after the flowers expand. I was actually impressed with how much "flower" was there from that tiny and light ball.

I sipped it and was snot impressed with the flavor. Light at that and must have been chamomile as chamomile smells like chicken soup to me and I am not a fan of chamomile or this "tea". It was the consistency of soup, though... a hearty chowder. It was not fragrant in any way either so I think although you get plenty of flowers for a tub - you are defeating the purpose of adding fragrant flower petals to your bath. Plus no ingredients anyway. It seemed like all flowers - it really did - but I am not really sure what is in there. Plus some people are allergic to certain herbs and flowers anyway. I was hesitant to try yet another deodorant as most end up sucking big time and end up in a wasteland... But I did - and I AM SO GLAD THAT I DID! This stuff is AMAZING! It works - it REALLY WORKS!!! And a little goes a long way. I just rub a little under my pits, then I use an old large empty deodorant container that has a large rounded top to really smooth it in under my arms. Then that is it!

Even on the sweatiest, most humid days, where I am running around literally miles and miles - this stuff keeps me smelling fresh. Plus it also acts as a decent enough antiperspirant as well for me. While the rest of me ends up dripping - my pits were pretty fresh. I Really love that! Plus after already like three months - this stuff is STILL going strong. I am up to my second scent - hoping to maybe try one more - but so far Dreamcatcher is light and lovely! LOVE THIS STUFF!!!

review_title: NOT spirals in any way shape or form - but did a decent job making some body in my hair
review_text:
First off - how these arrive in the bag - like a little roll - is the way they will end up in your hair. There is no way to make them spiral at all. More like standard old school curls.

I found them a bit hard to use as well - as I found it a big pain to get the stick through the curler. I ended up squashing like four of five on the stick at a time (since that was the truly painful part) and then using it on my hair one after the other. Plus even though I cut my hair to like shoulder length - these are actually pretty short - just for the ends of your hair really.

With that being said - I tried these one night after a shower - letting my hair dry by at least half. I put the curlers in while watching TV. Left them in for like an hour, ran my hairdryer over them until my hair felt dry and took them out. My hair definitely had some bounce and was sort of curly. So if you are looking for body - these might definitely work. If you are looking for tight curls (especially spirals) - probably look elsewhere. On the plus side - for work the next day - my hair still had some body and felt thicker when I put it up. So again - they did definitely add body to my hair.

review_title: Surprisingly, it really makes a difference!
review_text:
I get "outbreaks" on my hands sometimes. Usually when my hands get bad (even just one hand) I have to apply a cortisone rub a few times a day over a few days to make the redness, flakiness, and itchiness subside.

I was hesitant to get this because the ingredients seem pretty simple for something that is supposed to make a difference in psoriasis. Well I am surprised at how effective this spray is. Instead of touching the cortisone rub at all - I just sprayed this on the backs of my hands. Granted I was working form home for the entire day - so I pretty much sprayed it a bunch of times over the course of the day. The redness got MUCH better. And the flakiness totally went away. The only thing is my skin on the bad hand looked a bit dry - but I guess that is because this is a spray and not an emollient cream or anything. To the touch, my hand felt pretty soft with only the slightest dry patches felt. Anytime I can avoid cortisone (steroids) I consider a really good time.

I am happy with this spray and have a feeling I will always have to keep some on hand going forward. Some might think the price may be a bit much - but if it works...plus if you can avoid drugs - it is probably worth it. Plus the bottle may last quite sometime anyway.

review_title: Sadly let down by this liner.
review_text:
I wanted to like this eyeliner pen, I really did...but I just couldn't. If you can get it for super cheap or almost free, it might be worth your time, but only if you don't have watery eyes AT ALL.

I have several issues with this eyeliner:

1. It isn't labeled as waterproof so I wasn't expecting it to be such, but I was expecting "water resistant". I mean, eyes are WET, and this product is meant to draw an artistic line on the eye area. Nope, it melted right off the second my eye got the slightest amount of dampness in the corner. Wing disappeared almost completely within 5 minutes of application on one eye.

2. The color dries a bit more muted than the actual color appears to look upon first inspection. The plastic housing the felt eyeliner is a very vivid and bright blue, so I expected the product to be similar in color. As I drew it on my eyelid, it appeared very bright...but sadly dried down to a deeper and less bold shade of blue. I didn't want one shade lighter than "navy", I wanted a color that would truly stand out.

3. If you miss a spot and have to go over an area that already has eyeliner, expect to have to redo the entire eye. Touching up a small area removes all of the color from the surrounding areas where the brush even gently grazes. Get it right the first time or redo the entire eye, there is NO layering with this brush eyeliner. Most of my liquid eyeliners are a bit more forgiving in this area.

So bottom line...not what I hoped for. I expected more from a major brand like Too Faced. I guess there is a reason why it has been discontinued and is almost being given away with such a cheap price. The idea is nice...it looks like a writing pen. You can even put it in your shirt pocket like one, and it's adorable packaging. You may have more luck if you have very dry eyes, or if you want to use it as a bottom lash eyeliner...but don't expect to make fine-lined wings or artistic designs with it. I have ultra cheap Wet N Wild eyeliner with far more staying power.

My first impression of the razor was that it was overly packaged. In a day and age in which we're becoming aware of environmental hazards, I don't think there's a need for an outer box enclosing a couple layers of thick hard-to-open plastic wrapping. A strong pair of scissors cut through the lot, and eventually I got to the razor itself.

I was pleased to see that it comes with a hard-shell case for travel. This is definitely a good thing to have, though I would have preferred it were only one piece that swivels open and shut, rather than two pieces that have to be separated to open it.

The instructions indicate that the charging pod should be unplugged when the razor is fully charged (which takes about an hour). While hardly the worst thing in the world, I don't see why they couldn't have designed it so that it could remain plugged it but turned off. In general, I prefer not to have plugs lying around exposed, especially in the bathroom, where I think most people would tend to keep it. It does have a very clear indicator, though, telling how much longer it needs to charge before reaching the full 65 minutes, and, after a couple weeks of usage, it still did not need to be recharged, so it definitely holds the charge well.

The razor itself is stylish and comfortable to hold, and it has a trimmer on the back, which is good for sideburns and the awkward just-under-the-nostrils area.

My first shave felt like it took ages, and, half-way through, I seriously considered giving up and getting out my old blade and shaving cream. I decided to stick with it, and, eventually, I figured out that you can't just press it to your face, but press it rather firmly. With more pressure, it eventually got the job done. Subsequent shaves went much easier, and as I got used to using the shaver, the shave-time got less and less. It does a significantly better and faster job on only one day's growth rather than two or three, so it's much more ideal for everyday use than if you tend to go a few days between shaves.

Clean-up is easy and fast. Just flip the three razor bits up and rinse with hot water. I'm a little suspicous about using water to clean it each day - I would tend to think it'll rust - but time will tell.

After shaving, my face sometimes feels less comfortable than had I used a regular blade and shaving cream, but usually it feels all right. This is the third electric shaver I've owned, and it has been the case with all three that the shave is not as close as even the worst blade I've used. There's really no getting around it: you'll always get a closer shave using a real blade. I'd say this is easily the best of the three electric razors I've used, though, and did a significantly better job on the chin, due to its swiveling head.

Overall, I find myself liking this shaver, particularly for the traveling and the cold winter months, when I don't really want to deal with a wet shave in the morning.

This bag would be PERFECT if it had mesh pockets in the main compartment. I love this style of bag, with the two additional outside pockets, but there aren't a lot of bags in this style and they're all missing something. This one is missing inside pockets. I hope Veckle will add pockets in the future. A slightly smaller everyday bag with a similar design would be great as well.

Anyway, this bag seems very well made. It has SBS zippers which all my Gonex bags have as well, and they've all been excellent. I have like 10 Gonex packing cubes that I've stuffed beyond reason, and the zippers are still perfect. So these zippers should last, too. The top zipper has two sliders so you can open it in either direction.

The bag is made with lightweight materials without any padding or rigid structure, so you can flatten it. If you pack only a little bit of stuff, it stays small. If you pack a lot, it gets bigger. I love that. The main pocket is just for dumping stuff. There's no organization, which I need, so I won't be able to use this bag as a toiletry kit. There is one outside pocket with mesh so you can put your toothbrush or razor in there while it's wet. The other outside pocket has three little elasticized mesh pockets inside to hold things like eye drops or travel contact solution, or little pill cases. Those are the only sub-organization features in the bag. They're nice just not enough for my stuff.

The bag has one closed loop handle that you can hang from a hook. Most of the hotel rooms I've been in recently have one or no hooks, so I learned from my mom to bring a rubber coated S hook with me on trips. They're for holding scarves or whatever on your closet rod. You can hang one from a shower or towel rod and keep your stuff off the tiny hotel room counter.

Anyway really nice bag, just needs more organization for me.

This is a nice Nautical gift set with 4 pretty polishes.  They are 13.5 ml each, and made in the U.S.A.  Initially I thought I would love Stay Nude the most, but it ended up being my least favorite of the set, only because it is pearl and streaks are unavoidable due to the type of finish it is.  All 4 have a shiny topcoat built into the formula.  The 3 cremes are all very sheer formulas, not super opaque.  The thickness of the formula for all of these is good.  If you like a sheer formula, where you can see your nail bed thru the polish, then these are your jam.  I did several manicures with each of them, and found that if I wanted a sheer look then 1 coat worked perfectly, otherwise 2 or 3 coats for full coverage and less peek thru of your natural nail and smile line.  I did 2 easy coats for each of my manicures.  The blue (Hypnosis) seemed to have the best coverage, and the formula for that was my favorite of the 4, it dried the fastest at 8 minutes to the touch.  They all go on easily, with a regular round brush (not flat) and they dry fairly well, in about 10-15 minutes each layer.  I did find that using my own quick drying topcoat that these wore much better, but from the manufacturer neither base nor top coat are required.  I did not get any staining from these, which I love.  The pink and white will both be really good polishes for doing either French tip or pond manicures when you just want a sheer base, where you do a layer, do art over it, then cover it again, and more art on that layer-it gives a layered effect that is fun to do.  The color palate is a fun one, with lots of options for artwork.  These are not quick drying-more of the typical 10 minutes per layer, and I expected them to be hardened on their own, without the help of a quick drying topcoat, but that was not the case with them.

I figured I would get a few more so that I don't have to worry about washing them as often, and was thrilled when I saw the price on this listing. The featured image shows the same microfiber fabric that my other Turbie Twists are made of. However, the items I received are plain old towel material, and not even nice towel material. I tried one and left it on my hair for 20 minutes, and water was literally dripping down the back of my neck. I just removed it and water is dripping from my hair onto my lap. These do not absorb anything. They also arrived rolled up in organza bags, without any official packaging or anything. Not sure if they are knock-offs, but if you have thick hair or are used to a Turbie Twist you bought in a store, you will be very disappointed by these. Will be requesting a refund.

This was my first time trying shampoo or conditioner in bar form, and I had the opportunity to try both from this company's line of products. My first impressions were very positive - the ingredients looked clean and natural, as well as being cruelty-free and vegan, I love that it’s plastic free (both the lack of bottle and the packaging), and that the scent options were relatively gender neutral. The bars were a little smaller than I expected, but ergonomically they fit comfortably in the palm of my hand and don't seem to be shrinking too fast after a week or so of use. I'm glad that they have different colors, so that I can differentiate between my bar soap, shampoo, and conditioner!

My experience using them was pretty good. It felt odd at first as I've only ever used bottled products, but quickly got used to it and could definitely see myself using more bars in the future. I tried both running the conditioner bar down my hair and lathering it up a little in my hand and applying that way. Between the two, I felt that I got pretty good coverage and results. My hair felt less tangled and I was able to work a brush through pretty easily once I got out the shower. When my hair dried, it seemed softer and healthier looking than it had previously, and my curls had a little more life to them.

I only have two concerns - the first is that I'm struggling to find a place to put the bars in my shower where they won't get misted by water and disintegrate more quickly that way. The second is the smell. Although it's not unpleasant, it reminded me a little of a scented candle, and was very strong. Three different people commented on the smell of my hair that week, which is not something that usually happens to me. My husband thought that I smelled like cologne! I could see this being a pro or a con depending on how you feel about fragrances. Personally, I found it overwhelming as I'm more on the sensitive side to smells.

Overall, I would consider trying this or a similar product again in the future, but only with a less intense scent.

In reading the comments I noticed that almost no one compared different shavers.
I have used a Norelco for years but I wanted something that was better and quicker to use on a two or three day beard. I have a Philips Norelco 4500. I bought the Wahl Smart Shave and the Braun 3040s.
After a two week trial I came up with the following observations.
On all three the blades float so they stay close to the face as you shave.
On the Norelco and the Wahl the head swivels too. It’s nice but I would not miss it if it were not there.
The Norelco is smoother and quieter than the other two. It is also the easiest to clean. It only takes one hand. Norelco recommends (and it is true) that saving in a circular motion works the best with their shaver.
The Norelco and the Wahl have Lithium batteries. The Braun has an NiMH battery. I like the Lithium.
I think the Wahl and the Braun shave closer than the Norelco but they are all close.
As for the trimmers, they all cut about the same. I would not buy a shaver without it. The Wahl is harder to manipulate. It has a nice metallic finish but that makes it hard to move up or down. It slips under your thumb.
The Wahl has the better battery and charge level indicator and a five year warranty. Wahl replacement head and blades are not on Amazon now. The Braun blades are easier to replace and the part is available on Amazon. Norelco blades are also easy to replace and available on Amazon.
I like all three shavers. For those with a light beard or with a medium beard and you shave every day I would recommend the Norelco. For those with a heavy or a three day beard I would recommend the Braun.
