review_text: I really want this on subscribe and save but Amazon only has a couple shades available. :( anyways a few years ago my skin became super sensitive and Almay consistently puts out products that don't bother my skin. This has pretty good coverage and you can build it up. I am rather happy with it. That is the only reason I am not giving it 3 stars. Here is my problem. I am colorblind and finding makeup that matches my skin by myself is a nightmare. For those of you who do not know colorblind is where we have a cone that is low in color which also affects other colors. We do not see in black and white. My green is low sometimes making certain greens look like a light version of goldenrod copy paper or as I say 1970's gold. Yuck... Anyways this affects how I view other colors and I cannot match makeup well. Certain shades will appear the same leading me to believe I have a match until someone (usually my cousin) points out my makeup looks ridiculous. Let me mention my cousins call me "educated" colorblind because most of the time I know how to compensate for color deficiency. I know color theory well. I wrote Almay about the problem because my only alternative was to drag my cousin to the store and have her "sample" shades. I am sure other customers and the store does not appreciate this so in the end I have tons of money wasted on the wrong shades. I know this happens to people with normal color vision but multiple that by 5-10 times you have done that and that describes my experience. Anyways I thought I'd write them and ask as Covergirl used to sell a 3 pack sampler of similar colors so you could find your perfect shade. The reply was to purchase full size products. I thought this lacked empathy as I wasn't writing to get free products. I was writing to find a resolution that would result in me being a long time customer. I don't think them going the extra mile to send something mini even if I had to pay was asking too much from such a large corporation. This leaves me felling like I should rate them 3 stars. While I remain a loyal customer they don't care about me. :( I wouldn't have minded paying for some sort of samples, but I guess they rather keep taking my money while I experienced trial and error finding a shade. Now while my cousins have not compared my makeup to mud since using this shade I haven't exactly had them inspect it closely for me after applied. I will ask to get a final opinion. The smart shade does not provide adequate coverage or I would go that route. I have that product also for lazy days. I rate the product a solid 4 stars for being a good product especially on super sensitive skin, but I rate the company 0 stars for not even considering people like me. They got my money so I guess they're happy. Still let wondering if this is the right shade for me.. *sigh* still holding on to the heap of bottles because I paid good money for it. review_text: I was skeptical about this product but I was happily surprised.  I have used this product three times to remove gel polish (I do my own nails).  I find it to be much easier than soaking the polish off with acetone, especially since that method only allows me to do one hand at a time.  With this product I have to file down the top coat, I make sure there are no shiny spots of the top coat remaining, then I apply a thick layer of this polish to my nails.  I found that it takes around 5 to 7 minutes to get the full effect.  I do have to gently scrape the polish off my nails but it comes off fairly easily.  I do have polish remaining on my nails after the scraping so I apply a second coat and allow it to set for 5 minutes.  After the second coat I am able to scrape the remaining polish off my nails.  There are some areas where I may have to scrape a little harder than gentle pressure; however, I do not feel this is damaging to my nails.  I would recommend this product because it is an easier way to remove gel polish but it by no means comes off as easily as it does in the video.

Before giving a review on a polish it should be tested on your fingers and toes.
Just because a Polish doesn’t stay on the fingernails well does mean it isn’t good. Try it on your toes too.
Did it chip and peel off of them the same way as your fingernails?
Then it isn’t the polish...it is either the application, nail or the way you use your hands.

This mask is unlike any other I've used. Unopened, it sounds like a heavy liquid when the container is shaken; I'm used to masks that are "solid" and extremely thick, but was looking for an exfoliating mask because my skin gets very dry and flaky in winter. Got this one because I was offered a discount in exchange for an honest review. Used it last night for the first time...

It should probably be well-shaken before each use, and it looks very strange. Kind of a greenish-grey pearlescence, and it is a "runny" mask. A little goes a long way, too! I was surprised. There must be at *least* 20 treatments in this little jar. Required less than two teaspoons to do my entire face and under the jawline.

It feels strange. Kind of an icy-hot sting in the beginning; interesting, but not uncomfortable. It doesn't feel as though it would do a lot of exfoliating, and it doesn't dry quickly (maybe it's not supposed to dry, at all). The instructions said to leave it on for 20 minutes, but I left it on for an hour. At that point, it was flaky. Rather than simply rinse it off, I rubbed it off with my fingers, and THAT was definitely exfoliating. This wouldn't work with any of the other masks I've used, and I really liked being able to easily/gently rub every bit off using my fingers. Post-rub, my face felt very dry, but after rinsing with warm water that feeling went away and my skin was SO soft.

Today when I awoke, my skin felt great. No dry patches. I did still apply my usual three or four drops of cold argan oil, just because the humidity is so low right now.

As-is, I like this mask much more than I thought I would when I first opened the jar (though it smells wonderful, again, it's very "liquid," which seemed strange before I'd actually used it). That said, I'll probably alternate between using it straight out of the jar and adding some bentonite to make it a bit thicker. Very happy to have this organic mask!

I've had this trimmer for probably 6+ years and it is still going strong. Just a hint if you have one and are looking to replace the G380 due to battery loss give this a try once a year:
Run until the battery discharges fully. By this I mean when the battery is getting weak I take the attachments off and turn on the power switch. Leave the switch on until the gizmos stop rotating then turn off. Wait about 20 minutes or so and then power on to deplete the rest of the battery (you can try this a few times to make sure it is fully drained). After discharging, plug it into the charger and let fully charge (I think I let mine charge overnight). This unit is now back to original power, and I haven't had to recharge in over 3 weeks of normal use and it functions like new). Just a tip to save you some money before deciding to buy another unit which I almost did. I could not find a replacement battery when I thought the battery was the issue.

I purchased an sleep mask just like this in a store and, when it went missing, searched for it high and low until I found it here on Amazon. The mask blocks light well with little or no light leaking in around your nose and none around the eyes. The contoured eye coverings place no pressure on your eyelids. I never felt comfortable sleeping in a traditional sleep mask until I used this style. I can even open my eyes in my mask and my lashes don't even brush it.

The comfort in wearing meant I quickly adjusted to its use and now can't hardly sleep without it. As someone who has had trouble sleeping and finds napping almost impossible, having the routine of perfect dark when I sleep at night has allowed me to build a trigger. Now, when I need to sleep early, want to catch a nap, find myself in a plane, or other times I might ordinarily find it hard to sleep, I can place my mask on and it signals sleep perfectly. It's improved my sleep length and frequency, as well as reduced the time it takes me to fall asleep, which I think anyone could appreciate.

My only gripe is that, while I thought this one was exactly like my previous mask, there's a little difference. There's a little plastic piece on the side of the elastic that joins loops for the adjustment system and they sit very near my ears. I can sometimes feel it digging in and I never remember feeling that on my previous mask. For occasional use, you may not notice it, but using them nightly, the little part can bother me sometimes. My solution plan involves breaking the part and replacing it with something soft or hand-sewing that connection point. Customization is a very small price to pay for the amazingly comfortable contoured foam that makes up the main body of the mask.

review_text:
Overall, I liked this sheet mask but I would not buy it again because it was so heavily fragranced that I couldn’t bear it for more than 5 minutes. This mask is the first mask I’ve seen which contains kaolin clay. You leave the mask on like any other sheet mask, but after you take off the mask, you can see a thin layer of gray clay on your face. You have to rinse that off. After I rinsed off the mask and applied my usual Cerave cream moisturizing cream, I felt that my skin looked noticeably brighter.

These masks are expensive. They cost $6.00 each (a pack of 5 costs $30.00 on Amazon). Although the two-piece mask fit my face, did not slide off, and is the only sheet mask I know which incorporates kaolin, I found the floral, perfume fragrance overwhelming. A sheet mask should be enjoyable and not make you want to hold your breath.

Instead of buying this mask again, I want to try clay/kaolin/bentonite masks and continue to use masks with some of the same ingredients as this mask (e.g., niacinamide (brightens skin but can be irritating for some people), allantoin (soothing), centella asiatica extract (soothing), and dipotassium glycyrrhizate (potential brightening effect)).

ALTERNATIVE CLAY MASK: I highly recommend the ISNTREE Real Mugwort Clay Mask* ($23.60 for 3.38 fl oz). There is a strong earthy, herbal scent when you apply the mask, but it disappears quickly. I noticed decreased redness using this mask. It has been more effective than any sheet mask I have tried.

ALTERNATIVE SHEET MASKS: To brighten skin, try Keana Nadeshiko Rice Mask 10 Pieces Japan** (10 sheets for $9.50). The fragrance free masks contain glycerin (moisturizing), rice ferment filtrate (sake) and rice bran for a skin brightening effect.

Update: I made a rookie mistake and accidentally left my flat iron on all day while I was at work. I came home and my house was still standing. There were no burning smells, my mat was perfectly fine, and just the sides of my flat iron were a little brown from all the heat. I'm glad I have this mat.

I've been resting my flat iron on random surfaces every morning and slowly melting them, so I finally decided to be responsible and get a mat. I wanted something simple, and this one could also be rolled up around a heat tool to stuff in a suitcase, so I chose this one.

I've put this on the corner of my vanity, and it works great. I can put a flat iron and a clampless curling wand on top, and nothing burns and nothing smells. I also sometimes put hot pots on top and use it as a pot holder. It's a perfect small, compact size.

It has raised bumps that lift the heating tool off the surface to give a little ventilation for all the heat. The silicone material grips the vanity surface, so it won't ever slide off.

I think the only possible con is that since it's a black rubbery surface, it picks up lots of dust and dirt. Since it's on my vanity, if I get any makeup powder or dry shampoo on my hands, it gets on the mat. This is easily remedied with a quick rinse with water, but it seems to get dirty all the time, and it could get a little annoying.

review_title: Another good sponge from Real Techniques (I like their others equally well.)
review_text:
I like this, but I don't love it. It works well, but I don't think it really stands out as a revolutionary shape or as a favorite among my sponge collection.

The feature of this sponge that I like best and used the most is the pointed tip (which has more point that is currently pictured). The point is excellent at getting into little creviced on the face.

The other sides a re a little gimmicky but usable (although I never use the smaller rectangular facets for anything!). Overall I think I prefer using their brushes with rounded sides, and I think their shape feels more natural in the hand as well. Still, I have no complaints about this one, and I really like the texture of it. The pleasant point to this one probably renders this a tie. Basically, I think you need a Real Techniques Face Sponge, but I don't think it matters which one; since the other is cheaper, I would probably go with it.

It is a very soft sponge, pleasant feeling on the skin, and it seems made from quality material. It washes clean and dries well.

I really like this palette, but feel it should be noted that it is NOT as expected. Very nice colors, but more subdued than bold, more satin/shimmer than metallic. This is my first Ulta palette and I am happy with the quality. I only deducted one star because the colors are somewhat other than expected. I paid $12.

I specifically bought it for the green color, and I still like the green color, but it's not as bright or as metallic as the collection name caused me to expect. The finish is something of a shimmering satin, not metallic. The colors are somewhat subdued. The package says "jewel tones" which may be more accurate than the "metals" description, but still (to me) implies more brightly colored shades, with fewer earth tones. I would also expect a "jewel toned" palette to include a strong purple, and this only has the lilac (Dynasty). (The Royal looks purple but swatched brown with a hint of burgundy.) The colors are more woodsy than jeweled. The green is more mossy than emerald, the purple more floral than jeweled, the blue more night sky than sapphire.

The quality of the shadows is good. Neither buttery nor powdery, it's a slightly dry formula that nevertheless doesn't kick up a lot of product or cause a lot of fall out. I wear them over a primer, but I have been happy with their wear time. As stated above, pigmentation is good in that you don't have to build heavily, but it's also not a bright coloring.

A lovely bonus is that I actually love the brush that comes with this item! How often do you say that about a brush in a palette? It's not only soft and usable, it's unique among my brush collection. It's flufflier and less flat that most brushes of it's size, and it's also smaller and more pinpointed that most brushes that have a bit of fluffiness to them. Overall, I feel like it gives good control while still blending well. It's quickly become a favorite brush.

There may have been a naming crisis when creating this palette, lol. As the palette name is Metals, the subtitle is Jewels, and every individual shade is named with a royalty/gentry theme. The shares are: Noble (white), Lady (pale pink), Reign (earthy pink), Crown (gold), Dynasty (lilac), Royal (brown), Honor (platinum), Jester (silver), Armor (bronze), Fortress (green), Duchess (navy), and Duke (off black). No mattes, all satin/shimmer. All smooth, no fall out, some apply more evenly than others (drier formula). Swatched dry on dry skin in photo. Will build to brighter, more shiny finish.

I ordered this palette on a whim, and I've enjoyed it. However, if you are wanted super metallic finishes or bright colors, you should manage your expectations.

review_title: Great and functional, but similar to very strong liquid latex
review_text:
Pros:
- fine tipped brush makes it easy to apply
- a fine wing tip is easy to draw, once the product dries and hardens on the brush a bit
- waterproof, smudgeproof, an accidental rub won't ruin it. a hydrogen bomb probably won't remove it.

Cons:
- reminds me of strong liquid latex; sticks to itself and pulls off in pieces. it's difficult to remove without a lot of soap and makeup remover. it gets caught in my eyelashes and hurts like hell trying to pull it out. rubbing it off has been the most effective method of removal after using makeup remover, but then the hardened substance gets in my eyes.
- because it's similar to liquid latex, it makes me (possibly irrationally) believe my skin can't breathe well underneath it.
- dries hard (latexy) in the tube
- if it remotely gets on your eyelashes (which it will), you can forget about using mascara. (see photo)

Other notes:
- it is glossy. I prefer matte, but this is subjective. (see photo. this was taken ~4 hours after application. dried and settled by then.)
- the handle is a little farther from the drawing tip than I'd prefer for finer control
- it took all the king's horses and all the king's men to unscrew the tube for the first time

I'd purchase this product again, if I can't find a comparable non-latex-like product.

review_text: After years and tens of thrown out pillows, finally found this. This has been used by someone who takes hot baths every night. The usual vinyl suction cups On pillows normally start failing within weeks as vinyl hardens in heat and soon stop providing suction. This had been true no matter the cost of the pillow. The suction cups, which is  molded as part of the pillow (not just attached onto the pillow), truly provide incredible suction. Bath oil usually sticks onto other pillows’ woven fabrics and even under the suction cups. But being that here, the suction is so strong, the oils won’t sneak underneath the cups. Even the surface of this pillow does not allow oils and soap scum to stick onto it. (would have loved to see a larger version of this such as one size of a clawfoot tub back). This pillow allows one to open the back up (for cleaning?). It was inspected after 3 straight months of daily usage with oils, etc...not a single grain of scum and oil stuck inside. I've been using Bare Escentuals "Bare Minerals" mineral makeup since about 2002. I've tried other brands but till now I just didn't find anything I liked as much, let alone better. Lately though the BE makeup just hasn't been agreeing with my skin. I'm getting older and my skin is a bit more sensitive these days apparently. The one thing I never cared for with the BE makeup was their use of bismuth. Anything with bismuth it just makes my skin itch. I've been reading about the negatives of parabens too, and I decided I wanted to get away from that as much as I could.

BE doesn't have that but it does use bismuth, at least they did as of the last time I ordered a big kit. After perusing Amazon and reading ingredient lists I chose to try this kit. Mainly because of the fact that this makeup doesn't have any of that and reviews here already are mostly positive. Also because I liked the eye shadow colors in the trial kit. These are colors I'd use a lot so I didn't feel like I was wasting money on colors I'd never use just to get trials on everything else. The jars are about the size of a BE eyeshadow, a little smaller maybe. The brushes weren't bad but they are small. I put them in my purse kit. They're useful for that, but not for much else. But they're sturdy. They're not losing bristles and they seem fairly soft.

For the most part I like this makeup. It's about the same grind as the BE mineral makeup, feels a bit silkier to me actually. It smells about the same seems maybe a bit less noticeable, the smell. It blends as well, but doesn't feel quite as heavy. The finishing veil is good. I have combination skin and oil in my t-zone and it did a good job of keeping me matte all day. The foundation covers well and doesn't make my face itch at all. The bisque is okay but I don't think it's got quite the coverage of the BE bisque. I did have to use more of it to cover things the same way. I kind of wish this kit had come with sample jars of the colored concealers as I would have liked to have tried those combined with their bisque. I think it might have worked better with that combo. I'm admittedly at a point where a simple bisque concealer is probably not enough for me. I'm getting dark under eye areas and have some red I need to cover now and again.

Their "glow" mixed with the pink blush is my new blush. It's too much for me as a bronzer. I have very pale ivory skin and it just does not work for me all over. Just a little too much orange, a little too dark but it did work okay as blusher over the pink they send you. Combining both that gave me a blusher that worked well for me. The pink blush they give you is just way too light and frosted for me. It just doesn't show up at all. It was the one product in the kit I just did not care much for. I would definitely want a darker more mauve or cinnamon toned blush rather than this one. The pink on it's own is pretty useless. I had to combine the two or forget it. It didn't even look like I had any color on my cheeks.

The foundation colors are decent. Their Fair #1 is actually a near perfect match for me but I'd probably never use the Fair #2 unless it was combined with the Fair #1 maybe. My skin is never that dark, not even in Summer. But Fair #1 I must admit I like that one. It's hard for me to find a foundation that's fair enough that's not too yellow, but Fair #1 works well. Fair #2 is just a tad too dark and just a bit yellow for me.

Overall I'd have to say this kit was a positive experience except for a couple of colors being slightly off for me. I do plan on ordering a big kit but I'm also going to email them and ask if they might send a slightly darker blush and just the Fair #1 x2 instead since they're supposedly picking the cosmetics as they pack for you. Can't hurt to ask, and if they do then their "Fair" kit will work very well for me and I can see myself becoming a regular with this one. I did not expect this product to be as good as it is actually. It was a very pleasant surprise. I'm used to spending a lot more on the BE product. This is much less expensive and in some ways I think I actually like it better than BE so I probably won't be a BE customer much now that I've discovered this.

By comparison, when I used [[ASIN:B002KO903M Manic Panic Hot Hot Pink Hair Dye #13 4 fl. oz]], I constantly needed to use dry shampoo and apply touch-ups.

Also, if you blow-dry your hair after dying it, you'll need to be careful to get any errant hairs off your counters, walls, etc., or else your wet hair will stick to the surface, the dye will seep in, and you'll need to use bleach to wipe everything down. review_title: Believe The Waring Reviews and Not The Description
review_text:
Having mixed feelings, I fought with writing this review being that I'm a beauty industry pro and I usually purchase wholesale from an overseas vendor. Just for clarification there is a Loose Wave and a Deep Loose Wave. I have woren borh.
So after unpacking , the loose wave bundles were beautiful until I took it out of the net.... the curl dropped.. What was even more disappointing was the tangling/manageability and how dead/dry the ends were. Testing, by lightly -medium spraying with water and letting dry,I was able to see how much wave /curl was left.... No curl and was puffy/bushy very little to no wave . Usually with loose wave you can wash and go. Not the case here. I also noticed that some bundles lighten faster than the others. During the lightening process there was a toxic chemical smell, yellow residue and I noticed the hair was REALLY hot to the touch and there was a sizzling sound that made me extremely alarmed .. I immediately rinsed in luke warm water. Was afraid to process again so that I could get the potential color want not knowing if the hair was going burn due to how hot the hair was during the first process. Good thing it's for myself and not a paying client so Im fine with the color that I have. There isn't any unusual shedding even after the lightening process BUT it's still early!
To sum things up... I do not recommend using this company. Trust and integrity means a great deal in the business word. As a consumer on Amazon did read the vendors return policy before placing my order AND ALL of the hair vendors have the same policy BUT what I can't understand is how was I supposed to know the hair wasn't as the vendors description and have the problems that occurred without disturbing the bundles? I would have to give a refund if this was for paying client!! The vendor return policy implies they hold no responsibility for misrepresentation in the description so if once you've disturbed the hair... that's it! Classic case of "Take your money and run OR "Next". SMH!!!

review_title: Original Gillette M3 Power Razor better than new black handled one
review_text:
I first purchased the Gillette M3 Power Razor in 2004 when they were first released. I was just not happy with the Gilette I was using. It was exactly what I was looking for. Wet the face, lather with a small amount of shaving cream, turn on the razor and what a surprise, easier smoother shave. I was pleased. That razor lasted until November 2009 when the green off/on switch popped out and washed down the drain. I stopped at the drug store that night and found the new (improved ???) black handled M3 Razor. The next morning I used it, seemed ok but something was missing that I could not hang a wisker on. In January, it refused to turn on when I tried to use it. I started to replace the battery and noticed that the plastic support that holds the battery in place was crumbling. That is when I started an internet search for the original M3. I found it on amazon decided to order two just to play it safe. at the same time, I read a single review that stated that the razor made the persons neck break out. Started me thinking, I wondered how many newly wiskered youngsters tried shaving without a clue as to what they were doing; after all, there are no instructions on how to shave!!

An aside, Gillette has a new super M3 like razor with a 5th blade, costing a lot more money. I thought about it but ordered the Original M3 Power razor anyway. I highly recommend this to anyone who wants a clean shave without breaking the bank over blade replacement. Battery lasts a good three or more months, blades a dozen shaves, depending on beard thickness. Just remember to use water and shave cream or soap, good lather and go for it. For us oldsters, we already know how to shave and know a good Razor when we see it. Gillette, your new improved black handled M3 replacement just does not cut it. I have 5 stars for the Oldie but Goodie!

We picked this up to use on dogs and cats. Most of them are short-haired, but one of the cats is a bit fluffy. They're all happy with the brush (one cat and one dog get freaked out with certain brushes and I'm not sure why).

I LOVE Coconut oil and use it for lotion and hair all the time. The nice thing about this product is that it's liquid and has different options on how you want to store it. The normal lid (after taking out the little stopper) is nice, but the pump is what I was excited for. I can use this on my massage clients, my dry ankles, or my over damaged hair quicker. Just a few simple pumps and I have more than enough.

Coconut oil is amazing at hydrating your skin, my favorite use is for my inner thighs so they don't chaff. Coconut oil stays smooth and oily for a long while, so be prepared! Even if it stays oily, it doesn't feel heavy, I don't even notice it most of the time. That's why it's my favorite oil to use when I give massages. Not as many of my clients have coconut allergies and they tend to enjoy the smell of coconuts. Some say it makes them feel like they are on a tropical vacation. You don't have to wipe it off either, your body sucks up that moisture and it makes your skin super soft! My leg has these scabs that won't heal and dry patches from when I had to wear a leg brace and this has helped the healing process more than I could have expected.

You don't have to trim down the pump tubing which was a huge relief because I always screw it up somehow. If that ever goes bad for some reason, the nice thing is you could switch back to the other lid. Usually when I buy coconut oil, it's hard and has to melt a bit, so I was thrown off that this stays liquid. Makes it easier when I'm using in my hair.

I love all of the amazing things coconut oil can do for the body and I would really recommend giving this a try.

review_title: Salty, Sweet Brown Sugar and Pistachio Cookies
review_text:
B&BW had all of their body sprays on sale for $5 last Sunday, so I stopped in and picked up the new Magic in the Air (very nice), a back up of A Thousand Wishes (surprisingly very nice), and Golden Pear and Brown Sugar. This review is for the last.

Top Notes: Italian Bergamot, Decadent Pistachio Mousse, Sugared Almond Cookie.

Heart Notes: Caramelised Praline, Toasted Hazelnuts, Plum Blossum.

Base Notes: Silken Vanilla, Glazed Chocolate Wood, Whipped Musk.

As you can see by the listed notes, this is a sweet gourmand fragrance intended for the Autumn/Winter seasons. It is festive and has a bake shop vibe. In the top and heart notes I am able to detect the pistachio, almond cookie, and hazelnuts, but I do not detect either the bergamot or the plum blossom. As with most B&BW fragrances, this one dries down to the base notes within 15-20 minutes. In the base, I mainly detect vanilla and chocolate. I do not pick up on a musk note which is fine by me because musk is not one of my favourite notes.

All in all, this is a well blended, sweet, sugar cookie type of fragrance that is warm and comforting. If you like gourmand scents, especially those with a few or more of these notes, then I think you would like this fragrance. It is probably too sweet and cloying for warm weather, but on cold, windy, wet Autumn/Winter days this fragrance can be the perfect compliment to a cozy sweater in front of a warm fireplace. Smells good enough to eat! The one thing I do not understand is why they named it "Golden Pear" and Brown Sugar. The notes combined definitely give a brown sugar smell, but I do not detect any pear smell.

Recommended for those who like (or think they might like) sweet, gourmand fragrances.

I've seen these steamer machines that are used to remove gel nail polish and while I've always wanted to try them, I was very skeptical and unwilling to spend the money on a gadget that may or may not work. But, removing the gel polish is the worst part or the thing I hate about gel polish: it's time consuming and so hard on the nail bed. I've seen mixed reviews online about gel polish steamers but I finally decided to try one.
This gel polish remover machine actually works. It was easy to put together and I was able to completely remove my gel polish in under 20 minutes. First and most important is to file the top layer of gel down first with a nail file before using this device. I was not able to get the gel polish offf without filing the surface first. I put about two capfuls of 100% acetone (you can use less) into the little tray and turned the machine on. Once it beeps, you can stick your fingers inside. It gets a little hot but it's not painful. After five minutes the machine will beep and I am able to scrape off most of the gel polish. I have to do a second round to get certain areas that just won't scrape off. And when I say scrape off, I mean easily scrape off not scraping and hurting the surface of the nail. I guess I should say push off the gel polish to remove it. I leave the remaining acetone in the tray and either reuse it or dump it. I would say this is easier than using aluminum foil or plastic nail caps because you do the whole hand at once. With foil or plastic caps, I never get my whole hand done at once. This was easier and I didn't use any cotton balls and I used less acetone.

The device is a little pricey. It's basically a warming plate fitted inside a contained area with holes to place your fingers. It's worth the money to me because I hate the process of gel removal. I like that the company provides four replacement plastic pieces for the nail holes. It took me a while to figure out what the replacement pieces were for but after reading one of the reviews I now realize what it's used for. There is also a second plastic tray to put the nail polish remover or acetone in. My only criticism is that I wish the device was smaller as I have a lot of nail stuff and this will just add to it all. It's not the fanciest looking device but it does the job.

review_title: Will not work with Optical Signals from Some TV brands
review_text:
The original TVlink I did not have a optical input, so they added a crippled one to the Tvlink II. The issue is that virtually all modern TV sets output audio thru a optical connector and are set to Dolby Digital 5.1 by default. The Tvlink II will not respond to a optical signal with Dolby Digital. Why?? The Resound Reunite works fine with a Dolby Digital optical signal.

So, if your TV allows it, you can go into setup and muck around to change the audio decoding to PCM in order to make the TV link II work. Unfortunately, many Panasonic and LG TV sets will not allow you to change to force PCM output, so you need to buy a separate decoder. A high quality decoder is expensive, the cheap ones delay the signal.

So, my Tvlink II works with my Samsung TV once I changed the audio format, but not my Panasonic.

review_title: The Messiest and Most Effective Handcream I've Found
review_text:
I wash my hands often, especially since Covid 19 appeared on the scene, and this dries out my skin and causes the fingertips to develop cracks that are as painful as paper cuts. I have tried every kind of hand cream I could find to remedy the situation, from those purporting to prevent such cracks to those advertised as ultra-dry skin salves to petroleum jelly. Nothing works. Then I decided to give Dr. Naylor's a try and bingo! I've used it for about 2 weeks, and everything has healed. Even my hand doctor--this is the absolute truth--noticed the difference! So I love Dr. Naylor's Udder Balm and am a convert for life.

However, the reason I didn't assign 5 stars to this product is that it's the messiest stuff I've ever used. It's like an ointment, but it comes in a can, and the can arrived leaking the stuff, even though the can was sealed. It's both sticky and gloppy. You need only a little bit to put on your hands (or feet) in order to get full coverage, so I imagine that the tin I bought will take years to use up. I have actually set it inside a small cardboard box to absorb the mess that exudes from the can. If you can accept this fact about the product, you will appreciate its benefits. If not, Bag Balm is less messy (but I can't stand the smell). The scent of Dr. Naylor's is, unlike Bag Balm, not heavily camphorated and not overly medicinal. The smell also evaporates as soon as the cream is absorbed.

review_title: The Negative Reviews Don't Do This Shaver Justice ⚖
review_text: I will start out by saying that I did not purchase my Wahl Smart Shaver from Amazon since I found it cheaper elsewhere.  With that being said, I'd like to comment based on my usage of this shaver thus far. First of all, I just recently used a Braun 9 series shaver. Unfortunately, this shaver does not have a cleaning/charging station but I'm not convinced that is a deal breaker. I am also puzzeld by some of the negative reviews here. I literally turned on both shavers, and in my honest opinion, the Wahl was slightly quieter. The Wahl does have some similarities to a Remington shaver. For example, the two inner blades resemble the Remington as does the sound of the shaver. The outter foil seems to be very unique to the Wahl brand. So in using the Wahl Smart Shaver, I found it to be very effective on 2+ days of beard growth as it went through the facial hair with ease. The shaver head is thinner which in my opinion allowed me to get closer than both Braun and Remington shavers. The hypoallergenic foils that have symmetrical and asymmetrical foil slots provided me with an exceptionally close and clean shave. Almost 12 hours after my initial shave, and I barely felt any stubble growth. To me that speaks volumes about this shaver. I was very skeptical about trying this shaver based on the prior reviews here and the fact that the Wahl shaver was cheaper than the leading brands (e.g., Braun, Panasonic, Remington, etc..). However, for now I'm glad I took a chance and decided to give the Wahl Smart Shaver a chance. Also, if you view other sites, this shaver ranks significantly higher than it does amongst Amazon shoppers. Not sure why this is but something doesn't make sense to me. So if you want a clean shave and also don't want to go into debt buying a shaver, I suggest giving this shaver a try. By the way I'm retired military and this would've been nice to use while I was active duty. Lastly, if you're still not convinced, please take into account that Wahl guarantees this shaver for five (5) years. Take a chance. You'll be glad you did!

review_title: Great If You Want A Slime Factory - But There's a Cure
review_text:
Despite rinsing and wiping the exterior of this unit after each use, a pool of slime soon forms in the charging base. It's even worse inside the top of the handle, visible when the brushing element is unscrewed. If you want to avoid a disgusting mess, you really need to disassemble this unit every day for a thorough cleaning. That's a lot to ask for a tool that is supposed to make our lives easier. I used a previous Sonicare model for years without ever encountering this issue. My wife's toothbrush is identical to mine, and it has exactly the same problem, so there's pretty obviously a serious design flaw with this model.

A CHEAP FIX: The problem is that the gaskets in the brush head don't seal out liquids. One possible solution is a product called "Sonic Seal" [[ASIN:B001S2PLNK The Sonic Seal for E-Series Sonicare Replacement Heads (3 Pack of Blue, Pink, Frost)]] available on Amazon -- currently 3 for $16.95. Pretty expensive for what's essentially a toothbrush condom, so I tried making my own in three easy steps. (1) Take a latex glove and cut off one of the fingers. (2) Cut off a very tiny section at the end of the detached fingertip (the resulting small hole will stretch temporarily in the next step). (3) Slip the glove finger down over the brush head, leaving the tip end above the top gasket of the brush head, and pulling the rest of the latex down to where the brush head joins the handle. Voila, no more slime build-up. (Keep the glove on hand in case you have to make more protectors later on.)

This Norelco (actually made by Philips) one was bought to replace an older shaver (I've used Norelco, Philips and Panasonics over the years.) This one is more efficient (faster, better shave) than my older one, and an amazingly amount quieter. What do you know- this time, "new and improved" really is accurate!
What I like: the shaver fits the hand well, the pivoting blade heads fit the face and as a result shave quite well. The battery strength indicator, consisting of bright LEDs showing the percentage of charge remaining in 20% increments, is very useful, and the flip-up hinged shaver head section is easy to clean with warm water (I still have to consciously force myself to do this!) They have also "shrunk" the half-egg shaped power transformer, and you can use 100 - 220 volts to plug / charge, a good thing for someone who travels globally as I do.
What I don't like: the pop-up trimmer is only fair - it works, but it's actually not as effective as the one on my old shaver! The deep well holding the head rotors shafts is not so easy to clean with a brush, particularly with the hinged head; they are still using a non-user replaceable NiCd battery; the gimmicky cutter head plate section with holes seems merely that - gimmicky, not useful for any real shaving.
Tips: After cleaning the head / blade assemblies, allow them to dry fully and spray-lubricate with something like "Shaver Saver." When power seems low, turn the shaver on and allow to discharge fully before reccharging - these are, after all, still NiCd batteries with the "memory" effect. These tips have allowed my previous electrics' battery - and cutter head assemblies - to last a long time (I have a heavy beard - even with a blade shaver, I have to shave again in the afternoon if I have a dinner appointment.)
Recommendation: This is a very good, easy to use, quick and quiet electric shaver - the best I have ever used. review_title: Two sizes, I'm good with that :o)
review_text: Brian doesn't care about dual forms, but I do! Hi! I'm Drea, Brian's wife and I purchased these forms. :o) First let me be very clear here: THEY ARE NOT REGULAR NAIL TIPS! These are forms that give 2 uses hence the word DUAL (which means 2) These forms are for use with a product called POLYGEL. Polygel is a perfect mix of acrylic and gel products. The beauty of this marriage is that the polygel is cured in an UV/LED light. The function of the dual form, is to hold the amount of polygel you need to achieve a completely covered nail in one go. You fill the dual form with polygel, use 91% alcohol as a slip solution and pat, pat, pat that polygel until it is where you want it. You then turn the filled form over and apply from the cuticle to the nail's free edge. You do clean up with the alcohol around the form's edges because there will be gel coming out of the sides, and then cure under the UV/LED lamp for 30 to 60 seconds WITH THE DUAL FORM STILL ON. This 100 pcs set is perfect for achieving the above goal. What I can say about them is that I got two sizes and that is fine with me. I am grateful for the two sizes as I have narrow shaped nails and a slender nail bed. I can only review the sizes right now as I am waiting for my polygel order. Once I receive that order then I can review the form properly. I can also say that it is awesome that they come with the length box that allows you to see how far you are "moving" the polygel up in the form. I know they will work for me.

This stuff is amazing. I don't know what they put in my hair at the salon, but even with only washing my hair in cold, and not every day, it still was fading almost immediately. I mixed just a little of this half and half with conditioner and left it on the pink part of my hair for half an hour, and it boosted the color right up! At first I did that every other week, but right now it's been a good 2 and a half months (and I gave up on cold washes a month ago - I visited Peru where it is winter, and wanted the hot showers!), and while the ends have faded a bit, most of my hair is still vibrant hot pink. I think when I get my roots done I'll just have them bleach it and put this on myself, since it seems to work and stay far better than what they used.
Also, there's plenty in this bottle! I only have about a third of my hair pink, but it's long and thick, and I've still only used less than a quarter of a bottle after 3-4 uses. It doesn't need to be full strength to work, in my experience, so I expect this bottle will last a good long time.
As with all fun color dyes, this will stain everything! Be careful, wear gloves, put vaseline around your hairline, put a shower cap or something on while you're letting it set, or you'll have pink where you don't want it!

Edit - it's now been over 10 months since I last touched up the color, and 10 months since I gave up taking special care of it. That's nine months of HOT showers, and not doing anything special, just plain shampoo and conditioner as I would usually do. There were parts at the ends that were lighter bright pink with hints of peachiness, but the majority was still a very bright hot pink! Not as dark as freshly dyed, but still very bright and vibrant. I had a ton of roots obviously, but the color was still fantastic. Last night I bleached my roots and re-dyed, and now my hair is even more super vibrant bright pink. I'm very pleased. I've finally got to the bottom of the bottle, so I'm re-ordering. Atomic Pink is my color. (Also, highly recommend Manic Panic's Dye Away wipes. They do a great job getting the stray dye spots off your ears and arms, and help a bit with surfaces too.)

review_text:

I'm in my early 30s and just now getting more serious about anti aging skincare because I'm trying to avoid fillers for as long as I can.
This moisturizer is extremely rich and I only need to use a tiny fingertip size for my neck and face. It works great under makeup and doesn't feel greasy or heavy.
As far as the price tag goes, it's a lot...I personally don't think I could afford to purchase on a regular basis and really wish that it was more affordable because I feel like a lot of people would benefit from this cream.

review_text:

The packaging is beautiful and looks gorgeous on my countertop. I do however have some trouble with the dispenser pump because it gets finicky and will only pump out product from one side. The component is made of plastic which is why I'm not giving it five stars. For the price you would expect glass or some sort of refill that was more eco friendly.
For those that have arthritis, the pump can be tricky to use because you have to press down fairly hard. Hopefully this is fixed in the future because it's a lovely product.

I personally love the extra long handle so I don't apply too much pressure when rolling away. I do use it "upside down" and pull rather than push which I'm not sure if you're supposed to do but it feels a lot better that way.
This tool should last a lifetime if cared for properly so the price doesn't bother me as an investment piece.

review_text:

The scent is to die for with a musky woodsy kind of scent with very light floral undertones. Would absolutely recommend for a holiday gift!

I got this to help organize make up on top of our dressers and it does a fine job of that.

Quality: The organizer is made of plastic with rubber on top and the mirror comes apart from the set and then is used to clover the middle sections. The mirror is not on a hinge and only just slides into a slot when you want to use it, I would have liked for it to attach more securely or to be on a hinge instead.

How does it work? It allows you to push lipsticks and other cosmetics into rubber X shaped holes that hold the make up in place standing up. On the other side you can lay make up across divided rubber slots and in the middle there are bigger sections to hold a compact or other make up. It works well, the mirror comes off the organizer and slides into a slot to stand up and be used.

Overall, this is a compact and nice organizer for the top of any dresser or table. The only con is the mirror could have been built in a better way to attach it to the organizer more securely.

Quality: This is made of a stretchy material that is of high quality. The bristles on one side are very well made, they do not break off or wear down easily. The product should last you a long time and is easy to wash off after using.

review_text:
If you think about it, combining a straightener and a hair brush makes perfect sense, but how long have so many of us been using a separate hair straightener followed by vigorous, frantic brushing with a hairbrush? I usually have to wait for other straighteners to reheat after each use or after I put it down, but that wasn't the case with this straightener.

I also really appreciate how quickly the brush cooled down after I finished, so I can easily store it back in the fabric bag that came with the brush. I also love the hair clips they provided (the exact same as those used at my hair salon) so that I could hold up my top layers of hair while I straightened the hair at the bottom of my crown. Like everything else with this straightener, the combs were so well thought out that they fit into the bag with the straightener, so I could easily store the entire setup in a drawer, rather than cluttering my countertop. I wholeheartedly recommend this straightener as a first time addition to your hair care regimen or as a replacement for your old straightener and brush!

Unlike the typical beauty blenders which are completely teardrop shaped, this set has a sharp edge cut out on various surfaces. It's like being in precalculus all over again. I didn't know why those corners were so useful until I realised that I can use it to tuck makeup into hard to reach spots, or to draw down sharp corners. Imagine you just finished blending out a good smoky eye. You've got a couple of colours in that eyelid. A clunky beauty blender won't get in there and blend out that liquid eyeliner quite as nicely as one that has a sharper corner to it. Same goes for applying contour. You don't want to go in there with an eye pencil or something, and slash this harsh line over your face. Instead, having that good sharp edge lets you get product on the spots you want it and not where you don't (like when you're contouring down your nose). The quality of the sponges is excellent, and you'll find yourself reaching for a different one for each job.

This is that beauty blender that you see all the youtube makeup artists using on their face when they're all "OK, let's bounce it out now" and speed up the video. Get it wet, wring out the excess moisture, and bounce. I found that the sponge is not as easy to keep clean as my brushes are. When I'm done applying makeup, I'll give any of the brushes I've used a hit with either the brush cleaning spray, or a makeup wipe, or a spot of Dawn and water to clean them out before I put them back. I shudder to think of how gross it is leaving all that dead skin cells and makeup sitting out in the open like that to collect even more bacteria. It keeps my brushes looking nice. But for the beauty sponges, once that pigment is in there, it's probably going to stain. I'm not /as/ mad at it as I thought I'd be.

I'm 45 and my skin has changed dramatically over the past 5 years. I had to move from loose powder coverage to more of a "foundation" coverage to hid all the flaws. After trying several different products, I came across this product from Avon. So, it's a cream foundation that goes on very smooth. I only apply it in the morning and find that if I don't mess with my face too much, it stays all day. It covers very well. All the little sun damage spots, redness, etc are covered evenly and smoothly. It doesn't look like you have a foundation mask on, but I also apply it down along my jaw line and neck to make sure.

There are two cons to this product: 1) it tends to accentuate fine lines until it settles. I use a magnifying mirror and you can see the make-up in the creases. From farther away, it's not that bad. I also notice that as it settles into my skin, that seems to fade. 2) I have combination skin, and it feels oily on my skin after a few hours. It does not cause breakouts (actually, my skin is so much better since I started using this product), so I don't think it's doing anything, but just feels a little oily. It doesn't LOOK oily, it just feels oily and I can't wait to get home and wash my face. I'm not a foundation user, so this may be typical, I'm not sure.

Overall, I really like this product. The coverage is fantastic and far outweighs the minor "cons" I have listed above. Since I only apply it once a day, on work days usually, it lasts a long time. It comes with a round sponge and mirror compact. It is definitely Avon quality.

review_title: Glo Tooth Whitening Device is simple and easy to use; and it works great!
review_text:
We had previously tried the GLO Science 10 Day Teeth Whitening Treatment - which is just the vials and the lubricant, but decided to try this higher tech approach and found that it does work quite a bit better than just the vials by themselves.

At first we were worried that it might be cumbersome, but the device is small like an mp3 player and hangs around your neck from a lanyard string. The mouthpiece is like having a sports mouthguard in and is barely noticeable after you've had it in for a minute or so.

Because you can wear it around your neck, it is therefore hands-free and you can go about other tasks while you're wearing it - which is helpful, because the treatments are four back-to-back 8-minute sessions; so it is 32 minutes altogether, every day for up to 10 days. If you're doing other things, you don't even notice that you have it on; the device glows when it is on and blinks when a session has ended.

We found the taste of the whitening gel to be pleasant, kind of sweet, minty. You don't have to try to not swallow while you're wearing this - it's perfectly fine to swallow some of the whitening gel - I did and there was no stomach upset or anything because of it.

The blue glow is kind of neat, like something from a sci-fi movie.

The whole thing - vials, device and mouthpiece, and instruction book come in a handy travel or storage case.

We really liked i! We're gonna order some extra vials so we can keep using the whitening device once the original supply of vials runs out.

We think it's worth someone trying out if they want whiter teeth with little or no hassle, because this Glo device is just super easy and really convenient to use. And it will brighten your smile!

I put the lotion on at about 7 am when I got up in the morning with a lotion applying glove because other reviewers stated the lotion left stains on their hands. At about 6 pm when I took a shower I noticed a lot of the lotion simply washed off.

I suppose if you want a temporary tan for an evening out, this lotion would be a perfect solution. It does dry easily and smells quite nice. It is easy to apply, with a mitt, if you pay attention. Like I said, the color does not develop. I am not sure I would use it on my face.

review_title: A Lovely Change From Hospital Soap
review_text:
We do not get out a lot, but I do go to a lot of doctors' appointments and hospitals and there is nothing I hate more than hospital soap. It is abrasive and it has a scent that is so distinct and it sticks with you for hours and hours after you have washed your hands. I loathe hospital soap.

These little soap sheets are simply amazing. Not only do they pack light - I can stick one little tin in my bag and it takes up almost no space at all, but the sheets themselves are tiny. The sheets dissolve nearly instantly in water, lather perfectly and the smell so nice. They are like a little bathroom oasis at the doctor or hospital. The scent does not linger though, so please do not be worried about smelling like ylang ylang for hours on end.

My hands always feel clean when I leave the bathroom and I have even used a sheet to wet a paper towel and wipe my face off.

As a 42 year old woman with shockingly pale skin I thought it would be interesting to try a sunless tanner. When I was younger I used Jergens sunless tanner and unless I was extremely careful and diligent I ended up orange, streaked or some combination of the two. I did not have high hopes for this sunless tanner, so I started with a small area on one leg.

First, this lotion does not have any real scent straight out of the bottle, but it does have a smell that develops once it is on the skin. It is not unpleasant and maybe the scent is dependent on the person, but it is there. Second, it is easy to apply. The first application I only put a tiny amount on my right leg and then immediately washed my hands. I let it dry for about one minute and then got dressed. Simple. Third, it takes a bit for color to appear. I started to tan in about 12 hours and by the next morning I was noticeably browner.

The second application I put on both my legs just like normal lotion. I tried paying attention to my knees and ankles, but honestly, I did not really. I washed my hands immediately, but must have brushed my forearm. I let everything dry for about one minute and then got dressed. The next morning I was tan and had a streak of brown on my arm.

I like this stuff. It is easy to use and the color lasts. My super pale skin accepts the color and I don't look nearly as translucent.

review_title: A Real Lavender Lotion That Works
review_text:
I am sort of a lavender lotion expert. I love the stuff. Most lotions that have lavender either smell like nothing or smell like an entire shop of flowers. Those lotions that do get the scent right usually are full of chemicals.

I had never heard of Kneipp before but I really like it. This lotion is not thin, but if you are used to a thick cream it will seem thinner. It does take a little work to absorb, but it is worth it. The scent is not overpowering and I think it does not linger, but is just right.

One complaint I do have is that the bottle had no safety seal. For $18 I would think the tube would come with a seal on the top. I was not sure if the bottle had already been used and returned. I just decided to go ahead and be brave and I'm still alive. Kneipp needs to add a seal on their tubes.

This is not a sticky or overwhelming lotion and does not leave your skin feeling greasy. Sometimes paying a little more for a product that really works is worth it and this is one of those times.

review_title: A Nice Pack - Would Make A Great Gift
review_text:
First, these are your typical sheet masks. They have normal directions - wash your face, apply, wait 15 to 20 minutes, remove. Simple.

These masks are however a little different in that they come packaged in a lovely little box, wrapped in tissue paper and would be the perfect gift to send someone. There are 12 masks, including two panda masks(!)

I like that there are a couple of each mask which will make it possible for both my husband and I to do a mask together.

We already did the panda mask and the scent was not overpowering. There is a lot of liquid for the skin to absorb in each packet and we did notice some dripping. This was solved by simply wiping the extra off with a washcloth. We did not rub in all the extra to our faces because it would not have been possible. The masks did not improve our faces to the point where we were amazed, but they were cooling while they were on and it was a fun Saturday, movie night thing to do.

These tattoos are fun. There is a ton to pick from and each butterfly is just a little different. They are easy to apply and the sheets they come on are not gigantic so cutting them out is not a huge chore.

Application is easy - take off the clear backing, press on skin, wet with a damp cloth for 30 seconds, remove paper.

These are the perfect size for a child's party or to give away as a prize.

They don't last an infinitely long time, which I'm sure parents would be grateful of.

The butterflies that show a shadow clearly in the description do not transfer that way in real life. Those tattoos look more like the butterfly is smudged and not 3D. If this is important to you I would simply cut the shadow part off because it truly does look like a smudge.

review_title: A Stay Put Headband That Works With Short Hair
review_text:
When the covid pandemic hit I had a very short pixie cut, which gradually turned into a mullet because I was unable to get a haircut. I am a creature of habit and I have been getting my hair cut by the same person every fourth Saturday at 9 am for the past seven years. I do not like change. A lot of things happened at the same time. The person who cut my hair moved away, covid shut down our world and my hair continued to grow. I was a mess. I tried using stretchy elastic headbands and found those stayed in place for about fifteen seconds. I successfully used felt backed headbands, but as my hair has grown longer I've found the hair in the back does not cooperate as nicely and the back of the band slips up constantly.

I decided to try these bands only because I am now desperate. They work. Huzzah.

I will say that I wish they were a little wider and in black, but I know they are meant to appeal to women and girls who want to accessorize and not to people like me who have on more than one occasion stated "my favorite color is gray". These headbands stay in place. I have been wearing the plain green one for about six hours in the kitchen, around our two dogs and doing laundry and it has not moved. Also, it does not pinch behind my ears, which I completely anticipated being a problem I would need to deal with, but I was wrong. I have noticed the felt backing has already started to come unglued, which means I am going to need to get the glue gun out and fix it. These are not headbands that are made to last for years. The price does reflect that fact.

review_title: Decent Brush For Thin Short Hair
review_text:
As most of us are in quarantine and not currently getting regular hair maintenance, having weird hair right now is just normal. I am growing out a pixie cut, not by choice, but by mandate of the State of Michigan. I have experienced a number of difficult hair transitions during this stay home, stay safe period, all of which I hope to never experience again. Currently, my hair is just too short to tuck behind my ear, so it is constantly falling in my face, but thankfully, I am past the super trendy mullet stage.

When I had my pixie cut for seven years I washed my hair and dried it with a towel and went on with my life. No comb, no brush, no anything. It was really nice. Now that I actually have hair that tangles and needs attention I require tools. I have a brush with tight bristles that I like, but it pulls. I use leave in conditioner gel that seems to help, but I still pull a lot of hair. I have a very inexpensive comb that does absolutely nothing and I should probably just recycle it.

This specific comb and brush set is definitely not the fanciest around. The comb has some heft to it and it does a good job getting my part straight. The brush is very stiff compared to my other brush, but it does not pull all my hair out when it hits a tangle. I also like that this brush doesn't mash my hair down. I have thinner hair and this brush doesn't make me look like I have thin hair.

I don't use any styling products or tools, so I am not hard on my brush. I think this brush will hold up just fine in my hands, but I think if I person were using it with lots of accessories and products it might be a placeholder for a more expensive brush.

review_title: Good, but a word of caution for people with sensitive teeth
review_text:
The nice thing about this toothbrush is that it uses the same heads as most of Oral-B's other toothbrushes. This is a basic model, which probably cleans just as well as their other models. The battery lasted me about a week of twice a day brushing, and the battery indicator tells you when you'll need to recharge it a few brushing sessions in advance. Don't ignore it too long, because it takes about 18 hours to charge it fully, but charging it about an hour should be good enough for one brushing. The charger is small and doesn't take up much room in a drawer.

The small head really works well for cleaning the sides of your teeth and between them. Oral-B talks about the cupping action and it really works like the polishing tools most hygienists use. It even seemed to dig food particles stuck between my teeth(!), but you'll still want to floss where no toothbrush can reach. If you have gum issues, this may be the ideal toothbrush for you.

The dual clean head got my teeth acceptably clean faster, but it's noticeably bigger and the precision clean head worked better overall for me. It's nice that they included two different brush heads so you can see which you prefer.

Unfortunately, the slower pulsing action seems to irritate my teeth. A week or two after I started using this toothbrush, my molars started to ache. I ended up returning it and going back to my other Oral-B, whose head looks more like a normal toothbrush which vibrates up & down very quickly. It doesn't clean along the gum line quite as well, but seems to clean the grinding surfaces of molars slightly better.

Oral-B also sells softer toothbrush heads which people seem to like and may be better for my sensitive teeth.

I added another star for Amazon's good customer service and considering that most people don't seem to have sensitive teeth. In general, just about any electric toothbrush will do a much better job cleaning your teeth, removing plaque, etc., etc. - much better than a manual brush. Try one. If you don't like it, a different type may be better for you too.

This has some pluses and minuses.

The pluses:

This doesn't irritate my skin and even if it doesn't do anything for bumpy skin, it does certainly make my skin very soft. I'm not entirely sure about its claims about dealing with skin issues like acne, as I'm a bit nervous to put this on my face. I figure that it could certainly be used for the occasional acne that shows up elsewhere (we all get it), as tea tree is well known for being a good way to treat acne. Still, I have heard that the base oil is good for skin as well, so that is a plus as well.

The main minus I have here is that while the smell here isn't awful, it's still strong enough that it gave me a bit of a headache. (That's another reason I probably won't be using it on my face.) I was able to deal with this by putting it on in small bits, which seemed to work well since the strongest part of the smell faded away pretty quickly. The remaining scent is honestly pretty nice and mellow.

I do have to commend the company for their packaging. While the bottle did leak during transport, the company was aware that this would happen ahead of time and packaged this well. I do wish that it didn't leak, but barring this I do appreciate that it was properly packaged so that the small amount of oil that leaked didn't get everywhere.

This isn't bad and it works, I just wish that the design was a little different so that I could lay it on the counter more easily.

The good of this is that you can use it on wet hair and it does straighten. There's only one button on this, although it's surrounded by several lights that give off the impression that they should also be buttons, which is very slightly confusing at first. It's easy to change between temperatures and the unit heats up incredibly quickly, which is awesome.

The downside to this is that the design makes it more difficult to lay down on the counter - if you have a sink that is slightly raised then you can prop it up against that, but I do wish it had something like some of the curling irons have. It also comes with a small bag, but I'm slightly worried about putting the straightener in the bag if it's even slightly warm, as it's the type of material that could melt easily.

I'm not really familiar with straighteners in general, but this does seem like it's designed to be similar to some of the more name brand, expensive items out there. I'm not entirely sure how the price compares, though. Overall this isn't bad.

I've had water flossers before - they're honestly pretty fantastic since they can get in places and in pockets where regular floss can't. If you get the right one and know how to use it, it's a lot like having your own dental assistant to help clean your teeth. My last water flosser gave up the ghost after I dropped it while moving (RIP water flosser!) so this seemed like it'd be good to try out.

Upon using this I immediately noticed that the lowest setting wasn't shooting out water hard enough for me, so I turned it up to the max. That worked better, but it still didn't have the oomph that its larger counterparts did. So if you're looking for a particularly intense water flosser, this isn't really going to be it. On the other hand, this would probably do well with people who want lower pressure.

The fact that this is handheld is pretty nice, although it does take a while to get used to since I'm used to the smaller water flosser nozzles. It's a bit like holding a really huge toothbrush in some aspects, if that makes any sense. The water being in the unit is an OK feature but if you like being very thorough and doing several passes, you'll more than likely need to refill at some point. That part isn't a big hardship as filling this up is a breeze and one of the nicest aspects of it. It's insanely easy to do and isn't needlessly complicated.

In the end the main draw for this would be that I can take it with me on trips, which I almost certainly will. It's far easier to pack into a travel bag or throw into a suitcase than a standard water flosser with a huge tank would be. I just don't think that I'd prefer this for daily use over a more traditional unit, especially since I like my water pressure a lot higher than that. Still, for what it is, it's not bad and it'd be a good little gadget for travelers.

review_title: Almost everything you ever wanted and less
review_text:
It's a good mask, according to my wife and daughter. They both tried it and, after they did, there was enough left for maybe one application. Strangely, the tin came only half-full and I don't know if it was so only because it was from a batch sent to Vine reviewers.
The mask gets pretty dry after application but skin underneath stays Okay. Of course, it has all the right ingredients so, no surprises such as allergic reactions, swelling or redness. It's probably something that you would want to use once weekly but not more often.

The marketing blurb says, among other things "this advanced man face care formula features stem cells to help revive the skin and smooth out imperfections".
Well... stem cells, if they were actually somehow harvested, in a cosmetics container, mixed with various other chemicals and ingredients would necessarily be dead and therefore completely irrelevant. And, of course, the stem cells would help address things such as diabetes and repair of heart muscle following heart attack, not zits on one's face. Not to mention that they would need to be live and 'human' cells. So, I am quite confident that the 'stem cells' claim is untrue and, even if it were true, the presence of dead stem cells in a cream would make zero difference.
Other than that, the cream is thick and, as other reviewer found, it has an aggressive smell that reminded me of Noxzema. So I would never use it during the day. At night, it would probably be Okay if used by men who sleep alone.

I am one of those who prefer water flossers to string-based flossing. Process is much cleaner and, in my view, cleaning is more thorough.
This Chinese designed and made unit works well. You fill it with warm water, select the mode, possibly select a specific pick - but I always use the regular one - and you start flossing away.
Item design and ergonomics are generally Okay. However, the manual is not exactly helpful but most of us should be able to figure it out, eventually. Charging is via a custom USB cable but there is no actual charging unit so you need to find one such as your phone charger. You only need to charge it once every couple of weeks if you use it once daily.
Overall, a useful item and it does appear to be durable. Time will tell.

Surprisingly, this small set, probably the smallest I've seen so far, comes with everything you will need for beard-mustache trimming and it could be used for hair styling for as long as your hair is not too long.
I would recommend it as a travel option because of its small and efficient size but it could also be used as the default beard or generally facial hair tool if your needs aren't anything special.

review_title: Argan Oil Is Not Snake Oil
review_text:
I've been used this specific shampoo only a couple of times as it was offered by vendor as a 'for review' item but we've been into Argan Oil shampoos for the past half year or so and we are very happy with the results. In fact our teenage daughter insists that whatever shampoo we purchase it contains the Argan Oil.

This shampoo provided a thorough, gentle cleaning of my hair and scalp and there is not discomfort or itchy feeling whatsoever after use which is a good thing. Our daughter likes it too but she observed that 'it smells funny'. I do agree that there is a strong, not necessarily unpleasant, smell for a brief few seconds while you are applying the shampoo on hair.

Additional facts worth sharing:

- It comes in a tube and a tube this size should probably last 2-3 months if used by a couple of people so, while the price is higher than what you'll typically see at a supermarket, it's not THAT high when spread over several months and it's worth the extra few dollars.
- While it's not stated anywhere, it seems to act as a conditioner. I would not use use a conditioner after this shampoo myself.
- For what is worth, the ingredients include: Aloe leaf extract, Argan oil, Xanthan gum and dozen of ingredients that are difficult to spell or pronounce but the maker promise that there are no petrochemical derivatives or parabens and that no animal testing was conducted.

The odds are I will continue to use this shampoo until I am made aware of a superior product. Until then, I am happy with it.
