Somehow, calling the Norelco arcitec 1090 a "Men's Shaving System" seems to be a little pretentious; so I'll still call it a shaver... a very, very good shaver!

I got the aritec with the idea that it just might be time to adjust my look and rid myself of the beard I'd sported for the past two and a half years (long story, dull, boring and not germane to a product review). I played with it and the beard for a week or so and then got real with the scissors and trimmer one evening. Wow! This is great!

This represents my fourth (or fifth?) Norelco shaver over the past 40-odd years, so clearly I'm guilty of some serious brand loyalty. But while my previous Norelco shavers each represented a modest improvement over each predecessor, the arcitec is so far advanced that I'm really amazed. It's cordless (uh.. duh...), but the first appealing little techno-googah in its arsenal is a display that tells you how many minutes worth of charge remain. Nice touch! Another informational readout tells you when to clean the stubble from the unit, nice for absent-minded souls like me that can get in a rush some mornings and are left wondering days later why the razor sounds a little "off".

I'm kind of a "good design" junkie. I can't innovate myself, but I'd like to think that I recognize when the designers really, really sat down and looked for ways to make their product better. The arcitec delivers on that big time!

Cleaning the shaving head ensemble is absurdly easy. The heads just flip up so that you can blow, brush or rinse them out. Yes, I said rinse, as in the use of running water. This isn't the first razor that claims to be water friendly, however it is the first one to give me enough confidence to actually hold the shaving head under the tap. The only criticism that I have is that the trimmer almost seems like something of an afterthought. It's fine for trimming sideburns, however when I had the beard it was a little clunky to use while trimming around the edges etc. But with my newly clean-shaven approach, that's a very minor complaint.

In the end however, all of those lovely little features like numeric display of the remaining battery charge, maintenance and cleaning access, and other things would all fall by the wayside if the quality of the shave were substandard. So I will simply state that the arcitec leaves me with a smoother face than any other shaving system I've ever used... electric shaver or razor blade!

Nothing ticks me off more than paying a premium price for a product that doesn't deliver premium performance. And the arcitec delivers in every way... design, usability, reliability and performance!

review_title: Great Trimmer, Leaves your Bathroom Clean and Works just Right
review_text:
As usual great service when buying directly from Amazon.

This review is mostly a comparison to old trimmers I have used such as one that charges on a base and one that runs off 2 AA batteries.

Positives
1. The charger is just a cable that plugs into the bottom. I personally hate bases as I have drawers and other storage and this allows me to pull it out real quick to charge the couple of hours it needs and then I just bundle it up and put it away.
2. The Battery lasts a long time, even with the vacuum this thing just keeps going. Should easily last me a month as I have goatee and mustache versus a full beard.
3. The vacuum does a good job and picks up most hairs so there is minimal cleanup. Usually I just blow on the head to get rid of loose hairs so they don't end up in my drawer.
4. The size adjustment is quick and doesn't require separate attachments.
5. It gives you a great look, it gives a nice even cut and I will be using this for a few years.

Negatives
1. If your trimmer batteries are dead it still won't run even when plugged in. The trimmer turns off the charging port when you press the on button. The more expensive model allows this so it's just a up sell not a technical limitation.
2. This device is huge compared to most other trimmers I have tried. For the most part this isn't too bad but it's sort of difficult to trim my mustache under my nose but with a little practice it isn't hard.
3. It can get clogged when doing longer hair as the vacuum is smaller so either cut long hair in two steps or just keep cutting because it still cuts just fine even when the vacuum is clogged..

Overall I compared this to the higher end model that has the smaller trimmer attachment and I would say get this plus a tiny Remington trimmer as I feel these are too fat for delicate work.

UPDATE: I purchased this item June 2009 and gave it a full charge. I trim my mustache and goatee regularly with this and I have not charged it since new and it performs perfectly. In regards to durability, everything works fine and I have no issues with it.
UPDATE (6/15/10): Working like new, I've only charged it like 3 times and I am a hairy guy. Trimming goatee, mustache, and keeping that scruffy look without issues.

review_title: No Norelco, I still prefer my 550 TL
review_text:
I bought a Norelco 550 TL about 17 years ago and I still have it. I like the way the Floating Heads give a close shave, and the way the pop-up sideburn trimmer works crisply and efficiently. It cleans easily and is compact. I think I spent a $25 on my 550 TL brand new.

When I had the chance to try the Norelco Cool Skin 8040X, I looked forward to putting this Norelco newbie through its paces.

But I was very disappointed.

THe VERY first thing I DID NOT like (ZERO stars for this!!) was the plastic "Clamshell Packaging" -- which is a waste of plastic and time. IF Norelco had decided to incorporate a Travel Case into this Clamshell packaging with re-usable features, then I would have been content. But as it was, this was just a waste of plastic. Clamshell packages have sent numerous folks to the hospital with some nasty cuts inflicted while trying to open this sealed, thick plastic, stubborn packaging. Then again, it is a waste of plastics made even more wasteful when you consider the price of petroleum nowadays, and the inability to recycle this type of plastic. I suppose someone who wants to, can, with a little ingenuity and transparent mailing tape, take this Clamshell Package and create a travel container for their 8040x-- which might be a good idea, because the fabric travel pouch that Norelco supplies with this shaver only holds the shaver, and not the accessories -- unless you want to cram everything into the travel case and NOT close it.

Well.... now -- about the shaver itself. The instruction book is very thorough -- but the warnings interspersed throughout are in grey print -- how about bold black?

The shaver itself is nothing I would want to use all the time -- in fact, after trying it, I still prefer my 550 TL. The heads on the 8040X DO flex, but the moisturizing cream/gel only comes through two of them when all three heads with moisturizer would work much better -- the heads also drag across my skin -- and in some instances gave me a bit of razor burn -- especially on my neck. This shaver was used in the shower, so there was plenty of (acqua) moisture, in addition to gel moisturizer, available for a close shave, but the shave was not as good as it should have been.

Putting the moisturizer into the shaver is a feat that involves pumping the cartridge manually and then cleaning up the excess moisturizer that suddenly splats out of the shaver when it is full. Um.........

This Norelco 8040X is a nice idea, but it's gimmicky and labor intensive, when all I want is a quick shave and then a quick rinse of the heads and the knowledge that my shaver will be ready and willing the next morning. The Norelco 8040X IMHO probably work just as well on dry skin as on wet -- but it's nothing I would want to use on a regular basis.

review_title: How is this "sanitizing"? Where is the alcohol at suffient concentration to be a sanitizer?
review_text:
The description claims this is sanitizing, but a cleaning product and a sanitizer are not the same thing. Sanitizers aim to kill germs directly, which sets them apart from soaps or cleansers, which often work by removing germs from skin rather than killing them.

Hand sanitizers need a minimum of 65% alcohol content to be effective against the coronavirus for instance. For this product to make the claim that it sanitizes rather than simply clean raises big red flags for me, especially during this Covid 19 coronavirus pandemic when people can't find acyual hand sanitizers.

And when it comes to removing germs from the skin by washing, you not only need soap, you also need running water to flush away the soap and germs.

This may be good at removing visible dirt and such, but it cannot replace actual hand washing or real hand sanitizers to suffuciently remove or kill germs.

I received this shaver as a Christmas gift, and returned it within a week.  I have used Norelco shavers for 20 years, but this one is poorly designed. Third, the cleaning system is bulky, and cumbersome.  What ever happened to the simple Norelco technology: open the head, brush them out, and replace the blades when the shave gets poor.  This design is made to attract, but the shave is no better than the Norelcos I have had for years.  I'm back to my old Norelco now.

The chamomile/rose soaps clean satisfactorily (used for body washing), thin suds like most 100% olive oil soaps, rinse well leaving a squeaky smoothness, not too drying or oily; seem to be naturally colored with clay or oxides: however, I do not think they are naturally fragranced. The smell from both is synthetic, sharp, burning, catches in the throat, fills and stings the nostrils, causing sneezing. The perfume makes it unpleasant for me to use. Essential oils do not do this. Plus, they both smell suspiciously similar. Sadly, this has ruined a decent soap at a great price for me. Reluctant to use even as hand soap.

An Effective Solution For Razor-Issues For Men And Women...

I've been using these razors since the early 90's. And while I wear a beard now, I still have to shape the hairline up around my lower neck and face.

If you're prone to razor rash or ingrown hairs, this is a much better pick for you than any other disposable razor. Originally designed by a black dermatologist, this razor was created specifically for black guys that have a chronic problem with daily shaving. Well, as guys go, they're not alone. And this razor fixed that problem for me handily!

Back when I wore a suit and tie, and worked minimally six days a week, daily shaving became a real bummer for me. This razor offered an affordable and convenient "fix" for a real problem.

How It Works: A thin "rake" overrides the single blade, preventing the cutting edge from shaving too closely, thereby eliminating the aforementioned problems of razor rash and ingrown hairs. No, you won't get as close a shave... But a five o'clock shadow at two o'clock, is a lesser evil than a face or neck full of razor rash and ingrown hairs! Some people's hair/follicles and skin-types will simply not tolerate an ultra-close shave, and that's the end of it.

Note: Anybody that is troubled with razor-related problems, should avoid using the double and triple blade cartridges, as these will just exacerbate your problems. Further, guys (or gals) with such problems should avoid shaving against the direction of the hairs as well, as this too will just exacerbate your problems.

Also: There are better solutions for shaving than shaving soap. Hair conditioner, warmed slightly in a microwave cup shaves far nicer than any soap I've tried in 62 years. And it's good to let the conditioner sit on your skin a few minutes before shaving. Just keep your razor rinsed-out really well, while using it. Clogged razors can be cleared with an old toothbrush, always brushing away from the blade's cutting edge to avoid damaging it.

Depending on your beard, a single Bump Fighter Razor can serve well between say, three days and one week... Some guys alternate these razors with the more traditional types... After a while, I found that I really only needed these Bump Fighter Razors on my neck, where my collars rubbed.

Note: My wife favored these razors for her personal grooming as well, reporting zero rash or ingrown hair issues when using them. She later found that she could make do with regular disposable razors on her legs and underarms, but greatly preferred these Bump Fighter Razors for bikini-line work, and such. You'll figure it out...

I was very pleased to see Amazon pick up these razors, since Wal-Mart and Walgreens stopped carrying them in stores. I had to go looking for them online, and while I did find them, it's so much easier just adding them to my Amazon orders!

Note: People with severe shaving-related issues should look into permanent hair removal via laser or pulsed light depilation by a professional. The winter rates are getting more and more affordable, I hear, and it offers at least a "semi-permanent" solution.

For the price, I'm genuinely surprised with this nail drill. First of all, it doesn't suffer from the two major issues most cheap nail drills face: lack of torque and internal wobbling. A lack of torque is when the rotation mechanism stalls out if you press hard enough against the nail. You'll know a nail drill has internal wobbling because it will almost tickle or feel uncomfortable when you file your nails.

With that being said, here's what I don't like: I prefer much thinner nail drills. Even if you "choke up" your grip onto the thinner part of the drill it's still thick enough to make my hands tired if I'm using it for longer than a few minutes. I can't imagine this being comfortable to use all day in a nail salon. Next, the instructions. It took me way too long to figure out how to change the drill bit, partly due to the vague instructions and partly because I had to use so much force I genuinely thought I was going to break it. The twist mechanism is misleading. You turn it and it stops so you think you're done turning it but in actuality you have to keep turning it until you hear a click.
It also would be nice for the manufacturer to explain the differences between all the drill bits and what the intended use case is for each one.

FOR THOSE OF YOU THAT CAN'T CHANGE THE DRILL BIT:

Turn the top portion of the drill toward the side labeled "R" until you hear a click (this is important) use pliers and pull out the drill bit. You'll need to use more force than you think.
Once you've removed the drill bit, stop turning the top portion of the drill toward "R". The mechanism will go back to the center by itself. Pick your desired drill bit and put it where the old drill bit was. Turn the top portion of the drill towards the labeled "S" until you hear a click to secure the drill bit (The drill bit WILL fall out if you don't twist it towards "S" until you hear a click).

review_title: Crest White Strips Do Work - A Dentist Reviews this Product
review_text:
I am a dentist who recommends Crest White Strips because they do work to whiten teeth. Follow the directions in the box, and here are some further tips:

1. (Optional step) I recommend you first brush your teeth with water (don't use toothpaste) to remove the layer of plaque. Your enamel has pores and the pores need to be open for the chemical to penetrate. If you use a fluoridated toothpaste, the flouride may block the enamel pores. (Crest's instructions indicate you do not need to brush. I talked to a Crest representative on this point, and she indicated that the hydrogen peroxide will penetrate plaque, therefore this step is optional. The instructions indicate no brushing because they do not want fluoridated toothpaste on the teeth before whitening).

2. Use the strips twice per day for maximum efectiveness. The inner part of the strip has a chemical called carbamide peroxide (a 6% form of hydrogen peroxide; in-office dental whitening uses a 15-30% version of the same chemical) that causes the stains inside your teeth to be oxidized and turn white. Applying the strips has a small learning curve as you will probably bend or fold a couple of them before you get the technique down.

2. Leave the strips on for 30 minutes at a time. After thirty minutes your saliva has probably diluted the peroxide to the extent that it is no longer effective. You can reapply a new strip immediately if you chose, for the treatment requires one hour of treatment time per day to work. It does not matter if you do this in one continuous 60-minute period or two 30-minute periods. Do this for two weeks and your teeth should get whiter.

Disadvantages

1. The chemical may "burn" your gums. If you notice a burning sensation when you use the product, it is the peroxide oxidizing (or burning) your gums. Depending on how severe the burning is, it may cause you to stop the treatment. It is OK to stop the treatment for a day or two to let the gums heal. Once they feel normal again, resume treatment with the White Strips.

2. Your teeth may become senstiive during the two-week treatment time. Try to push yourself through the sensitivity if it is mild, but if it bothersome to cold water or air, take a day or two off to let the teeth settle down and then pick up where you left off.

3. The strips only cover your front teeth, so only your front teeth will bleach. You may notice the distinct difference between the back (unbleached) teeth and the front (bleached) teeth. Since most people notice the front 6 teeth anyway, this is not a concern. However, if you have a wide toothy smile, you may want to have a dentist make you a tray that will hold the chemical on the back teeth to whiten them too.

3. The bleaching effect works best on yellow stains. If your stains are due to tetracycline (brownish grey stains in a band on your teeth, your best bet is to have a dentist whiten your teeth as the dentist will use a tray to hold a more concentrated form of the chemical on your teeth for a longer period of time.

Crest White Strips work for the vast majority of people. Over time, you will get a result that should be whiter than when you started. Crest White Strips are a good place to start with bleaching, and if you are not satisfied with the results, you can then see your dentist for a more concentrated form of bleaching or other cosmetic options.

konedog DDS

review_title: Great E-file. Bad decal ("Nail Drill") (update, they may have changed that)
review_text:
Pros: this is fairly lightweight, very quiet, low vibration, battery charges quickly and lasts very long. Overall, I think it is a really good value for a more expensive e-file, while still being more affordable than the $400 options.
Cons: one of the biggest cons for me is a personal pet peeve. It's that damn Giant nail drill written on it. ** If the product pictures are accurate, this seems to have been changed** It takes a tool that looks otherwise very professional and sleek and makes it look cheap and amateurish. (I painted over the writing and black and then matte top coated. I'll probably put a sticker on it anyway.) People in a professional setting, please stop referring to this as a drill! It just bolsters peoples fear of efiles, in addition to being completely inaccurate. The other con is that you have to turn the speed dial to turn off the file. A separate power button would be better, so that you could keep your RPM setting as is. This is especially cumbersome and time-consuming when you are switching directions. Turn the dial down to turn off the machine, hit the direction button turn the dial back up to whatever speed you need. May not seem like a big deal, but when you're doing it over and over on lots of clients, it's just a pain in the neck.
Overall, I think it's actually pretty high quality piece of equipment, but In fairness, I have never used some of the more expensive professional units from Kupa or youngnails, etc.

UPDATE: I LOVE THESE GUARDS.... that being said the truth is these lasted for exactly 2 weeks. I think I could of gotten longer if I capped my tips better with gel because the edge of my nail tips were the first area to start showing wear and ever so sightly the guards at the tip started to peel (2 weeks). It was soo easy to take the Guards and GelColor off, in a matter of a few minutes. My natural nail is perfect after taking them off... no damage, no dryness, no staining, no brittleness. My tips were white and not stained and my nail beds were a normal pink and best of all they have grown out healthy and are my own nails, YAY!!! I will never need fake tips again. I am sooo excite how well these worked. Honestly they never looked so good after taking off any nail color that includes plain nail polish which would stain my nails and dry out from nail polish remover. The bond of these shields sticks very well and strong. Also anyone having trouble with gel sticking to there natural nails because of their own natural nail chemistry.... this maybe be a great solution for you.

UPDATE: Amazing! I have figured out the PERFECT combination to make them last longer then 2 weeks, actually they last until I am ready to remove. Here’s what I do... I prep my nails using opi nas99 and opi bondaid then I apply the Nail guards, then I apply 2 thin coats of HARD gel I used iBD hard gel (nail builder) right over the Nail Guards, cap the end of the nails well, then I apply 2 coats of color gel (GelColor) and then 1 or 2 coats of OPI Top coat the OPI Top Coat is stronger then the gelcolor so I usually put 2 coats of top top but 1 is fine, it just depends on what you like, I like my nails supper glossy, a little thicker, this combination makes them super strong. Caping the NailGuard on the end with iBD Hard gel is the secret to gelcolor lasting longer. This combination last for weeks on end without any peeling or chipping. My nails are now super strong and protected, are healthier, my manicure stays for weeks on end and best of all it easily comes off when I am ready to take it off with no damage. The only thing is I have to use my regular UV light for the Hard gel (180 sec ea coat of hard gel) to cure and I use my LED OPI Light (30 sec ea coat) for my Gelcolor to cure but it’s 100% worth it!

These are essentially giant temporary tattoos very similar to the ones you sometimes get as novelty gifts and promotional material.
Like those, you simply peel off the protective cover, press the design where you want it, then wet the back of the paper holding the tattoo, until it transfers to your skin.
Rubbing alcohol helps wipe the tattoo off, if wear and tear and sweat don't take it out first.

The reasons I personally did not care for these:
- A lot less vivid on my skin, than in photos or against the paper
- There is no precut opening for your mouth; FYI, you get the best result cutting (carefully) an opening after you put the tattoo on, not before
- Very difficult to line up with your own mouth
- If you wear these over your mouth, the activity of talking, drinking, eating, etc... rapidly degrades the tattoo, causing wrinkles, gaps, tears, etc...

In my opinion, the best use of these temporary tattoos would be to create the illusion of a fake mouth somewhere else on you body, like your tummy, neck, back, hand, etc...
Honestly, I was just really disappointed with these all around.

I really like these press on toenails for special occasions in the summer.
After you finish a pedicure, you can glue these on, then slip into your favorite open toed shoes.
I would just keep three things in mind before ordering these...

1st, sizing is tricky. Turns out toenails vary widely in shape and size.
I was able to make my set work, but one of the nails looks wonky.
If you were getting these for a hugely important event like a wedding, I might order the two sizes closest to your toes just to make certain you could get an absolutely perfect fit.

2nd, these do not last as long as press on fingernails (at least not for me).
I am lucky if I can get these through a whole day without needing to reattach one of these nails.
To be fair, I am a bit of a klutz.
That being said, I think it's more a product of how much wear and tear most feet get on an average day.
You also tend to hit your foot harder, so one stubbed toe and you're going to have an issue.
The good news is these are super easy to reattach, plus you get a few spares to replace any nails that are completely lost.

3rd, preparation is critical to getting the most out of these nails.
Getting or giving yourself a pedicure before applying these is not just about making sure your feet look their best, the cleaning and buffing is necessary to get the best bond from the glue tabs.
You do get a little file to help you with this; though honestly, most people will prefer to use their own tools.

I really like these as a way to show off shoes and feet.
Attaching them takes very little time and the end result is quite elegant.
Still, I would consider these best for special occasions, not every day.

review_title: Takes some getting used to, but holds hair well
review_text:
When I first began using these I really struggled with getting them on/off, particularly when trying to put my hair up in a ponytail.
The problem was that when I was pulling my hair out through the circular clip, it would get caught on the prongs spread out along the inside
After using these a while, however, I am getting better at putting the clips in and taking them out.

One trick I figured out pretty quickly is that twisting my hair before pulling it through the circle prevents it getting caught.
The other thing I have learned is that this is excellent for putting my hair up in a bun.
That's probably my favorite use for these because I get a nice symmetrical look and a very tight hold that keeps my hair up all day long.

Overall, I am very glad I stuck with these because, the longer I have them, the more I like them.
The clips which start out as kind of stiff and hard to open, also get easier to slide open and closed with repeated use.

In the end, I cannot promise these will work for every type of hair out there.
I can, however, confirm that they hold my long, fine, straight, and very slippery hair in place well.
That's a huge deal for me since my hair is exceptionally hard to keep up with scrunchies, clips, bands, and ties.

If you like the look of these clips, I do recommend getting a set, but caution that patience and practice will be needed before you are able to make the most out of them.

review_title: Ideal make-up when you are on the go
review_text:
This makeup is very different than any other I have used in terms of how it is stored and applied; however, I really, really like it.
If you are someone who travels or likes to touch up your foundation throughout the day, this might well be the perfect makeup for you.
It comes in a very well designed compact that holds the liquid foundation in a sponge in its own closed compartment.
The applicator sponge sits atop the cover to that compartment, so the entire thing is spill proof and well protected.

Applying the makeup I found that it blended very well using the included applicator sponge.
The coverage level is medium, evening out skin tone and obscuring imperfections, but not covering major discoloration.
Put another way, if you have a mole or blemish you really want to cover up, you would probably still want to use a spot corrector.

The foundation itself has a matte finish with a nice feel.
I've found I can wear it on its own or with a powder finish.

Color matches are always tricky, particularly online; however, I managed to get a pretty great one.
Unless I have been getting a lot of sun, my skin is pretty pale.
I'm basically one step up from ivory skin, which this Beige Color blended with extremely well.

To show how well it blends and how matte the finish is, I applied it onto one half of my inner forearm, then took photos in two different light settings.
In the photos, the bottom half of my forearm has the foundation on it, but it leaves almost no line and no shine.

As far as staying power is concerned, I would rate this is above average.
It stayed on well for me all day when I was not sweating, but would come off a little on anything that directly rubbed against my skin.
I also found this to be a gentle foundation that did not irritate my skin.

I can happily recommend this foundation compact.
I was truly pleased with both the design of the dispenser, which makes it perfectly portable, and with the performance of the makeup itself.

it would be to add a loop of some sort to hang it by, so it can be left to dry on a hook.
Still, I can add something like that myself or just hang it over a towel rack, so it's not a big deal.

review_title: Got a perfect color match with decent coverage
review_text:
I included a half make-up, half naked skin photo, taken with my phones portrait filter off, to give you some sense of how this foundation looks.
I was fortunate in that the time I spent studying the shades on the product page paid off with a pretty spot on color match for my skin, which had me very excited.

Regarding how the make-up went on, I actually found I got better results applying it with my finger than I did with the included make-up sponge.
I know using a sponge is better for your skin, but I found it just kept blending the foundation right off my face.
Whether that was a result of how I applied it, the foundation itself, and/or the sponge is up for debate.
Since you get two sponges included with the two bottles of make-up, you can experiment and decide what application method works best for you.
Side note, this is way too thick to be air brushed on and can't be diluted, so if you use an airbrush, this foundation probably isn't for you.

Regarding how the foundation looked and felt, I would say, standard.
This reminded me of pretty much every good quality foundation I have ever tried.
- It looks best after you first put it on
- It covers many, but not all marks and discoloration
- As the end of the day approaches, it starts to look "fatigued"
- It will wipe off on hands, clothing, etc... if you rub your face
- You need to put some effort into getting all traces of the foundation cleaned off at the end of the day
- For best results, you'll probably want to pair it with a spot concealer and finishing powder

Overall, this is a solid foundation that performs well, but is not exceptional.
If you get a good match to your skin tone like I did, I suspect you will be very pleased with this make-up set.
In the end, I would definitely recommend this, so long as you understand this is not the ultimate fix all your problems, find your prince, do your taxes, and make you smarter miracle in a bottle all foundations claim to be, but instead, a quality make-up that will give you good coverage.

This drill is POWERFUL!
And I mean that both in the sense of how fast and strong the drill is, as well as how long the battery pack lasts.

I have a rechargeable nail drill that I like, but it doesn't always work as fast or as long as I hope, so I was curious to see how this would compare.
Well, I was blown away.
This is like a rechargeable drill on steroids.

To be clear, there is still a wire connecting the drill to the power source/control panel.
While that cord is not a huge problem, it does handle differently than the rechargeable nail drills that are a single unit.
That being said, for me the trade off in power you get makes the two piece design well worth it.

One thing to consider before committing to this nail drill, which is AMAZING, is that as the saying goes, "With great power comes great responsibility".
Put another way, you need to be very careful when using this nail drill, particularly on the highest setting.
This drill can turn fast enough to: quickly heat up your nails, file right through acrylic and natural nail material, get away from you and damage the skin around your nail.
Basically, you need to respect the power of this drill when you are using it, particularly when you start out learning how to handle it.

Other things I really like about this drill:
- The remaining charge is digitally displayed on the battery portions, so you know exactly how much power you have let
- You select the power level with a dial; this allows you to adjust the rotation of your drill very precisely
- You get a wide range of attachments that cover almost anything you would want to do with your nail drill
- Charges with a standard USB cord, which is included (you need to provide an adapter or USB port)
- You change the nail bits by locking and unlocking them with a twist release; I find this is easier and makes for a more secure hold of the bits than the drill bits that rely on a simple push/pull mechanism
- Reverses direction quickly and easily

It took a while to get this review together because there was a lot to unpack with this steamer and all the little extras that came with it; however, what stood out most was how fast and powerful the steamer itself was.
If you were thinking you'd be waiting around a few minutes for this thing to start producing steam, chances are you will be pleasantly surprised by how little time it takes for the device to start pushing out huge clouds of steam.

While the instructions that come with this set are detailed, using the device itself is fairly straightforward.
Simply be aware that the steamer needs to be plugged in to work; moreover, you will probably want to sit during its operation so that you can lean over it for a few minutes at a time.
That means you'll want to find a place where you can use the steamer comfortably, like a vanity or desk.

Other things to keep in mind as you consider buying this.
- The handheld, portable, rechargeable device is a mister, not a steamer. This wasn't completely clear on the product page, so I want to make note of it. Basically, the mister is a nice thing you can use to cool down and refresh your skin on the go.
- Packaging suggests two different types of water for the steamer and mister respectively.
- steamer = distilled water
- mister = mineral water
- The steamer's cord is about 2.5 feet long, which is something you will want to consider when decided where you will be most likely to use the steamer.
- The little extras like the headband with ears and the pore clearing tools make this a great gift to give someone who enjoys getting and giving facials.
- The manufacturer warns that acne which is hormonal in nature will not respond to the steamer
- The instructions also advise you not to use the steamer everyday, nor more than 10 minutes at a time. Accordingly, this is not something that is likely to add a lot of time to your daily routine, but rather something you will use once or twice a week.
- The steamer itself is cute and compact, so you're not giving up a huge amount of space if you get one, nor do you necessarily have to hide it in between uses, unless you want to.
- The steam produced is hot/warm and there is no way to control the temperature; however, you can easily regulate how you experience the heat simply by adjusting the proximity of your face to the steamer.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this facial steamer set as a purchase for yourself or as a gift for someone else who enjoys giving/getting spa treatments at home.
I personally like the effect it had on my skin; I felt as though using it has helped with both the cleansing and hydration of my skin.
Once you get through all the instructions, procure the right type of water for your steamer, and identify where you want to set it up, you will be rewarded with an easy to use machine that produces copious amounts of steam very rapidly

review_title: Definitely casual and a bit tricky
review_text:
What I was expecting to get with this was not what I actually got...
Still, the real problem is that this hair accessory requires a lot of work, yet produces only a very casual result.

The set itself consists of: scrunchy with hair attached to it, a small black elastic tie, and some black hair clips.
In order to use it, you put your hair up in a bun with the elastic tie, pull the scrunchy over the bun, then secure it with the pins as needed.

The biggest issues I had with this set were the overall quality and the difficulty of use.
It also won't be much help to those with very thin/sparse hair because it only makes the end of your hair look longer/thicker, while doing nothing much for your scalp or hairline.
You also need enough hair to form a small bun to begin with, which limits the number of women who will be able to wear it at all.

The color I selected was a light brown that matches my hair well enough to wear,
though not well enough to make it disappear into my hair style completely.
Since you are ordering from a photograph, you have to simply use your best guess to decide what the right color for you would be.

Other concerns include that fact that the scrunchy shed several strands of hair pretty quickly and the accessories are very chintzy.
More likely than not, you will need/want to use your own pins to secure your bun before you add the scrunch element.
Personally, I had to fuss with this a lot to get it to look right and stay put; however, I am not naturally gifted in the art of coiffuring, so that may be a reflection on me, as much as the scrunchy itself.

In the end, I would definitely not recommend this for a formal occasion because it does look very tousled and I doubt that is something you can change.
If you are someone who likes to play with your hair, this might be a fun way to create the illusion of fuller hair.
Personally, I would rather this set either be easier to use, since it would most likely be used on casual days, or be more amendable to formal hairstyles, so that investing the effort of getting it to look good would feel more worthwhile.

Keratin treatments rebound the keratin in your hair so that they are all put back into place. There are a lot of steps but don’t get discouraged because they’re quiet simple. To start of give 2 good shampoos with a clarifying shampoo (specifically the keratin complex one, then towel dry and blow dry the unconditioned hair. Once fully dry, make small sections and apply the treatment from roots to ends and comb through with a fine tooth comb to make sure hair is fully saturated. Let that sit for 30 minutes then blow dry again without washing out the product. Once fully dry the final step will be to straighten the hair with a flatiron so the keratin will set in your hair. review_text:
I’ve got the KXAMELIE mountain green short nail set. It’s a lovely hunter green, as pictured, but that’s about it. They’re not nearly as nice or thick as advertised. I don’t think they’re UV gel, just plastic.

The instructions are vague and unhelpful for beginners and you have to carefully peel off a sticker just to read them. I really wanted to like these nails, yet the glue tab system is a real pain in the neck! You have to get it on your nail, wrestle off the plastic cover, hold under a hair dryer until it looks wet or your skin feels like it’s gonna fall off, pop the nail on and hope it’s straight, and then repeat over and over and over. I guess I could’ve used liquid glue but I didn’t have any handy that day so…. I will say the glue stickers were stronger than I was expecting. They remind me of those little glue dots you get on stuff in the mail sometimes.

My biggest beef with these is that they all come with jagged edges on the ends(however they were manufactured I presume) that snag on things and zero instructions on how to file or trim them. Just a tiny cardboard file tossed in.

Also, beware if you have small hands, which I do, so I’ve run into this problem a lot. The nail sizes are either a bit too small or too big. There’s no good in-between and you can see the gaps in the pictures. I prefer a little gapping to the plastic overlap digging into my skin. Trust me, they looked worse in person, tho. I was kind of embarrassed to wear them at work.

Overall, better than dollar store quality but not by much. Not for beginners due to the hassle. I wouldn’t try again as they only held up for a day. It was the rare color that lured me in.

This product is a perfect example of a good product compromised by packaging. Each of the four pampering products was lovely: the body butter was rich and moisturizing without leaving the skin feeling greasy, the scrub had a good texture that never scratched or left skin dried out; the body wash felt great and cleansing, and even the bath salts, the weakest offering in the bunch, left the water pleasantly scented with a fresh, sparkling pineapple scent. Indeed, if you are a pineapple fan the combination of all these products is heavenly.

But the creams and potions are difficult to extract from their packaging! Instead of bottles or pots, a sealed envelope is used, similar to the ones you might purchase loose tea in. It takes up less room and weighs less than traditional packaging, so this option is very environmentally friendly. I was able to squeeze the body cream and body wash out in a manner similar to pushing toothpaste out of a tube, but I wasn’t able to get everything. The bath salts shook right out, so that wasn’t bad. But oh, the scrub! I loved the texture of the scrub but it was impossible to get out. It wouldn’t squeeze out and it was too sticky to pour, so I had to try and reach in and scoop it out with my fingertips. I gave up after using less than half of it because so much of the scrub got pushed into the deep corners of the envelope that I couldn’t get to it.

I recommend skipping this travel option and buying full-sized products instead. They’re great to use and very moisturizing for the skin - I would rate most of them 4 or 5 stars if not for the travel packaging.

It cleans your teeth pretty well. I also like the pressure indicator that lets you know if you're pushing too hard. Because it's fully functional, I don't feel like I can give it less than 3 stars. But here's why it doesn't get more.

First, the brush cycle. I've used other electric toothbrushes that also have the concept of a brush cycle, a beep, series of beeps, difference in the brush, whatever, that informs you to switch to a different area of your mouth. This toothbrush has that too and it works. Then it keeps working. The others I've used ran through the full cycle then turned off. This one, just kept going. You have to manually switch it off before it will stop. It's not a big deal since I know what part of my teeth I'm brushing, but it's part of the general behavior that I don't like.

Next, drool. Again, I've used other tooth brushes and I know that you have to maintain a good seal or you'll spray things everywhere and/or drool all over your chest. But with this brush, I was getting drool despite maintaining a good seal. I was very careful and always was leaking. Why exactly? I'm not sure, but I attribute it somehow to the shape or action or ergonomics.

Finally, the easiest to fix, I think the brush is way to strong. If I were to continue using this, I'd need a softer brush.

It might just be me, but I'm just not crazy about it even though it works adequately.

review_title: Larger than expected, but works well.
review_text:
They made this out to be pocketable. It's not really, too thick, but it's also not crazy large like the Equigroomer is. I wanted to try this out before seeing if I should buy the equigroomer. OVERALL, impressed.

Pros:
-Dual blades, one for short hairs and one for medium-long hairs.
-EASY and reliable self-cleaning, retract the blades and easy to pull off the hair, also like how the hair (as long as you don't have a fan or a large gust of wind) stays on the surface of the comb. Making it easy to collect. and dispose of.

Cons:
-DOESN'T LOCK into position, so, I'd be mid combing my dogs and the blade would slowly crawl back inside and I'd only realize it since it would start to feel smooth, or there wasn't the expected resistance. SO you have to develop a combing method where your thumb sits behind the slider to keep the blades from retracting.
-CHUNKY, not bad for IN-HAND feel, but they made this out to be pocketable, it's not. I mean it is if you have baggy pants or cargo pockets. The thing is about 4x2x1 inches. It's that 1in thickness that kind of hurts the pocketability of this. THOUGH, if you're throwing this in a "CARE" bag like a pet version of a "baby" bag, then this isn't so bulky that it's going to greatly consume space.
-Cheap feeling, I know it's not expensive, but it does feel cheap. Like I don't know if this would survive a fall.
-Clogging- while I like that the simple act of retracting the blades pushes the hair out, don't know if the tolerance are there to prevent dander and dead skin from building up and clogging it.
-Questionable Shorthaired issues. I have one dog that is clearly medium haired, It's a dutch Shepherd lab mix; and the other is a foxhound catahoula. The foxhoud thinks the longer tooth blade is painful, but the shorter toothed blade is too short for it to be useful. The Dutch/Lab dog has zero issue with the longer tooth comb.

Tip:
-NOW this might be just logical and common sense to some people, but it took me a while to realize. The best results come from using this product PERPENDICULAR _|_ to the body. I was doing a 45 degree angle and it wasn't catching as much. Also, go with the grain of hair growth not against.

Conclusion:
I think it's a great travel comb, and it's well worth the sticker price. Short haired dogs may not like it and may make it hard to comb them with it, but medium and long will more than be fine.

review_title: Might be the best out there for the $, but not terribly impressed
review_text:
I purchased this unit to replace a 7-year old Norelco trimmer (that had an integral main blade and an integral mini pop-up blade, but no vacuum).

Good Points: Comfortable, not too noisy, even on "Turbo" setting. Strong blades clip everything in sight. Mini trimmer blade is sharp and precise. Guide pops off easily. Comfortable to hold. Vacuum does pick up lots of beard/stache clippings and it's easy to empty clippings,too. Easy to change lengths. Nice travel bag. Battery life excellent (but do NOT overcharge and obey the drain-to-zero recommendations).

Bad Points: Vacuum not strong enough to suck up all clippings...you'll still need to trim over a sink or trash container, which really takes away from the advantage of having the vacuum (even on the Turbo setting). Length indicator needs a stronger click-and-hold ratchet mechanism -- too easy to accidentally change length settings. I miss the pop-up mini trimmer: Having to manually swap out blades is a pain. The trimmer can't stand up, even temporarily...it can only be stored in the bag or lying down.

Summary:
This trimmer might be the best compromise of cost / features / functionality out there, but was disappointed with the vacuum capabilities even on Turbo. I was very impressed by the cutting quality.

It comes with a manual and is easy to use.

Power on by pressing the power button (on the side) for a couple of seconds
Below the power button, there is a PLUS (+) and a MINUS (-) button to turn the temperature up or down. The temperature can be seen on the temperature indicator on the back of the brush and, once you turn it to the max, you can watch the numbers go up until the temperature desired is reached (it goes pretty fast).
The temperature goes up to a max of 230, which is best for thicker and more unruly hair.
The pics I uploaded are pretty self-explanatory.

My hair doesn’t have deep or very tight waves but it gets wavy and frizzy if I just let it dry naturally, which is what I did to test the brush.
I set the brush to the max temperature and just brushed my hair naturally, brushing the same spot a few times but not separating the hair in small sections and brushing small section by small section separately.

I thought that the result was great, as it can be seen in the pictures. That is really my hair, the pictures are from the same section of hair before and after using the brush, and the brush not only straightened the hair but it also made it look silkier.

The brush works wonders for my type of hair.
I can’t guarantee that every kind of hair will have the same exact results and the brush will probably not make very thick hair with very tight and deep waves completely straight, but it will probably straighten and make smoother any kind of hair at least to a certain degree.

review_title: Hard to beat this beard trimmer!
review_text:
I’ve had numerous rechargeable beard trimmers over the years but I just bought my second one of these (slightly different model number but definitely the same device) and I’m so happy with the product that I just had to write this review. (I am not being paid or compensated in any way, shape or form for this review.) A beard trimmer is the only thing I ever shave with. (Blade and electric razors give me razor burn and PFB.) I’ve used this product every other (sometimes every 3rd or 4th) day for 5 years. I use most of the attachments. The nose hair trimming attachment works great for when my nose hair starts to tickle (it’s never nicked me or pulled a hair out). The longest comb attachment is perfect for when my goatee gets too long - takes it right back down to my preferred length. Some of the shorter comb attachments are great for manscaping - although some care needs to be taken in the southern regions. Occasionally, I’ll snap on the foil shaver - for those times when my wife needs my face to be stubble-free (if you know what I mean ;) And it’s pretty much flawless when I use it without any attachments as a substitute for a razor/shaver. I would guess that it leaves my stubble about half a millimeter long (~ 1/64”) and the only time it ever pulls a whisker is when I’m shaving against the grain when my whiskers are too long. (In those situations, I need to cut with the grain first, then I can go against the grain to get a closer shave.)

The fact that it comes with a 5 year warranty is a big selling point. My first one lasted 5 years and 3 days (Is there a timer in there, or what?!) but I’m OK with that. (Obviously - I replaced it with the exact same thing!) $8 per year for shaving is pretty great! I can’t really give any specifics on the battery life but it seems pretty awesome to me. When it was new, I charged it about every 3 weeks or so. As time went by, that went to two weeks, then one, and for the past few months, I’ve had to plug it in and charge it after every use. I was going to try to replace the LiON battery but I couldn’t figure out how to take it apart without destroying the rubber grip around the handle. Speaking of the handle, the grip is so good that it’s hard to get whiskers off of it; I have to use the little cleaning brush that’s included. Needless to say, it has never slipped out of my hand; I’ve never dropped it. For those who are wondering, it runs off battery only. If it’s out of juice, you can’t just plug it in and use it.

If you’ve read the reviews on other beard trimmers, you know it’s a mixed bag out there... under powered, poor battery life, dies after a couple weeks, pulls hair out, etc. Not this one. Highly recommended.

I got this thing when I was working retail, a lot of long shifts standing stock still wih only a single 15 minute lunch break can kinda kill your feet especially when you're heavy. I got this thing to help me deal with the calluses and just oiverall roughness of my feet. By itself it does a great job but even using the black tip if you have feet like mine won't do you much good especially since that low grit means it tends to catch and stop itself due to thesafety feature built in to the device.

So some tips I found are:
Use this once or twice a week. It feels like it's made for that especially with the high grit white tip for fine filing and polishing

Use with a cheap dust mask and away from electronics. Trust me while most dust is dead skin as it is, this thing doesn't so much grind away deadskin and calluses as it vaporizes them. Nothing worse than having to dust a computer or going to check your phone and just realise the horror you've created.

Don't use pressure, the machine does the work for you and applying any pressure, especially witha black tip, will just flat out stop the machine.

And lastly and probably the most important, NEVER STOP MOVING. Even if it's a particurally rough spot or calluses, even if it's on low if you leave it in the same place too long you will give yourself a friction burn or, even worse, take of too much and leave your foot raw. Instead if you want to focus on the same area just rapidly tap the machine aagainst the problem area giving it a second or two to cool off in beteween. For the rest of the areas making sweepng, brushing, or lazy cricular motions work the best

review_text:
I've used Orange Ya Glad for about 2 years prior to this purchase. Been unable to find it in stores anymore, so I was excited to be able to buy again.

This is not a brownish or reddish orange. Even when stores are well-stocked, it's almost impossible to find a true orange. And you can forget about a long-lasting orange. All the long-lasting colors tend to be deep reds or brownish. This orange is bright, but not loud, works well with my skin tone, and makes me look livelier. What works for me to ensure it lasts as long as possible on my lips:

I apply excess amount to my SLIGHTLY damp lips, let it "set" for about 5 minutes. (The dampness allows color to penetrate and drying process allows color to bond with my skin) Then I rub it in with my finger (or built-in smudger), which also removes some of the excess, wait a moment, then blot with dry or slightly damp paper towel (tissue leaves lint). Ends up looking natural, not lipstick-y.

If you're a fan of the glossy look (which can also be beautiful), this probably won't work for you. But if you're into mattes and oranges, this one's hard to beat.

review_title: Great Idea, Needs Some Fine Tuning
review_text:
I own a foot filer (Amope-style) already and was intrigued by an electric nail filer. The product came well-packaged and with some toe seperators, which was a nice bonus. I also appreciated that it comes in a plastic, TSA-type storage pouch.

As for the product itself, there is still some work to do before it's a great product. Firstly, the fact that they do not offer refills yet is a huge deterrent. I've only used mine a few times and the heads are still functioning adequately, but soon I'm sure they won't (particularly the filer) and then it will be useless until they offer refill file heads.

Secondly, the file head itself could be of better quality, in terms of filing power. The buff and shine ones are pretty good, but not amazing, as it still takes a little longer than I'd expect to get great results.

Finally, because everything just work "okay", the end result is perfectly fine. Fine is not bad, but I can achieve a better, more fine tuned result with a quality multi-way filing block in only slightly more time. Changing the file heads vs using 1 block for my hands, it's a no brainer I'm better off just using the block. I have found the buff & shine heads useful on my toes, though, for a quick shine boost when I'm in-between polish and letting my toenails breathe. For my toes, the speed of the machine is a little helpful to be bent over lslghtly less long.

All in all it is a pretty okay little device, but for the price it's not quite "ready for prime time". I can only see this being beneficial to those with hand problems, such as carpal tunnel, arthritis, etc, because then not having to grip a block and make a repeated motion for so long would be helpful.

Packaging: The brush comes in an attractive box, so you can give it as a gift. The brown stripes in the resin give the impression of lacquered wood, and the silver-colored aluminum alloy trim pieces are without blemish. It’s a good-looking brush. And it fits nicely in the brush holder I have. Some of the advertising copy could use a good going over--it's awkwardly written ("best gift for gentleman"???).

Performance: For this price, you can get badger bristles. For more money, you will get softer bristles, and more of them. This is a modest-sized brush, but it is adequate for creating, holding, and spreading lather. When I used it, I could feel a couple of bristles poking at my face. Most of them were soft, but these few made the experience less than ideal. On a second use, they seemed a bit softer (but still noticeable), so perhaps over time the lanolin in the soap will work some magic. But on my more-expensive brushes, this was never a problem.

Value: A higher price is no guarantee of better quality, but my experience over many years of using a variety of shaving brushes says you will get more if you pay more. Still, this brush does work. And it is three, four, even ten times cheaper than other, softer badger brushes. My advice is to splurge on your brush and economize elsewhere. review_title: This skeptic is a true believer
review_text:
I'd like to start of by stating that I did not buy this as a medicinal product. I had already ordered this when a mosquito entered my home. I had two types of off repellent. One was in a pump bottle that I had previously used and the other an aerosol can. The pump just ran out so I used the aerosol can which my son probably almost finished. I usually say to spray our cloths, hats or supplies like sleeping bags and sheets, not our skin. I was in my home with a tank top night shirt since it's summer so I sprayed it on my hands and rubbed it on my arms and legs and broke out all over. I didn't think it was that bad at first, but it kept getting worse to the point I was ready to see a dr. I tried witch hazel, kosher activated charcoal, aloe, eucalyptus, tea tree, lavender and probably something else.

This body scrub came right on time. I figured, I tried everything else I cud think of, why not this. I washed, then applied the exfoliating scrub and let it sit on my skin for a couple of minutes. I would have left it longer, but I had an appt. to attend. To my amazement, by the end of the shower, the hives were almost even with my skin although I still itched terribly. I figured there was hope. Later in the day the itchiness lessened to the point of almost being totally gone and the hives didn't pop back up from me scratching. I never knew coffee was good for the outside of the body.

I am a skeptic and when I find something remarkable like this product and charcoal which we use for various things, I tell everyone I can about it. I'm a believer.

2016- I'm back for an update, sorry I took a while to get update. Turns out, I did react to the OFF, although there was no mosquito. The itching was stress related and the OFF brought out the hives. UPDATE: Since writing the previous five star review, the straightener stopped turning on after maybe ten uses. Currently in the process of seeking a refund.

I'm surprisingly pleased. I have long wavy (3A) hair. And it's thick. Super thick. Like, "I have to make my own ponytail holders because the regular ones aren't big enough" thick. And I live in Houston where our humidity can best be described as "lol good luck." Suffice to say, it's a little bit of a problem especially, during the wet season. I decided it was time to start looking a little bit more polished, and to that end I did some research and saw some really good videos on similar products and was directed here because of the low price and good ratings. Reader, it works. The temperature gauge is in celcius, but that wasn't really a problem. I used it on 205-210 and it only took me about 10 minutes to get my hair flat. And when I say "flat" I'm not talking about pin straight, which I had been a little afraid of. If I'd gone up to the 235 that may have happened, but 205 was just about perfect to leave my hair just a hint of a curl at the ends that looks like I intentionally put it there. I'd actually been concerned about that, because the last time I used a straightener I was in high school and I remember it gave me those super flat ends that look like you've straightened it. This is a much more natural look. I experimented with a few different things and what worked best for me was brushing my bangs straight up to give them a little more volume and then the rest of it I just brushed like it was a regular hairbrush. No sectioning hair, no going back with a curling iron to put texture back in, and no burns! The little rubber dealies do their job well, and I was able to touch them with the palm of my hand with no discomfort at all. It even got the super coarse curls around the back of my neck with no problems. I can run my fingers through my hair like a regular person without stopping to untangle anything!

My only quibble would be that the location of the buttons (right on the handle) made it difficult to use without accidentally turning it off or adjusting the pressure, but it does make a nice loud beep when it happened so it was more of an annoyance than anything else and it may be one of those things that gets easier once you're used to it.

review_title: Half the cost, but more convenient than a regular Sonicare
review_text:
Pros: half the cost of a Sonicare w/charger, less bulky
Cons: None so far

First of all, I should state that I have owned this product for over a year, and I am still giving it five stars.

Here's why: I had a Sonicare Advance for about three years and it worked well during that time, but at the end of those three years I had to keep it in the charger at all times or it would die in the middle of brushing. I was sick of lugging around the bulky charger any time I traveled, so when I saw the AA-battery model at Target for $40 I scooped it up.

Now instead of having to rely on an internal battery and a charger, I just keep four rechargeable AAs that I swap out when one pair dies. This isn't something I have to do very often--a pair of AAs lasts about a month (that's with two two-minute brushings a day). I have also not had any water damage, so the brush still works as great as my old Sonicare ever did. I do try not to get water on the brush and dry the entire unit whenever I finish using it. In addition, I take it apart once every two or three months and swab the O-ring with alcohol to keep it clean. This seems to be all of the maintenance needed to keep it in top condition.

So, if you want a good Sonicare brush that takes up less space and is easier to travel with, I highly recommend this model. I recommend cleaning it once in a while and trying to keep water out of the insides. I acknowledge this might not help if you get a bad unit (as many reviewers seem to have gotten), but mine has been great and I figure it can't hurt!

UPDATE: I have now owned it for a year-and-a-half and it still goes a month on two AA rechargeables. Even though I stopped doing the maintenance described above it's still working like new.

review_title: You can wear this for days.
review_text:
If you're looking for a lip product that really, truly only needs to be applied once a day, this is it. This is my second LipTint from LA Splash (The other was Bellatrix/Belladonna) and both of these have stayed on my lips through 48 hours of wear until I decided to remove them. If you've never used an LA-Splash LipTint, the first thing you're going to say about them is that they're super drying. I've found that the drying effect is really what keeps this stuff attached to your lips until you decide to remove it. My best advice is to keep your lips in good condition before its use. review_title: Not quite my grandfather's shaving brush
review_text:
My maternal grandfather passed away some 40 years ago. After my mother returned from her out-of-state trip to be with her mother and bury her father, she gave me a small box containing some of his personal belongings. Among them was his Ever Ready PBT300 shaving brush. I had no use for it at the time. As I unpacked after a recent move I rediscovered this item and decided to use it. It was really enjoyable, so after a few months I decided granddad's brush should be properly retired and I should get my own. Since they no longer manufacture Ever Ready's, I looked here at Amazon. This was the brush I decided upon. It's ok.

It is definitely NOT my grandfather's brush - quality-wise. Grand dad was a farmer, and not a gentleman farmer. So he would not have paid a lot for his. So I thought this one might be similar in quality. I was wrong. It's very stiff. It does not do a great job with the soap lather. It also arrived with a very strong, musky aroma in the bristles. This is probably what badgers smell like. But as I am a native of southern California and we don't need no stinkin' badgers here, I am not positive. This aroma was also transferred to my face as well, for the first month of use. Just prior to the musky animal aroma disappearing, I was frustrated enough with the smell on me all day to look for another brush. Since my grandfather's brush had no aroma I knew it was possible to have one that was aroma - free. But was it a matter of quality or simply a matter of time?

I purchased a $70 Vulfix brush, hand-made on the Isle of Man in the UK.

[...]

It is much more like granddad's in color, feel, and use. It lathers very nicely. It's very soft on the face. It holds a lot of water. There was a slight smell (nothing at all like the SimplyBeautiful smell)that was gone after the 2nd use. If you are thinking about going with a shaving brush (and I LOVE mine and will only go back to the can for short travel trips), my advice is to spend the money and get one that will last for a few decades (like the Vulfix) and avoid the "badgery" smell - although it did eventually go away. I haven't made the decision to also go with the straight razor. I figure I will give the EMTs in the area a break and stick with the safety razor.....

review_title: Provides subtle, consistent improvement. Effects aren't striking -- but it works.
review_text:
I received a discounted sample of this product to provide a review on amazon.

I am a healthy 64-year old male with skin that appears tighter and healthier than that of many peers. While I tanned during the first half of my life, I phased it out during the second. I only use lotion under my eyes where skin is noticeably loose and darker than the rest. Over the past five or six years -- part of this is genetic -- the skin at the front of the neck has become especially loose, while the furrowed lines on my forehead have begun to look alarming. I wanted to try Puressant Neck Firming Cream to see what effect it might have on these two issues.

After a three-week trial, during which I applied the product at least once per day, I've seen a subtle but real tightening of the skin on my neck, which appears to have reached maximum effect. I will assume that to continue this trend I might have to use the product indefinitely, but received no indication from product instructions about this. In any case, there are few products I use indefinitely and particularly those with such an extensive list of known and unknown ingredients. Having said that, I might use the product at intervals to reduce symptoms periodically.

The product has had no effect on my wrinkly forehead, at least not yet. I'll just have to live with it.

The cream has a clean, subtle fragrance (I wish it had none) and rather heavy consistency: A little goes a long way. I've not yet noticed any staining of clothes after application nor any side effects. If not for its moisturizing qualities, I might have awarded this product three stars, but it generates enough cosmetic improvement at a low price to merit four.

review_title: I really wanted this product to work but...
review_text:
for me it was an unqualified failure.

I am trying to treat the knuckle of my right ring finger. It is arthritic and I have treated it very successfully in the past at a clinic that, among other things, used a paraffin bath. The bath was by far the most effective part of my therapy. I didn't want to have something so large to store at home so thought these gloves would be perfect.

I am unable to relate to other reviewers who mention the gloves fit almost any hand comfortably. I'm not sure how hands are sized but I can tell you I wear a men's right hand golf glove, size medium and it is a tight fit. The next size up would be the Cadet which, based on the sizes offered at the golf store fits right in the middle of men's sizes. Golf shops allow you to try gloves on without requiring purchase so this may be a good method to see if your hand will fit this product.

The first Paraffin Hands glove I tried would not allow my right ring finger more than half way into the finger of the glove. My little finger would only go in to its space by about 25%. Not wanting to force the issue, I left the glove alone and waited the prescribed 10 minutes. No benefit. The second time I tried the same glove, the plastic at the side of the middle finger ripped through to the inside wax while I was trying to get the glove to fit better. Again no benefit after 10 minutes.

The second Paraffin Hands glove fit much better, with the ring finger going in to its space about 75% and the same for the little finger. The other fingers went in about 90% being about 10% away from the tip of the glove and the space between fingers also being about 10% away from the palm of my hand. Gently pushing the glove toward my palm to get the best fit caused another break in the plastic of the middle finger so it followed its predecessor into the garbage.

This product still sounds like a good idea but the manufacturer really needs to enlarge the size although I am somewhat skeptical there is enough wax in the glove to give one the benefit I am looking for.

review_text:
Yes, the packaging is gimmicky and I totally fell for it, but I make no apologies. I bought 3 shades--PK01, CR01, and OR01--and they're all quite nice. That said, the PK01 is a bit lighter than I expected so I'll probably get more wear out of the other two.

The tints are pretty long-lasting. I was able to wear the OR01 all day yesterday, and even through lunch and drinking mugs of tea I didn't need to touch it up 'til the end of the day. (And, truthfully, since it was the end of the day and there was still a hint of color, I was lazy and just didn't bother.) The tints aren't noticeably drying, either--although I'm a balm addict and usually put some on over the color throughout the day. Luckily, this doesn't seem to have a terribly detrimental effect on the color. There is a slight taste, which is neither unpleasant nor pleasant--I didn't especially like it, but it didn't bother me. I'm not a wine drinker, but my guess is they don't really taste like wine, just kind of fruity.

The only other true tints/stains I've used are the Tony Moly ones and I think these compare favorably to those in terms of ease of application (I think these are more forgiving), durability, drying, and taste (the TMs had a more chemical taste). I don't dislike the TM's, but these are just better, IMO.

I'd recommend these tints, and will probably buy again, especially to try out the other other colors.

review_title: Shows AMAZING color on brown hair!
review_text:
I love love LOVE this dye!!!!
(TL;DR at bottom)
I have medium to dark brown hair, and the thought of bleaching it terrifies me because the last time I bleached my hair in high school I absolutely FRIED it. I was pretty hesitant to see how well this pink would show up on my dark hair without bleaching it first. Boy was I surprised.
First of all, I have a LOT of hair. I needed 3 bottles of dye to cover my whole head. Hopefully you can use my photos to compare your hair length to mine and use what I said to help you determine how many bottles you’d need to buy.
I didn’t just pour it in my hands and rub it all over my hair, I actually sectioned out my hair piece by piece to make sure I got the dye on every last bit of hair as evenly as possible. This whole process took about 2 hours. Yes, it was exactly as awful as it sounds. Man were my arms tired.. After I finished dying it, I put all of my hair up in a shower cap / bonnet and let it sit for 5 whole hours. Excessive? Probably lol.
I swear I remember hearing once a long time ago that when you wash out hair dye in the shower you’re supposed to keep washing it til the water runs clear. Well I was in the shower for a good 40 minutes shampooing the life outta my hair before I just gave up and got out the shower lol. My shower water continued to run pink every time I washed my hair for at least a good 2 to 3 weeks.
Oh and as for the washing?? Yeah I hate cold water so I never did any of that stuff that you’re supposed to do. I continued to shower every to every other day, and I used warm to hot water every time. Yeah yeah I know the color won’t last as long, but screw a cold shower. I also switched to using Herbal Essences Color Me Happy shampoo.
[EDIT: I am now aware that Color Me Happy is actually horrible for colored hair. That shampoo still contains SULFATES, which is the ENEMY OF HAIR DYE. So yeah make sure you read the ingredients on your shampoo bottles carefully, because clearly Herbal Essences is a bunch of LIARS.]
So after 1 month of warm showers and Herbal Essences, the third photo is what I was left with. I’m honestly incredibly happy!!! The pink definitely faded a lot, but there was still enough pink in my hair to the point where if a stranger on the street saw me they’d be able to say “that girl has pink(ish) hair.” This dye has exceeded all of my expectations.
One thing I’d like to add, though. This dye does seem to stain plastic showers. It kinda comes off when you scrub it with acetone (nail polish remover) and some abrasive cleaners. Over time the stains definitely do fade. But I just wanted to give y’all the heads up in case your shower turns pink and you can’t scrub it all off in one night.
I’m about to re-dye my hair with this same dye as soon as I finish writing this review, so it might even be brighter and last even longer this time!
~TL;DR~
1. Shows up great on medium brown hair, but I let it sit for 5 hours before washing.
2. Long hair (or at least mine) requires 3 bottles.
3. Stains plastic showers.
4. Color stays in nicely after a month of daily warm showers and using Herbal Essences Color Me Happy shampoo & conditioner.

I've been using a corded version of the Braun Silk Epil for a few years now so I was super excited to try this cordless version. Truth be told, I haven't used the rotating brush head yet, but I LOVE the epilator! They've made so many improvements to the design since I received my last one. The unit charges pretty quickly. I didn't time it but it couldn't have been more than 20 minutes after plugging it in from completely dead that I found it fully recharged. The contour of the unit is also improved, and I love the changes to the on/off dial. It was very easy to accidentally slide the on/off switch on my older model, but this requires two fingers so you won't be accidentally turning it on or off when you don't intend to. The new contouring head is also fantastic. The older model did not pivot with the contour of your legs, but this one works perfectly. The rounded epilator head is protected by the pivoting frame so that when it meets your skin, it is always in the right position. I had jabbed myself a few times with the older model as I was getting used to it. Not painful, but annoying and not effective. It's impossible to do it wrong with this new pivoting head. Overall, I don't feel that it's less painful than previous versions (and underarm hair is still excruciating and I will not do it!) but if you keep up with it every couple of days the pain is extremely minimal. The worst will be when you've let the hair grow out for a while and then do it all at once, and even then it's bearable. I'm glad to see they removed the cold pack from this version because it never helped with the pain despite the claims that it would and the ice on my legs was more uncomfortable than the actual epilating. The weight is just right, not too heavy to fatigue your hands but not too light as to feel like you don't have precise control. And of course, my skin stays smoother longer and epilating removes a lot of the dark spots that are left behind with regular shaving of my very fair skin. Definitely worth picking up for first timers or if you have an older corded version!

Finally some of the single pins have a raised design that runs the full length of the too-short pin. The problem is that the raised design catches at my hair and pulls. You might get the pin in, and enough of them to hold your hair up, but it may come loose, carrying part of your hair with it, making it harder to reinsert. Intentionally pulling these pins out is just as bad.

So if you are fine paying the total price for the double-tined pins in the collection, it's all good. If not, and your hair is fine with the shorter smooth pins, it's still good.

I do not recommend using the pins with the full length design. Ouch.

Bought these because I was looking for something to massage my itchy gums. Though my dentist has not said anything about gingivitis, I am pretty sure I’m borderline there. I have very sensitive gums and have been struggling for years to find toothbrushes that do not stab at them and make them bleed. One time, I tried the floss-tip toothbrush’s & they were SO sharp, they stabbed tiny holes in my gums & they got infected. Since then, I’ve tried Extra Soft Toothbrush from Di Qiu Ren (which was so dense, it did not dry, and got moldy very fast), back to my regular soft bristle toothbrush, which still irritates my gums and makes them bleed, and these silicone bristle brushes.

These silicone bristle brushes are very gentle on sensitive gums and have not cause ANY bleeding. Though, it does take longer to get plaque off the teeth, it’s great for my sensitive gums. The downfall, is if you brush your teeth too soon after eating oily foods, the residue sticks to the brush and it very difficult to get off. Most of the time, I just throw it away and use a new one. So far, one brush lasts about a month before it gets residue on it or starts smelling weird.

I don’t know if these are good for oral hygiene, but so far, my gums appear better and have built up a tolerance to contact & appear less sensitive to flossing and brushing. I will likely purchase these again to help with my gums, but will continue looking for cleaning alternatives for teeth.
