review_title: Good basic shaving soap, lightly scented.
review_text:
I've only tried a few different shaving soaps in my time wet shaving. TOBS (Taylor of Old Bond Street) Sandalwood has been my go-to for a few years now. My only nitpick is the fragrance...which is an oddly clean and powdery sandalwood that projects across my entire bathroom. The fragrance also has some decent longevity, and I can still pick up notes of it while I'm getting dressed and putting on cologne, which it sometimes clashes with. I guess my takeaway is that I needed a change from that scent. Mitchell's Wool Fat soap seemed like a good alternative, and from what I could tell from skimming forums and reviews, it doesn't smell nearly as strongly as TOBS.

I'm pleasantly surprised so far. It lathered in my hard water relatively well. Just bloomed it in hot water for a minute beforehand and went to work on it with a medium body boarhair brush. The soap had a slicker feel than I'm used to and the lather had slightly less structural integrity than TOBS but my shave didn't seem to suffer for it. Like I usually do, I used the remaining lather I'd made to wash the rest of my face, which worked like a charm. The post shave was just okay. I honestly felt like I'd done a worse job on my neck than I actually had. Might have been the switch to a tallow soap, might have been the lanolin but my neck skin felt a little roughed up and gummed up, even after my post-shave alum block and witch hazel. As my skin dried and everything calmed down, I could finally tell that I'd actually gotten an extremely close shave and had miraculously avoided any damage in the usual spots around my adams apple. Good stuff.

The fragrance is also a nice surprise. The Kent company, which markets and sells a repackaged version of this same soap in India claimed it had elements of Pine, Patchouli, Lavender, Musk, Cloves, Nutmeg, Cedar, Sandalwood. I now see what the folks on the forums meant when they called that BS.
It does have a clean lavender note up front, a bit of soft powdery musk in the middle and a nebulous slightly woodsy note hanging out somewhere in the background. All the other notes they claimed are MIA though. This is a very subdued version of a classic old-school barbershop scent. No long distance projection, no longevity past the end of the shave.

Actually, now that I smell my hands hours later, I can actually detect a bit of that musky woodsy accord hanging around. After it managed to trigger a sense memory of helping my aunt shear sheep as a kid, I now realize that I'm actually smelling raw lanolin. So I guess with that in mind, I'd have to reframe this soap as mostly smelling like lavender and lanolin.

Which I could definitely get used to.

ok - now that we have covered that - the actual product. it's sooooo easy to use. the process is so simple and easy. the directions are super easy to understand and follow and there are pictures included. it's pretty quick - you can get through it all within an hour once you get started on the actual product. just follow the directions.

then for maintenance between treatments there is a shampoo and conditioner provided. these are EXTREMELY thick! like the conditioner is so crazy thick it's almost too difficult to get it out of the bottle. it's a workout. but it's all good to help maintain though.

now - the results. i'm not disappointed at all. i know it's working. it's not a crazy perma-straight situation though. this is NOT salon results. let me repeat that ... NOT salon results. i have super natural curly hair - i can still wash my hair curly. the same amount of curls as i have always had. when i do wear it curly though, i also still have the same amount of frizz. it's sad and true. that said though - it's when wear it straight that the product shows it's worth! the picture i have posted it right after coming after getting caught in the rain. in the past my hair would just revert back to the full on curl, no waves just the game of 'how big is my hair gonna grow?' watch party. this time though ... i ended up with a style that i actually like! something i could easily still get away with wearing for the rest of the day/evening. as rainy and muggy as it has been lately - i can dig this and appreciate it through and through.

so all that said - do i wish it did a bit more for the curly hair frizz ... yes. but for the price and the fact that i will probably get 4 treatments out of this set - i think the system is worth for the investment - cost and time.

this is the 3rd system i've tried in around 5 months - and i finally feel like something is working.  my hair is truly starting to feel a bit thicker, and some of the thinner spots appear to be a little less thin.  i wish i had some super profound before and after photos - i do not, a lot of it is in how my hair feels, and to be honest the results are slow coming - i might have a very drastic result in 6 months, and i would definitely update then, but for now i feel gradual changes and i am thrilled about it.  age and stress have thinned my hair a ton - i hate it, so any iota of added thickness is going to be thrilling for me.  now ... i just need to find a way for all of the new hairs to stop growing in gray.

review_title: Heat feels nice, but otherwise not impressed.
review_text:
I wanted to like this product, but overall I'm not particularly impressed with it. The lipstick design is cute, but the entire device is covered in a cheap hard plastic that attracts dust and smudges, and doesn't feel particularly durable. The gemstone tip looks dull and cloudy, and has bubbles within it. Not a pretty pink rose quartz like in the product photos. I'm not really certain what the difference between the red and blue light modes is; They both seem to head the gemstone head. The 'button' being a touch sensor makes it easy to switch modes on accidental during use. Perhaps one of the biggest flaws of this device is that the motor is in the base, and the vibrations are extremely weak. This means that you can barely feel the vibrations at all during use. Additionally, the charging port is completely exposed on the bottom of this device with no water-resistant cover, so there's the potentially to accidentally get liquid on it if using this product to encourage product absorption.

Overall, I'm highly disappointed with this product. I think it's a really cool idea, and the heat emitted from the stone feels nice, but I feel like the overall execution of this product is poorly done.

review_title: Pretty good spa set, but a bit on the expensive side.
review_text:
Overall, I'm fairly satisfied with my order of this spa set. The first thing I noticed is that everything smells fantastic! A strong coffee fragrance wafts from everything in this kit, and all three body products contain real coffee. The scrub was my personal favorite scent-wise; I find it smells just like a caramel lattee.

The body bar is nourishing and non-drying, but it is exfoliating due to the coffee grounds, so I wouldn't recommend it for everyday use. I do personally wish it was a tad larger, as it melts down quickly during typical usage.

The scrub is quite dense, as it doesn't contain added liquid. However, this means you get a lot for your money, as you only need to use a little bit on damp skin to get good exfoliation. I like the addition of almond and coconut oil, as it keeps it from being overly harsh, and makes it quite hydrating.

A little goes a long way with the bath soak. I love using it in a foot bath; It leaves my feet feeling nice and soft, and the aroma is relaxing and pleasant. It does dye the water a light brown due to the coffee, however.

I like the candle, but I'd consider it my least favorite out of this set. It has a nice burn time for its size, and it's in a beautiful black candle tin with a lid. However, I found the amount of scent it provided while burning to be underwhelming.

Overall, I really like this spa kit, and I think it'd be fantastic for any coffee lover. It's a little expensive at the current price, but if the candle was a little stronger, and the bath bar was a little larger, then this would be a five-star product.

review_title: Super sharp and easy to use!
review_text:
I have had problems with acne all my life, and I find relief in being a picker and a popper. I also have a teenage daughter who follows the picking and popping type behavior. I've found these tools make it so much easier to get to the hard to reach or deeply embedded blackheads and blemishes and reduce the amount of scarring and marks left by using other things that weren't reall designed for this purpose. They really do help the removal process without damaging the surrounding skin or spreading the bacteria which can lead to even more breakouts.
This blemish kit comes with six double sided tools that are made from 100% stainless steel, a zippered leather storage case with elastic loops which hold the tools in place, and an instruction sheet on how to use and care for all of the instruments. This makes the storage and sanitation of these instraments easy and convenient.The tools are definitely of good quality, four of the six have textured grips and are easy to hold on to, the other two are squared. The lance and spoon extractors are stored in the grip, and you simply unscrew them to remove from grip, then choose the desired tool and screw it back in to assemble for use. I really like the lance provided instead of the needle tip lancet, and it's just as sharp. The leather case is nice and small so it would be easy to take in your purse or overnight bag if you should want to travel with it. The elastic loops are tight which makes it a little difficult to replace them, however, I like they have a secured fitted placement.
The directions are very clear and basic. It isn't hard to figure out which tool works best for each blemish. Honestly, everyone is different so I don't believe there is one way or one tool that would be more useful then another. That's why this varity is so great.
For the best results, it is important to sterilize the tools you will be using with alcohol, and to wash your hands and face with cleanser and warm/hot water. This step is necessary to open the pores and gain maneuverability. Find the appropriate tool and place it over the blackhead and press gently, removing the nastiness by force. If you press too hard you could damage the skin. If you are dealing with a whitehead, puncture it with the lance for removal. It's important to wipe the tool with alcohol prior to moving on to the next blemish, as to not spread bacteria. After you finish with the extractions, it is important that you cleanse your face using cold water. This rinse will help in closing the pores to avoid them becoming clogged again. Don't forget to sterilize any used instruments prior to putting them back in the storage case, you don't want to spread the bacteria.

I read a lot of good reviews on this hair care product and decided to try it for myself. First, I have fine hair that tangles easily after washing and detangler products are a must and I'm quite particular about what I use. I actually prefer spray over cream products, but over all the Total Vitamin Leave-in cream did distribute through my hair better then most creams I've used, but it didn't help entirely with my tangles. I cant really comment on the effectiveness of the Keratin Heat Protector since I don't cook my hair with blow driers, and curling or flat irons. Overall, these products are okay, but nothing to write home about. My biggest concern was when I was using these 3 products, my hair seemed to fall out...and I mean hair loss by the clumps. Never had this happen before. I didn't panic right away and blame it on the products, but after a week or so, I discontinued using Milania products and went back to my prior products and immediately noticed no hair falling out. So did the Milania products have something to do with my hair falling out? I can't say for certain, but I did read a review here that someone else experienced hair falling out too. I understand that everyone's hair & scalp is different and mine seem to react poorly, so use your own judgement call on whether you want to try these products.

Aside from "possible" hair loss, the products smelled incredible, distributed easily in hair, and didnt leave any residue feeling in my hair. So my final judgement on Milania hair care is that it's basic stuff and, in my opinion, overrated and didn't live up to all the hype. It didn't get my tangles out with ease, didn't leave my hair silky smooth soft and frizz-free as boasted. Its okay, but not "great"...expecially for the price. There's other products out there that work just as good or better for less money.

I have dark, thick hair on my head but for whatever unfortunate genetic reason, I have very light and thin eyebrows, and fill them in with makeup every single day. I have never dyed them before. This dye darkened them to match my hair perfectly, and my method of application gave me the perfect shape with no skin staining or irritation.

First of all, I only used about 1/4 of the powder in the capsule because I could tell that would probably be more than enough (and it was), so this stuff is going to last forever.

Instead of washing my face beforehand, I used a dry microfiber cloth to wipe off my eyebrow area as clean as I could. I think the fact that I didn't wash my face meant that my skin had a small layer of oil on it for protection against staining and irritation. A little oil also will not hinder the hair coloring process.

I used the included application brush, putting very small amounts of the dye on the brush and applying it in light, careful strokes. The movement is like sketching in a sketchbook instead of drawing solid lines all at once, and I did not have a pile of dye on my brows at the end.

I know that with my hair, I need to leave dye on it for a long time, so I left this on for 10 minutes. I rinsed the dye off with cool water to avoid opening up my pores. I checked my brows and thought they could be a little darker, so I re-applied and left on for another 5-10 mins. Total of 15-20 mins.

Finally, I washed it off for good with a gentle unscented soap, using my fingernails to help get all the dye off and exfoliate the skin underneath and around my brows, so I was left with no stains.

And that was that. I have eyebrows now! I can even TOUCH them! I can't believe I never tried this before, this will be a staple in my life now.

It looks the same, but the "scent" is now completely atrocious!  There's not a trace of that barely "fruity" scent anymore.  It has turned into a putrid smell, and I almost can't even bear to use it.  It seems as if almost overnight it turned from barely fruity to entirely unbearable.  I can't even put my finger on what it smells like now.  The best way to describe the smell is "chemical," which leads me to think this may not be as natural of a product as the company claims.  I've rated this two stars only because it seems to have done something for the better, but I am going to switch to another product.  This is much too expensive for it to turn stale so quickly.

review_title: Hair frizzes/unravels quickly but still looks nice...for a minute
review_text: Received the hair on time. Ordered 2 groups (which were 6 packs in all), but I still don't think it was quite full enough. The hair comes in 3 (or in my case 6) individual packs (PIC) with a twist wire going through. Care must be taken to not let each piece slip off until you are used to the loop because you may lose the grip of the loop. The loop holes are pretty small so you'll lose some strands if you cant get a hold of the loop properly because the hair will unravel if you manipulate it too much (PICs). Also the hair is a bit too shiny to look natural (PIC) although I still got compliments. It comes with hair clips and a loop needle package (PIC) with each order so I wound up with two needles and two sets of clips. At this point I've had it in one week and though it still looks ok, there is a lot of frizzing up at the root so I'm not going to be able to wear it for a month like i planned, I can tell already. Didn't notice any real shedding though the unraveling makes up for it. It'd probably better to order an extra pack if you want to wear it for a while since you should switch out the individual locs as they fray. Lastly the metal clips that are included are nice to cap off the look, but they tarnish pretty quickly.  The hair is veeery soft and 18" is the length I wanted it to be.

review_title: Good and bad - But I have notes to increase success.
review_text:
I applied this to my 5 year olds blonde hair. I did not want to spend a future at a salon because.... she is five!
She DOES love the end result but I will say, if you want a successful process I have several important notes.
1. I can NOT speak to the bleach because we did NOT use it. I hear BAD things about it.... so, read other reviews if applicable.
2. Product is messy! That said; count on the NEED for 2 person application. Do NOT attempt to self apply this product. Will absolutely regret it and ruin your home and clothes.
3. Count on purchasing extra items AND plan for 3 hours from prep start to finish. I will explain why.
EXTRA ITEMS: This product will ABSOLUTELY stain hand, face and scalp. Purchase: extra gloves, vaseline, and hair dye removal!
GLOVES: It only comes with one crappy pair of gloves. For best result, swing by Sally's beauty and buy SEVERAL good pairs of gloves. OR buy some of those thick bathroom cleaning gloves that come to your elbows. this way you can use them and take them off and on easily to both apply AND rinse hair.
VASELINE: COMPLETELY coat ears, forehead, neck, etc with a THICK coat of vaseline to avoid staining
DYE REMOVAL: Swing by sally's and buy a bottle of hair dye remover BEFORE you start. This will get on skin and you will NOT get it off otherwise.
EXTRA TIME TO APPLY: I have applied this product in 4 different colors to both my own hair and others hair. I have NEVER gotten good coverage without having to apply it TWICE. (including this application. pictures attached are product of applying BOTH colors twice for an hour each time) For the vibrant color you will want, count on applying, waiting an hour to rinse. Blow dry and reapply for ANOTHER hour. Do not think you will "quickly" apply this product like a box of normal 20 minute color. You will be disappointed.

Overall, as I said, my daughter is happy with the turn out and I saved money so in my case, it worked out.
However, I have experience with this product so it was successful based on ALL the above notes.
Also, I DID experience severe staining to her scalp and it will NOT come off so far even with the hair dye remover. I did not apply it close to scalp but she is young and her hair is so thin, it bleed right through and left big nasty looking spots all over her little head. That said, I ONLY applied this to the underneath of her hair as an ombre look... so I can keep working on getting it off in the next few days.
I would be much more upset if I had this all over her head.

review_title: Easy way to accessorize, perfect for summer
review_text:
I love jewelry tattoos and am so glad to finally see them at a better price here on Amazon! (I paid over $20 for 2 sheets before on various sites) I always get compliments whenever I wear these and can't wait to take them with me on a beach vacation. These tattoos almost look like individual stenciled designs that took hours instead of quick jewelry tattoos that took seconds to apply.

The instructions are very easy - remove the clear sheet, place tattoo face down on dry skin, wet tattoo with sponge or towel, remove after 30 seconds and let dry. I've used these as "cuffs" around my upper arms, as "bracelets" around my wrists, as "necklaces", "ankle bracelets" - you name it. I also like placing 2 small designs by the collarbone. There's no right or wrong with these and just depends on the look you're trying to achieve.

I wore these for several days in a row and saw no skin irritation. They can last several days if you place them somewhere where the skin doesn't stretch/twist too much and if you avoid soap, sunscreen, lotions, oils, etc. near the tattoos. Since I typically use one or several of these products, my tattoos only lasted a day or two before fading and peeling. Tattoos can be removed by soaking the area in some kind of oil for about a minute (baby, olive, argan - I use whatever I have around) and then carefully scrubbing them off.

This is one of those products what tries to wow you with great packaging and high quality materials. Seriously, the packaging for this thing is better than a $450 watch I got recently. It's top notch.

RAZOR HANDLE - C
This thing is so heavy it borders on ridiculous. It's solid metal. If you dropped it on your foot, it would hurt. It feels good in your hand until you try to use it. There are no good grip points and the entire thing is smooth. Once it gets wet, it's a nightmare to hold and use.

BLADES - A
The blades are some of the best you'll find. Super close shave and they last a number of shaves. You really can't beat them.

CREAM - F
Garbage. This stuff is better than nothing, but that's about it. I used it once and then threw it out.

BASE - A
Yes you get a base to hold your razor. It's heavy, has a rubber bottom and it stays put.

USEABILITY - D-
Bad. If they have the best blades, how is it bad? The head that holds the blade is so big, that it gets in the way. Why this is not an issue for most parts of your face, it's a big issue when trying to shave under your nose. I had to grab a second razor to reach that area. They went for form over function with this one.

If you want a super heavy razor, that will last forever, then skip this one. You are better off with a blade from Supply. They do a very similar thing. Big high end handle and then try to survive off of the blades. The big difference is, their razor can shave your whole face.

review_title: The Bag Works, But Will It Last?
review_text:
The Gonex hanging toiletry bag works for short weekend trips, though I doubt it would persist through the rigors of camping or a multi-week, international journey. The bag is very lightweight, which is good for a backpack or small suitcase, but the thin materials of the bag appear as though they will wear out pretty quickly, especially when frequently loaded with heavy bottles of body wash, shampoo, and the like. I like that I can hang this bag on the back of a bathroom door (see photo), but the hanger on the bag is plastic, which limits the amount of weight you can hang in this bag.

I seldom fly or make long trips, so the Gonex bag meets my needs on short, overnight trips. If you are a person who camps or takes long journeys, you may want to try something a bit more sturdy and durable.

My biggest tip is to make sure you're applying it somewhere that is going to experience limited movement... avoid joints and go for skin that doesn't wrinkle or bend. This is especially hard with the very large tattoos which there are several in this kit. Unfortunately you won't get much more than a day or two out of those - not because of the quality, but because the natural bending and wrinkling your skin does when you move around causes the tattoos to get wrinkly. I have a graduated bob and bleached (level 12) hair. This means varied lengths, from about 4" to 10", and damaged hair that must be treated very tenderly. Because I favor a smooth underswept style, I was using my flatiron to achieve that look, but first I had to blowdry my hair or my natural wave would still turn through the ironing. A double process is a pain, and the blowdrying takes away the sheen from my hair, making it look lifeless.

The brush iron is easy to hold and does not diminish the hair's sheen. I strongly recommend sectioning your hair, doing a little at a time. Don't try to take a large section and roll it...unless you are very precise, it will be easy to cross-roll as you get it out of your hair, creating a nightmare tangle.

I take a section and hold the end of the hair so the section goes straight up. Then I put the iron under the hair...the stiff bristles keep the iron awaay from my scalp, so no danger of burning myself (unlike my flatiron). I pull the section of hair down over the iron and keep it like that for about 10 seconds (on 'high', and my hair is fine) then I continuously roll the brush through the hair as I bring it down to the end. I keep rolling it as I let the end curl around and roll it up like a regular curling iron.

Because there is no upper grip, there is no danger of getting an indention in the hair. Just beware of cross-rolling the hair.

Also, keep your fingers offf the barrel. Easy to say, but I did burn a fingertip. Now I let the cool plastic end of the roller rest in my left palm for guidance, and keep my fingers well awaay.

I'll post an update if I have more observations.

It has always performed as expected and made my thin, fine hair more manageable and a little fuller feeling.  The last time I ordered it, however, it did not perform or even smell the same as previous purchases.  My hair did not feel clean after shampooing, or more manageable.  In fact, by day two it looked a little greasy.  I subsequently developed dermatitis around my hairline and down my neck to the point where I had to consult a dermatologist.  She suggested it could be my shampoo and told me to stop using this product.  My dermatitis went away and after about a month, I tried using the Paul Mitchell Tea Tree Lemon Sage Shampoo and Conditioner again.  My dermatitis returned almost immediately.  While I suppose I could have developed an allergy to a product I have been using for a couple of years, I question whether this product sold on Amazon is genuine.  I will not order any more cosmetic products from Amazon due to their self-admitted counterfeit problem. Caveat Emptor.

review_title: Good quality, good price, very effective (pleasantly surprised)
review_text:
Bare-bones, just the tools and a case, but the tools are of pretty good quality (I was pleasantly surprised). The sparse packaging is typical of stuff from Asia (just a guess), but you also get the lower price that comes with that. I prefer it that way (less stuff in the landfill).

If you're expecting a manual with it, then this product is probably not for you, safety-wise, and I mean that most respectfully. I guess it might say "Insert in ear, please be super careful". This is the kind of thing they usually don't sell in the US (at least from a big company) due to liability. Especially with the ear, the rule is "Only let a doctor do it" (like it is for so many things). Let me tell you, the doctors I've seen don't want to do it either (would you?). They give you the 'yuk, that's beneath me' look and refer you to earwax drops (which never worked for us). I guess what I mean is that if you're looking at buying this, you've probably tried to clean your ear with other (usually unsuitable) objects (Q-tips, etc) without much success, so you have some experience on what's safe to do and how you might use this. Again, you have to be super careful.

Now my short experience with this is to clean out the wax of another (elderly) person, not my own. I don't need it (yet), tho I suspect it's much more effective when you can see what you're doing, which you cant on yourself. Also, I think by restricting your cleaning to what you can see, you're less likely to go too deep (like you might on yourself). It works really well on dry, flaky wax. On more wet, viscous wax, I cant say. Compared to what I've used before, it's no contest. I'm really happy with it. So much more wax than I've been able to get out before.

There are three tools, each with its own usefulness that is apparent or you can figure out as you go. One is for (dull) scraping (looks like a round paw), one is for twisting/catching loose stuff (bulb-shaped spring), and one seems like a combo of both (looks like a mace w/three ridges). The last one has edges that are a little sharp, which you might need (use gently), but can be painful on the delicate skin of the inner ear. I've seen bleeding from using a Q-tip too much, so be careful.

I would clean these after every use. I use isopropyl alcohol (cheap from walmart).

The plastic case is plain and flimsy, like a throwaway case, but is actually very useful (so don't toss it). You need something to hold the tools, and it's just the right size and transparent too. I need to get better at opening it (press down where the single retaining tab is). There's plenty of places for air to get in to allow the tools to dry. Convenient.

i have used three different types of clips in the salon. i have used smooth metal clips, plastic butterfly clips, and croc clips. the smooth metal clips work well for holding foils in place, but they don't do well for sectioning off large sections of hair. butterfly clips work well for sectioning off hair but not for holding foils in place. butterfly clips are also limited by their size. they come in two sizes but even the larger size isn't always big enough for some sections of hair. croc clips will do everything. they are long enough to hold foils, strong enough to hold large sections of hair (they have the expansion bar that bends to allow them to grip and hold large, bulky sections of hair), and they are versatile enough to be perfect all on their own. with croc clips, i don't have to have some of all the others in my station drawers. croc clips are the other clips all rolled into one. i don't foresee that i will ever use a different clip.

the Rioa croc clips are pretty standard. they are stamped with the brand name of "toni & guy," a well-known name in the styling community. i have purchased several sets of "toni & guy" croc clips from other merchants (including professional beauty supply stores) and the Rioa clips are equivalent to those.

Thank you for reading, and if my review was helpful to you in any way, please click "yes" below.

review_title: A modern classic in the fundamentals of card magic - but get the 2013 edition!
review_text:
A NEW VERSION

I recently picked up the new edition of Oz Pearlman's Born to Perform Card Magic DVD, which was released in 2013. I was curious how it compared with the original DVD that was released in 2003, and in this review I'll summarize what the differences are, and what the contents of the new edition include.

I bought my DVD of the 2013 version directly from the creator, Penguin Magic, but it's also available elsewhere online including at some retailers and sometimes on Amazon. The nice thing is that in addition to sending you the DVD of the new edition, Penguin Magic also gives you access to a digital download of both the 2003 version and the 2013 version, so you get the best of both worlds. Both videos are videos in *.mp4 format, with the 2003 video being 753 MB in size, and the 2013 video being 1.43 GB in size.

LENGTH

The new edition is billed as an updated/expanded version, and that's clearly evident when you compare the length of the two videos:
2003 version: 1 hour 44 minutes
2013 version: 3 hours 48 minutes

DIFFERENCES

So what's the difference exactly? Well for starters, Oz himself is now 10 years older, and has a lot more professional experience under his belt. He has a new look and even a new smile. Everything has been re-filmed and the explanations have been re-done from scratch. Most of the content covers the same material, but not exactly - I'll mention what exactly those differences are in the next section.

CONTENT ON THE ORIGINAL 2003 EDITION ONLY

Not everything that was in the 2003 edition of the DVD is found in the 2013 edition, and several sections from the original have vanished. These are the following:
a) Controls: - Classic Pass; - Hindu Shuffle Pass; - One Handed Top Palm; - Elmsley Count
b) Forces: - Riffle Force

CONTENT ON THE NEW 2003 EDITION ONLY

The new edition is about twice as long, and that's because some of the explanations are more detailed and elaborate, but also because it has some new material. Here's a list of all the new topics:
a) Controls: - Gamblers Cop; - False Overhand Shuffle
b) Forces: - Dribble Force; - Spread Cull Force
c) Flourishes: - Swivel Change
d) Routines: - Slop Shuffle; - Card to Mouth; - Blossom Production

COMPARISON

It's a pity to see some material from the original version left out in the new version, especially the Riffle Force (given its popularity), and the Elmsley Count (given that it is used in so many tricks). I'm also curious why a decision was made to eliminate the Pass, although this is a more advanced move that is typically beyond the scope of beginners, and perhaps that's why it was removed. If material was going to be added, the Glide would have been an obvious addition as a fairly basic sleight, so I'm surprised that this continues to be an omission from what is intended to be a good introduction to fundamentals.

But the additional elements are very solid, and the increased number of routines in the new version will especially be welcome to many people. What I like most, however, is the fact that the sleights and moves are taught in a little more detail, and I think the more elaborate explanations here are very helpful.

Oz himself appears to have lost some of his youthful innocence, and comes across a little more brash and almost over-confident. I'm still not quite sure what to make of his new business suit attired persona, or whether I prefer the younger Oz. But he is still an excellent teacher, and that's really what this video is all about. It's always been an excellent choice for relative beginners looking to get a good handle on the fundamentals of card magic, and overall this enhanced version only makes a good thing even better.

RECOMMENDATION

Oz Pearlman's "Born to Perform Card Magic" DVD has always been applauded for being a great introduction to the fundamentals of card magic, and one of the better entries in this genre. The updated and expanded 2013 edition takes something that is a proven success, and expands it for a new audience that may not be familiar with the original. It still deserves to be one of the top recommendations for new magicians, and continues to be an excellent starting point to give beginners a good head-start with their card magic.

review_title: Works great! Double beachy wave, Heatless curling system.
review_text: This works great! You just have to know how to use it correctly. The double curler band allows you to use less hair on each curler so that the hair dries faster and curls faster. Here IS MY 2 HOURS TO PRETTY CURLS METHOD: Part upper hair at crown of head,  and put hair from the upper head at crown,  in a pony tail for later. Snap the curling system closed, so that there is 2 round circle bands to use to curl with, and put both around head like a double crown head band. Push the top curling band where pont tail is for later use. Separate the bottom layer of hair into two parts... left side and right side and use only the bottom circle band curler for the bottom portion of head. Begin curling in left side by spritzing a little water onto the hair at root and curl it under band tucking it under and around curler one time only and then in next pass, grab a little more hair with it and continue going around the curler band. Keep spritzing new hair with water each time you pick up a new piece of hair and add that hair to the previous end of the one you just curled, until the whole left, bottom  side is done. Then start on the bottom right side of hair. When finished,  the  whole bottom curling band  will be filled with the hair from the lower portion of. Now it's time to take out the pony tail that was  on the grown of head  and put that hair under the second curling band and separate the left side of hair from the right. Start curling the left upper part of head as you did the bottom portion... spritzing small portion of hair with water at root and curling it once around the band and then pick up a little more new hair, spritz it with water and curl together with the former portion around band until all left side is done and now do right side. DO NOT SOAK HAIR.  Only LIGHTLY MIST IT a little with water or it wont dry in 2 hours. Dont curl too big a portion of hair at a time either, or it won't dry in two hours. Wait about 1 hour to 2 hours and remove curlers and you will get beachy type ringlets that are big. It takes about 10 minutes to wind hair around curlers. Lovely curls.

HOWEVER, parents of babies with sensitive skin please note that the scented versions contain SYNTHETIC FRAGRANCE (or at least the pear scent does). I wrote to the manufacturer to inquire about it, and the below is the reply that I got. I thought it was pretty sketchy that the manufacturer did not disclose this in the product description (and in fact includes misleading information - saying the product is 100% plant-based, and only that "Aroma May Contain Fruit Extracts or Fruit Oils"). Our baby has sensitive skin and a history of eczema, so we got the unscented version, with which we've been very pleased. Just wanted to sure in case this is helpful for other parents of babies with sensitive skin.

------------

Reply From Paradise Island Organics customer service, 3/14/14:

"I heard back about the Pear Scent from the manufacturers. The Pear scent is synthetic and does not contain any real pears. The pear fruit does produce an essential oil, however, it takes 20 tons of pears to produce about 3 ounces of essential oil, which is why it is not available to purchase. But, the synthetic pear scent we use is free of phthalates, parabens, nitro musk, sulfates, glycols, petrochemicals, formaldehyde or formaldehyde releasing agents. Using pear extract or flavor is an option we are looking into for the future, but it depends on how strong the extract or flavor is on how well it holds the scent in personal care products. Some particular fruits hold the scent much better than other fruits. But, we will certainly look into having our chemist test it to see if the pear extract or flavor scent would hold well in our shampoo for the future.

If you have any more questions, let me know and I'd be happy to help.
Have a good weekend!
Sincerely,
Camille Scott
Sweet Baby Shampoo"

I've been getting into nail art, uv gel polish, and nail stamping plates of late, and acetone was chewing up my nails so they were dry and thin.  I saw that this product was being offered during Prime Day, so I decided to purchase and try this product.  I have tried it on both regular polish as well as uv-light cured gel polish.  I must say, I prefer to use this on normal polish only.  It gradually removes the polish, and leaves a nicely scented, moisturizing residue behind that really conditions my nails.  I was much less successful using this product to remove my uv gel polish, but I'm also not surprised.  I may read more reviews for tips, but I am content just using this for removing regular polish and nail stamping art.  Now here is the miraculous part...  I had nail stickers on my nails for 3 weeks, and for whatever reason (the acetone, the pre-application buffing, etc) to put those on left my nails SUPER thin.  They would split and flake if I even tried to grow my nails out longer than my fingertip.  I noticed that after using this to clean my nails after my weekly cuticle removal process, my nails looked really moisturized and clean.  Then, I would top off my thin nails with Sally Hansen Hard as Nails so they wouldn't be so plain.  I'm not sure if it was because the SHHAN sealed in whatever essential oils are in this remover, but my nails grew so fast and bounced back stronger than ever so I was able to grow them out very long past my fingertip!  I literally could bang my nail tips on any surface and I could feel the strength.  I think this will be my go-to recovery method for my nails whenever the same issue arises in the future.

review_title: Helped my recurring chalazion and stye problem
review_text:
I’m writing this review for people like me who struggle with recurring chalazions and styes:
I started getting chalazion 5 years ago on both eyes and I don’t know what even started it. It was very frustrating because these bumps would form on my eyelid and nothing worked on them. I got surgery once to get rid of one on my lower eye lid. They stayed for months and warm compresses and eye massages that doctors recommended me did nothing.
I read many research papers to see what I can do to help my condition and here is a summary:
1. this eye wash helped so much. Since I started using this eye wash two months ago my chalazions are almost gone and very unnoticeable. I wash my eyes every mornings and before going to bed and also whenever it starts to itch.
2. One doctor prescribed an antibiotic called “Doxycycline” I think that also helped my condition
3. I make tea with tea leaves and I let it cool, then I use a cotton ball to put the tea inside my eyes. I use 3-4 drops in each eye.
4. mix of one drop of tea tree oil and 4 drops of olive oil and put it on your eye lid. I wash it after 15 mins.

That’s a summary. Some people say warm compresses help them but for me, I did not see noticeable results. I used to wash my eyes with baby shampoo and it worsened my condition. only this eye wash helped. My condition has improved 80% since I took the steps I mentioned.

review_title: The line of silver dye we've needed!
review_text:
I want to start by saying that most of the poor reviews of the SilverWhite line are written by people who clearly don't know what they're doing. This is for light hair, as in WHITE or platinum blonde. If your hair is not light enough, you won't get the results you're looking for, and that isn't the product's fault. With that in mind, these colors are a wonderful alternative to custom silver formulas that require mixing many shades!

I've been dyeing my hair silver for years and I've tried just about every brand of "silver" dye out there with various amounts of success. My hair is naturally a cool dark blonde (ranging from level 7 to 8) and I have to bleach my roots twice to get them light enough for a proper, no brassiness silver. I currently use the Wella T18 toner + 050 for the length of my hair, and do my newly bleached roots with Schwartzkopf Slate Grey + E-1, which fades and blends nicely as new roots grow out. I use Fanola No Yellow shampoo to maintain it. This is a 1:1 dye, meaning you should use the same amount of developer as dye. The great thing about this line is that the dye truly doesn't have any warm undertones (with the exception of the dove grey, which is still cooler than most silvers). I like to add a little E-1 to the slate grey because as with every dye, no matter what brand you use, the cool pigment is the first to fade and adding this extra purple gives it a little more staying power.

I've found that the slate grey does fade more quickly than you would expect from a permanent dye, as it is meant for hair that is naturally grey and has a transparent quality that helps match new grow out; this transparency will also make it VERY obvious if you have any brassy areas or your hair isn't light enough to begin with. Using 20 vol. developer instead of 10 (as is recommended) helps with permanency. The lilac shade also seems to last longer than the other three.

As for being true to color, the slate grey tends to come out darker than shown, and you have to pay close attention to processing time with the silver, which does lean slightly blue and can really take over if you leave it on too long. The dye is relatively gentle since you're using 10 or 20 vol, but don't be tempted to let it process for more than twenty minutes. Both of these color issues will fade within a couple washes if you do though.

TLDR:
These are really great cool shades with little to no warmth and stay true to that as they fade, but
- You MUST have white or near white hair
- Most SilverWhite shades fade quickly, so use 20 vol. developer
- Slate grey is dark and silver leans blue; don't over-process unless you want that

I’m a sucker for a good brush set. It’s even better when it comes with case and a sponge!

So the case is very sturdy and feels well made. You can use it as a brush holder and you can use it store brushes. I am using the shorter half as a brush holder and find that it blends in nicely with my other holders.

Now I’ll do a brief breakdown of the brushes and sponge.

The lip brush is great and it blends in my lipsticks really nice.

There are three brushes for eyes- eyeshadow brush, blending brush and angled liner. I have tried these and they are very soft and work very well.

The powder brush is a bit smaller than I would personally like for powder. It’s not quite dense but in a brush that is used for powder products that’s okay. When I’m buffing in the powder I don’t want the brush to be too dense or it will move the foundation around. I’ve been using this brush for blush because of it’s smaller shape and it’s working great.

Now the final two- the foundation brush and the sponge. I decided to do half of my foundation with the brush on one side, and the other half with the sponge on the other side.

The foundation brush is a typical brush of it’s kind. It did not make the foundation look streaky and applied very smooth.

The sponge is the most interesting piece in this set. It doesn’t feel super soft like a Beauty Blender or a Real Techniques sponge. It feels like a softer stress ball and feels a bit rubbery. I’ve never had a sponge like this. I soaked the sponge in water and drained the excess as I would do with any sponge. It felt heavier but did seem to soften a bit and did expand in size. I dabbed the foundation on my face and pressed the sponge around to press the product in and I got a really smooth finish. The sponge did not seem to absorb much product.

Overall I think it’s a very nice set!

Let me preface this by saying that the colors are pretty and generally well pigmented (I use it with Too Faced Shadow Insurance). My issue is that many of the colors are very glittery - I like shimmery shadows, but we are talking big chunks of glitter here in several of the colors. If you're familiar with Urban Decay's "Midnight Cowgirl" shadow family you'll get the picture. Basically the entire palette is gliterry, except for two matte shades. If you get this, make sure to put a tissue under your eyes to catch the fall-out or you'll look like a disco ball. I'm talking serious fall-out here.

The colors are:

Full Moon: Glittery Champagne
Night Light: Supremely Glittery rosey pink (this one has a chalky texture, making it impossible to apply without massive fallout.)
Spotlight: Matte Beige
Nightcap: Shimmery medium tan
After Hours: Chalky glittery medium beige
Moonstone: Glittery deep tan
Cocoa Star: Matte chocolate brown
Eclipse: Glittery Chestnut brown
Night Fever: Glittery Chocolate brown

The positives: The packaging is cute, the colors are fairly pigmented, Too Faced includes looks cards so you can get ideas on looks.

The negatives: This is only a good palette if you already have a nice collection of eyeshadow and you want something to throw in your purse when you're going out of town and know you'll be partying (and you have the patience to deal with massive fallout). You can definitely make some work appropriate looks, but these are more glittery than shimmery, making it a bit juvenile. Some of the shadows are chalky too. I also have the Urban Decay Naked palette and the colors are MUCH better, as is the quality of the shadows. Personally I think Naked is also a better deal. It's $50, so $14 more, but you get more colors, the shadows are better quality (creamier and smoother), and it comes with a nice brush.

I find that I don't use this palette much. It isn't a palette that has an obvious place in my makeup collection.

Updated: I am still experimenting with this palette (I brought it in my makeup bag on vacation and left my UD Naked palette at home) and I've definitely created some nice looks that are completely appropriate for daily life. I just don't LOVE it. The problem is, I have the Urban Decay Naked palette. The colors are similar between UD Naked and TF Natural at Night (warm browns and champagnes) but the Urban Decay colors are shimmers (I love shimmers) and many of the shads in the Too Faced Naked at Night palette are glitters. That makes the TF colors much harder to work with due to fallout. Ultimately, this palette is 3.5 stars to me. It has nice colors and you can create some great looks (provided you put tissue under your eyes to catch the fallout), but the UD Naked Palette is just better in my opinion in terms of pigmentation, ease of application, and blending.

review_title: III Sisters of Nature Coconut Milk Cleansing Co-Wash
review_text:
This co-wash has some interesting ingredients for its self-proclaimed title of a "cleansing co-wash" but a quick look- up of the ingredients doesn't reveal a cleansing agent. It is a moisturizing co-wash made up of mainly oils & butter which are good ingredients to use during colder months. I've used this product 3 times (twice after a hot oil treatment) and had more positive results after the hot oil treatment, rinsing with warm water: my scalp felt cleansed and curls were moisturized with minimal frizz. When I used it as a straight co-wash & rinsed with cool water, my hair felt overly coated & slimy and only felt clean after a prolonged rinsing.

Positives: Able to work the product throughout hair after initially applying it to my scalp & roots; very thick product so a little goes a long way; hair felt moisturized after rinsing; brought curls to life; fairly cheap at Beauty Supply stores.

Negatives: Strong unpleasant scent that lingers after rinsing (smells like cherry cough syrup); can be too heavy for thin/fine hair if too much product is used or if not completely rinsed out; hair didn't feel 100% clean after rinsing; difficult to find on the ground.

Although the product is giving me a good base to begin my wash day regimen during these colder months, I can recreate the same effect by adding oils to any cheap conditioner so I won't repurchase it.

review_title: Great but, get the cheaper one. Just as good.
review_text:
Do you have migraines or Meniere's disease or just have a sensitive head? Don't get any of the pulsating Oral B brushes. They will just make you nauseous or trigger a headache.

I have used the classic Oral B electric brush for many years. A fantastic simple white design by Braun of Germany - since discontinued after Braun was bought by an American company. Now I have the simple low end non pulsing model. Essentially the same guts and head as the classic but with an ugly, over stylized, blue body.

When the battery started to die on my classic model, I picked up a pulsating Oral B. It is really banging away at your teeth and does as good a job as the non pulsatinging. But it vibrates your jaw and skull like, well, a vibrating electric tooth brush! After a month, it was just too much for me. I went back to the dieing battery original, but soon got its replacement as a gift.

The verdict: I'm in my 40s and I've had about 6 different dentists (moving from job to job) in 5 different states. One was a professor at a dental college. After each visit, they all proclaim my teeth are in excellent shape. I use the cheapest Oral B electric brush (non pulsating) in the morning and before bed with Colgate Total. I also floss just one time before bed and use the Crest rinse for night time. I get them cleaned every 6-9 months.

Save your money and get the cheapest Oral B electric toothbrush. I think it is on sale sometimes for about $10.

This opens all lilies and bergamot, heady and strong. It dries down quickly to a soft jasmine with a touch of gardenia and a hint of rose, amber, and cedar. The fragrance remains true from drydown until it fades completely, which is a good six hours or more; surprisingly long for eau de toilette.

The sillage is a bit more than moderate. You can keep it closer to yourself by spraying it below the waist. I always wear fragrance below the waist, usually at my knees to allow it to float up rather than away. That way I can enjoy any fragrance I wear without bothering other people.

Not quite a soliflore, but close. It smells almost like jasmine green tea, except that hint of gardenia. I wear it by itself or layer with a woody or rose fragrance. I think jasmine is wearable all year long, and it doesn't belong to a particular age group. This is a quieter fragrance than Tea Rose. It's cheerful yet cozy, and easy to wear.

Because of the generous size and the nature of the fragrance, I sometimes use it as a room or linen spray. Sometimes it's hard to believe something so pleasing and universally appealing can be found for such a small price. Kudos to Perfumer's Workshop for this treasure.

review_title: Great at removing makeup. Leaves skin smooth and doesn't dry it out.
review_text:
There are various important aspects that a facial cleanser needs to have or shouldn't have. The Simpir facial cleanser hits all the right categories for my skin and preference. This doesn't dry out my skin at all, which is a common problem for me. On the other hand, it doesn't aggravate my generally oily forehead. I haven't experienced any unusual acne since starting this and I didn't have any skin irritation or redness. It does a good job of removing makeup, and it rinses off easily. I have noticed a slight reduction in the size of my pores and number of blackheads on my nose and chin. I have been using this once a day for about 2 weeks.

I'm not a fan of the smell, but it's charcoal and should be expected that it's not going to smell great. I won't fault the product for that. Fortunately I don't smell it at all once I rinse it off. The pump works well and doesn't over dispense the cleanser so I don't feel like I'm wasting anything. I do prefer pumps that twist open/close rather than having to be pushed down and twisted to close because it's easier for travel. Not the end of the world though. I appreciate that the cleanser is made in the USA and uses organic and natural ingredients. You can never be too careful with something used on your skin regularly, and I feel a product of that quality made in the USA seems safer.

review_title: Well made, works great, easy to clean
review_text:
This is the first time I've ever purchased a foot file. From my pictures you'll see how clear it is I should have bought one a long time ago. The only time I ever get my feet filed is when I get a pedicure. Maybe once a year. Having the ability to do that at home will definitely help me keep my feet looking, well, normal.

The wood on the file looks really nice and it comes with a suction cup and string so you can hang it up if you want. The red side of the file is quite coarse to help really clean up your feet, but causes no discomfort at all. The black side is also coarse, but less so. It helps with smoothing. Overall it seems well made and like it will last quite a while.

I haven't had it long and have actually only used it once, but just once made a huge difference. I did not follow directions and soak my feet for 10-30 minutes in salt water. I simple took a shower, dried my feet, and used the file on both feet for 5 minutes total. If I had soaked my feet I'm sure I would have got even better results. I also put aloe lotion on my feet after. I never put lotion on my feet and they're usually very dry and cracked because of that. I intend to use the file every day for the next couple days briefly after I shower until I get my feet looking good. After doing so I'll add the lotion as part of the regimen. Using the file is going to help keep me conscious of keeping my feet hydrated so it does more than just file. :-)

After using the file I rinsed it off in the sink with mild soap. It took 10 seconds to get all the skin off and looking brand new again. If you have calluses or other rough spots on your feet this file is a great way to take care of that with little effort. I definitely recommend it.

review_text:
When I initially read reviews for this, I was excited to see people complaining about it being tedious and painful. That's honestly what I was kind of hoping for. Guys. Let's be real. Getting this done professionally is also tedious and painful, but you're on someone else's schedule. I'm so here for the convenience of just being able to sit down and do this tedious, painful task on my own time, while watching season after season of Always Sunny in Philadelphia. A few things I learned:

1) using salt water rather than just regular water is crucial.
2) you can't do this to someone else, it don't work. It means PERSONAL when it says personal. I'm going to guess it has something to do with science/electrical current, but I don't actually know, I just found that I couldn't help my sister out with the little black hairs on her neck, but when she held the wand herself, it worked fine.
3) yes, that's lye.
4) yes, those are burns.
5) aquaphor.

It's performing the job it's meant to do, which is a painful, tedious job, but it absolutely does what it says it will do. The only reason I'm not giving it five stars for fulfilling it's intended purpose as described is because of that annoying beeping. I don't understand the purpose of that. It's irritating. Why not use a pleasant LED light fade on the box instead?? Something that doesn't scream at me? Maybe?

review_text:
This is not the same HeelTastic I've been buying for years. First, it smells different. The new scent is much lighter and, to me, less pleasing than the old scent but not bad. The color is different as well. The new color is white, whereas the old color is more champagne or a pale gold. Coloration could be the age of the older one. They seem to go on the same though. Same viscosity, same melt and spread.

The thing that gets me is that the product is only 1-1/5" deep (and 1-5/8" diameter). So much plastic for such little product! The old container is 4" tall; the new one is 3-7/8" tall. Only the height of the lid is different, since the bottoms of the lids align and the containers without lids are the same height. There are some slight packaging differences, and the ingredients list is quite different, though the logo font is the same.

In my case it took three weeks to get these. If I'd known all this, I would have just gone down to BB&B (three dollars cheaper) and bought the stuff there. I think I will do that anyway, just to compare them. (My old bottle is almost used up.) Both containers claim to have 2oz of product, but I don't know.

In summary: Too much plastic! Very little product! Almost 25 percent more expensive. I do not recommend this product.

review_title: Ok powder, not worth the long wait on shipping
review_text:
Let’s see. I was looking for a nice, inexpensive mint green pallet. It’s hard to find a genuine mint green. No one had left a review of this, so I decided to take a chance. First of all, the shipping took forever. I ordered this April 25, and I didn’t receive it until May 22, almost a month later. I’ve received things faster ordering them from China! Then, once I got it, I tried it out (see pics). The colors are nice, but not extremely impressive. The matte colors are very powdery and get all over your face. The shimmers are nice. I usually dust my eyes with powder, after I apply eyeshadow, to set it, and then apply more shadow, if I need it. I lightly dusted loose powder in my eyes, after application, and I dust very gently. Most of the shadow came off. So I reapplied. The color was nice, but the matte shades faded a lot, after two hours. The shimmer stayed, but the pigment wasn’t as strong, after a few hours.

So do yourself a favor. Buy a mint green palette from a store where you can get it faster, and where the color payoff is better.

review_title: Nicer looking in person, drill bits in case attached under drill, files pop off sometimes,
review_text:
I got this to be able to do my nails from home.
Pros:
* Much nicer in person. The images listed don't do it justice. The box it comes in, the plastic that holds it, and the machine itself is sturdy.
The drill bits can be stored in a little case that pops open when you push the button on the mid-bottom portion of the case. The best part is that it can be stored in the bottom of the machine itself, so you don't lose them.
* The drill is powerful and it has a knob so you can make it faster or slower. (The origional images were lost so I had to retake them after I had tested it. Sorry, I like to take picture of it before use. So excuse the arcylic bits from the nail.)
* It was powerful enough to file acrylic nails but it did get warm around the last nail. Not hot just warm it was pretty good for shaping all 10 acrylic nails.
*Grip it well but just gradually add pressure to the nail if you are a beginner until you get the feel of it.
*You have to hold it down for 3 seconds to turn it on after plugging it in. It will turn blue for forward motion and push it again and the light will switch to red for backward motion.
Cons:
* The reddish-brown filing pieces, that attach to one of the bits, has 4 pieces but they are flimsy. They don't look like they will last very long and they are thin.
*The dial can be adjusted but there are no numbers or levels. You just move it around until you think you have the speed you want. I don't like that because if you know a certain level you are comfortable with you to have to make your own markings with a sharpie or something because it's kinda hard to remember where you had it for a certain nail (real vs acyclic) or for certain drill bits. (minus half a star)
*There is no "click" when putting the drill bits in so you just have to push it in as far as you can. However, I did this and sometimes it would fall off, so I had to push it in as far as I could. (minus half a star)
Conclussion:
All in all I would recommend this for yourself or as a gift. The images from the seller should be updated somehow because their photos make it look kind of cheap or tacky but it really isn't once you see it. It has a good weight to it so it isn't cheap material (but the reddish-brown file did seemer lower quality). The machine itself is really good and we are all in quarintie so they are much cheaper and safer than going to a nail salon. Plus it is powerful enough for acrylic.

review_title: Super soft and silky results! Works fast on breakage and split ends!
review_text:
Wow! I've tried a lot of different Argan Oil shampoo and conditioners (and sprays and masks and hot treatments etc) and I can 100% say this is my All time favorite for no other reason than how incredibly fast I'm seeing a difference in the ends and improvement on breakage. I color my hair and have been for close to 10 years now and just in the past year or so I've started having really bad problems with breakage and split ends. I've tried probably 10 different brands or more with some kind of argan oil treatment and it really helps. But I didn't get results like this from anywhere else, and I've tried some pretty pricey stuff. After like, 3 days of use I happened to look down at my hair one day and it just hit me that I didn't have any frizz or areas that looked wild and untamed from breakage, the hairs that would normally have 2 or 3 splits or frays were just smooth all the way down. I tried to take a picture of the hair up close so you could see but couldn't get a clear shot at such a short distance. The color looks richer and has a healthy looking shine, it isn't greasy or stringy like you might worry about with Argan Oil.
This stuff even smells amazing! I usually like coconut scents, it's always been my favorite, but this smells more floral and a little spicy, which maybe sounds weird but I think it's soooo good.

It lathers up surprisingly well for an Argan Oil shampoo and I don't have to use much for my bra strap length hair. My hair is really thick, too, but a good quarter sized dallop works out to be about the right amount for me. I do the ends and body first and work my way up to my scalp, backwards from how I use regular shampoo. (I do this because some brands seem to leave my hair oily if I don't get it rinsed out well, that Argan Oil can be stubborn.) I usually let it set for a couple minutes while I wash my body so the hair can absorb the nutrients before I rinse it away. I follow it with their conditioner and my hair gets sooo soft when it dries. I really can't stress enough how well it helps my hair. I know everyone responds differently but for me, it's better than anything else I've tried. I'll be ordering this again for sure.

I did receive my Argain oil shampoo at a promotional price for testing and evaluation purposes. I was not paid for my review and was asked only to provide whatever feedback I may have about the product, whether it be positive or negative. I welcome both positive or negative feedback as well. My review is solely based on my experience and honest opinions of this shampoo.

review_title: Good for clarifying but questionable ingredients

I like how it worked but I'm not sure how hard it would be on my hair if I used it regularly.

Grammy® 18 Inch Long Straight Nature Full Head Clips In Human Hair Remy Hair Extensions Clip Extensions Human Hair Clip 7pcs ( #99J Red Wine Burgundy) ...

This is a review for Grammy 18" long straight nature full head clip ins. The hair extensions arrived as planned and they were attached to cardboard the length of the hair to keep safe. They were then wrapped in a plastic bag to cover hair. Upon opening the hair I did not smell any kind of smell to the hair. The hair is soft to the touch and was the right color that I had ordered. As with any extensions, you receive in the mail first thing you must do is use a hot iron and get the creases out from shipping. When combing through the hair there were no tangles or missing hair. I did have a little bit of shedding but that is to be expected and was not enough to have a second thought about. The hair straightened great with no problems. The hair is sewn onto a small comb metal clip and I did not see any loose clips.

The quantity: The hair is what I expected it to be. When I compared the two matching pieces together I did note that one has more hair than the matching piece. (You will see in pictures that I have included in this review). However, this was on the two smallest extensions and not any other piece so for me that is not a big deal because I usually do not use those pieces.

The quality: This is my second hair extension I have ever owned. The first one I bought I paid quite a bit of money for and the hair was not near as soft as this one from Grammy. The quality of this hair is what I expected it to be but with softer hair. I am very pleased with the quality.

In my opinion, if you have somewhat fuller hair than one package should give you the fullness you are seeking. With that being said, if your hair is really thin and you are seeking a full thick head of hair look than you might need to go with 2 packages. I would but then you run into how to clip all the pieces in your head. You must have hair to clip these on for them to stay in place.

How I manage to be able to keep the extensions in my head all day all night and even sleep in for 2 nights if I want is by starting with clean dry straighten hair. I then part my hair every spot that I will be clipping an extension to and I spray with a strong hair spray let dry and then I take a small man's comb and tease just at the base of my hair close to my scalp, that gives the clips something to hold them in tightly no matter what I am doing.

I hope that this review has helped in your buying decision. I have posted pictures that I hope will allow for you to see each piece and the clipping device. Thank you for reading and if you have any questions or comments please feel free to post. I have added 12 pictures and I hope this is helpful.

review_text: Trying to save you some time reading through all the reviews.  From my own personal experience, and that of many others I have seen on this and various other sites for reviews on this product, it just does not work well at all for course body hair, so do NOT purchase it for that.  To be fair, it may work better for it's title area, but I still have to give it one star, because it makes bold claims to remove body hair for extended periods of time over your entire body (which it failed miserably on for me and many others).  In fact, even on some of the positive reviews, people indicated it was like "a close shave" and that they have to use it very frequently, which goes against the company's claims.  A lot of hair removal gels and creams remove hair to skin level, so that is not really effective (or pleasant, as it leaves you with almost immediate stubble).  It also seems to be a cheesy company run out of somebody's basement, based on the Ziploc bag packaging, photocopied instructions, and weird 1960s children's glove.  If you have course body hair, this stuff is not going to help you, unfortunately.  So, buy it for your balls, but not for your body if you have course hair.  Major failure in that respect.

This teeth cleaning kit consisting of an ultrasound toothbrush and a “flosser” was fun to use. The rechargeable toothbrush is comfortable in the hand, requiring no actual conventional brushing. You just hold the toothbrush head over the tooth surface and let the ultrasonic waves do the work. It even gives warning beeps telling the user its time to move on to a new section of your mouth. The unit gradually builds up intensity over multiple sessions so new users can get used to the vibrations. One warning would be that if you have extensive repair work on your teeth (I had a chip filled on my front tooth) you may want to ask your dentist if its safe to use. If you use the brush correctly there is no problem, but if you accidently touch the hard plastic part of the brush head to a repaired tooth area it could cause damage. It has not happened to me yet, but I can see it happening.

The flosser is more interesting. You fill a small resevoir on the flosser handle with water or mouthwash, press the flosser head between your teeth, and press a button. This sends a blast of water and air between your teeth. It doesn’t hurt. It seems to be effective and possibly more effective than a string type floss. It is definitely more comfortable than using a string flosser. Only the front spaces of your teeth need the treatment so accessing the inside of your teeth is not necessary. It is a messy process if you do not have your mouth closed, as the water can spritz out of your mouth or make you drool, but with practice you should be able to minimize this (or use it in the shower).

Battery life seems good so far. Both the flosser and toothbrush have their own charging stand. No plugs are used (except the AC wall plugs). You just drop the brush or flosser on a stand with a metal stud to begin the charging process. It can take several hours to reach full charge.

I like using these the brush as it seems to be a bit more thorough than the average toothbrush. There are vibrating toothbrushes that act more like conventional toothbrushes available and you may like them just as much. The flosser, however, is truly unique, and if you are like me, a person who never flosses, you may find yourself actually enjoying the process.

review_text:
I’m a 29 year old, very pale woman who’s been self tanning since 16 years old. I’ve tried just about everything I’ve ever ran across and now it was time to try this. Hands down, this is the best can tan I’ve ever used. I’m very thrilled about finding it!! First off, the smell is very light, and nothing like the average self tanner. Also, let’s be honest, if you are seasoned at all with self tanning, you know self tanners make your armpits stink. This is the only self tanner I’ve ever tried that doesn’t do that!!! It has instant color, so you can see where all you’ve rubbed it in, rather than just guessing, in order to get that flawless tan we’re all looking for. I personally use gloves underneath the mit that comes with it. It works out wonderfully for me. I did my research before purchasing this product, and I noticed bad reviews from a different seller with the same product, which most all were saying the exact same thing..... the can is messy. I’ve used this exact can 4 times by now, and I’ve never had a mess with it leaking until this last application. If you experience this, here’s what you do!! Mine would squirt all over the bathroom every time I attempted to spray more. So, I wiped the can clean, effortlessly pulled the spray part off, then wiped it from underneath and also wiped on top of the can beneath where the spray top sets. Wipe it completely dry!! Put it back on, and carry on. No more leaky issues whatsoever. Very easy fix!!! I can’t stand to read a negative review on a great product simply because the reviewer didn’t use their head and fix the problem. Overall, this is by far a 5 star self tanner. It doesn’t wash right down the drain after your first shower like other tanners seem to do. The color is good, and it lasts! I’ll be keeping this stuff in stock for sure.

Also, I recommend rubbing in some moisturizer on the knees, heels, ankles, toes, elbows, and knuckles before using, and remember to go light on those areas to avoid orange patches. After all, it’s still a self tanner! And I purchased the back strap that helps you rub it in on your back, I recommend that too!! I’m telling you, this is the way to get your HEALTHY, beautifully flawless tan. This is it, guys.

Happy tanning!!!

First for a disclosure: I didn't buy the Plexiderm on Amazon, so you can believe my review or not.

Now for my review: I was concerned, despite many online videos that show this product in action, that it would be a scam product. And that's just because of the reviews here on Amazon. NOT! I tried it and it worked EXACTLY as promised. I watched in my makeup mirror as one eye bag disappeared before my eyes- fun! It didn't leave a visible film but I have very light skin especially around my eyes, so this product might leave a chalky looking film on darker skin. (They recommend mixing the product on the palm of your hand with your foundation 3:1 if that is an issue)

Next: This is a TEMPORARY fix, just like makeup is. It will only last 6-8 hrs depending on whether you sweat or have oily skin (both things will cause it to 'disappear'). Some bad reviews here reflect frustration over the bottle dispensor (you have to pump to prime it and must be careful not to overpump and waste product)- for me, maybe i got a new and improved bottle type, but I didn't encounter any problem whatsoever!

As for price and quantity- yes, its expensive and yes, you'll be lucky if one bottle lasts you a month. As for me, I don't intend on using it every single day unless I get hooked. :0 Each bottle has only 0.5 mls in it but you only need a teeny tiny drop each time.

Lastly, i think your review will depend on your expectation. My expectation was that the product would do what it said (temporarily de-puff some eye bags) and it does exactly that so how could I take any stars away from them? The cost was fully disclosed beforehand as was the product performance. All in all, I'm now obsessed! And I'm 100% sure that this product is in every single makeup artist to-the-stars bag these days.

This is a clip-on human hair extension.  Here's why I love this product (and have bought several): 1) its human hair. I find that the synthetics cause me to itch where the ends touch skin when it swings/sways, but the human hair doesn't.  Plus its softer than synthetic.  2) you can wash, color and curl this.  I hot curl mine all the time (one of the 'con's' is that the curl doesn't hold from wearing to wearing).  If you had to color or wash this, you could. I've done both too!  But needs to be handled with great care!!! 3) its one unit, so its easy to apply. It has 4 clips across the back where you clip it up under your hair in back to gain a bit of length and alot of volume.  Keep in mind that this one is only 10 inches. That means that it will come just about to shoulder length (depending how you clip it in). It is NOT a long hair extension (look to 15-17 inches if you want long hair).  Other info/tips: The colors shown online are slightly off from what the piece will actually look like, but the descriptions are good. They will NOT take this back if you wear it, brush it out, etc. - so be sure to know the color you want before you order.  This company sells a wheel of colors for about $20 (you'd have to inquire directly with them for current price of their color wheel) and if you never ordered any from them before, I'd recommend getting that wheel to be sure of what you will get under each color number/name.  That being said, and you still want to chance ordering from the online descriptions, remember there will be some 'forgiveness' to the color you order because its clipped under your own hair and gets kind of mixed in.  I would recommend a shade darker than your own color, rather than lighter.  Lastly, if your hair is VERY, very thin...you may find that clipping in a full extension like this one is not practical (won't hold or blend well) and it may pull uncomfortably at your own hair and even cause breakage.  Along same line, I would not recommended this for people with bald patches.  But for thinning hair perhaps due to aging, or because your own hair was never the thickness you wished, or for a fast dressing up of your own hair for special occasions- this extension is ideal and you will love it like I do!
