review_title: Why argue with centuries of dental success?
review_text:
I really don't understand people who think the flavor is so heinous. It's a little strange, but nothing that's going to make you gag. I also wouldn't say that it tastes are smells like synthetic chemicals. These come pretty fresh sealed inside the packages and are at first really easy to peel and loosen the fibers. Once it dries out, you will need to employ the water-soaking method, which makes it simple enough. Just make sure it soaks for at least an hour for very easy handling. I've been using the same stick for months. It usually takes about a week or two for the end to get ratty enough to cut and start over again. I wouldn't say this stick eliminates flossing. It depends on the way your teeth are situated. I have some problem spots that I absolutely need to use floss for. That being said, I've noticed a significant reduction of plaque that is removed with a floss after brushing with a miswak (vs. after brushing with a good conventional toothbrush or even a sonicare toothbrush). In my personal experience, a miswak works better than a Sonicare. However, if you like the convenience of the Sonicare, stick to that. It depends on each person's habits and personality. You can damage your enamel with a Sonicare, so please be careful and follow the instructions carefully. You really don't have a problem with hurting gums or the enamel with a miswak. It is also the perfect travel toothbrush.

Pros: Lasts a long time, is completely natural, no need for toothpaste, minimal flossing, travels easily, gentle on teeth and gums while getting into nooks and crannies better than a traditional western brush, dental study shows improvement of gingivitis with regular use of miswak.

Cons: Awkward handling for back of teeth, must peel to get a new layer, some people don't like the taste, not easy for children to use.

review_title: Not as Strong As I Hoped
review_text:
I am relatively new to solid colognes. I own this sampler set, Oak City Beard's Sandalwood Bourbon, and a sample set from another company. The other company's set was my first venture into solid colognes. I liked the variety it offered, and their colognes usually lasted most of the day.

I expected the same from this set.

I will admit, I liked variety that this offered, which is why I ordered it. Now that I've had time to try out each one, here are my thoughts. (Please note, cologne can smell different on each person, so what didn't work for me, may work for you.)

Barista - I don't drink coffee, so the thought of smelling like coffee all day was not a selling point for me. I figured this would be my least favorite of the four. When I opened the tin, it smelled like a 30-year-old motel lobby. A powerful scent of cheap black coffee, with a hint of musty cigarettes and pleather couches. I was not impressed. Still, I put it on and the smell changed to more of a 1990s coffee shop. Fortunately, the cocoa smell came forward more once it was on me, and the coffee was not as strong. I don't hate it as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of like how it smells on me.

Woodland Ranger - My favorite out of the bunch. While you may think it would make you smell like a Christmas tree, it's more of a clean outdoors scent.

Snow Leopard - I love me some sandalwood, so this was the one I really bought the set for. It says there is peppermint in it, but I can't smell it. Also, I feel like the vanilla overpowers the sandalwood. Not as good as I had hoped. Not bad at all, just not what I expected. (This one also seems to dissipate quicker than the others.)

Uncle Jack - I smell the bourbon and a trace of tobacco, but once again, the vanilla is the stronger scent here. It's definitely not a bad smell, probably my second favorite of the pack.

As I mentioned in the headline, the colognes are just not as strong as I hoped for. I mean, I don't want to overpower everyone in my general vicinity, but I do like to smell the cologne throughout the day and none of these do that. Perhaps I'm not putting enough on. Like I said, I'm new to this whole solid cologne thing.

It appears that, due to an observational study finding a small correlation between talc and cancer, many now believe that ‘science has prove talc bad‘. This is due, primarily, to ubiquitous misunderstanding of what constitutes ’science’ and how enormous a difference there is between the reliability of actual science and observational studies—the former, after repeated and properly-designed experiments, provides a strong basis for causal inference, while observational studies provide little more than a reason to conduct an experiment. Of course, we never hear about any actual experimental results, i.e. actual science, with things like this, because, either the observation result was merely promoted as a sensational headline and the people who conducted it know very well a minor correlation doesn’t even justify the time and expense of an experiment, or because experiments were conducted and didn’t produce the sensational result.

Unfortunately, when media takes advantage of this widespread misunderstanding, good products are removed from shelves and good companies producing good products lose money. Here, it appears the company chose to give in to the hysteria, which is a shame. I suspect that, if their actual customers had much of a voice, they’d find out this was a bad decision. review_text:
I was given the chance to test this out in exchange for an honest and unbiased review, and I was so excited to receive it. It's a big, kind of bulky, five barrel hair crimper, and it's awesome.
My hair is pretty easy to curl, but it takes a while, and as a mom of two boys, I hardly have time to spend curling.

That made it kind of difficult to know when to start, but I just turned it on before I started my makeup and it's definitely ready by the time I go to use it. (About two minutes later)
The waves it gives look great, especially if you use product made for curls, and it adds SO MUCH body and makes it really easy for Bobby pins to stick.

review_title: Lots of storage options in this bag!
review_text:
If you need a lot of space for your make up brushes and a place to keep them tidy/organized, this bag is for you!! This bag is approximately 10.5" by 7" approximately. It's black in color and made from high quality non-woven fabrics. It has two zippers for easy closure. It has the name of the company on the outside of the bag on the corner in white - "Louise Maelys". Okay, so once you unzip it and open it - on the left, you have a mesh zipper pouch on the top half. That little pouch is is about 5.5" long and 3" tall. It's mesh so you can see through it. On the bottom half of that left hand side, there is 3 elastic pouches. These little pouches are 5" tall and about 2" wide. Elastic at the top of them so it can hold in your brushes/tools/whatever. In the middle of this organizer, is another zip up pouch which moves back and forth. It is also mesh, so it's see-through. It is 8" long and about 5.5" tall. It zips up. The cool thing about this pouch is that it snaps in to the middle of the entire organizer so if you want to remove it - you can! Just unsnap the two snaps and remove! Love that feature! On the right hand (or back side of the organizer), is a ton of little compartments for your brushes. On the top row, there is 9 little elastic pouches for your brushes. These are the smallest ones, about .5" wide so these would need to be for tiny and slender brushes. This row of little compartments goes down 6". Next row is just a pouch. About 6" long and 4.5" deep. No elastic or anything - just a pouch. Last row, on the bottom, is 5 elastic pouches. These are about 1" wide and just about 4" tall. These pouches can hold fatter, more wide, brushes. On the backside of the outside of the bag, there is another zip up compartment. There is also a nice handle on the top of the bag so you can carry it easily. So many lovely options to hold your brushes and make up supplies! LOVE it. I checked all the seams and stitching on this - everything is flawless. It does have a tiny bit of a "plastic" type odor to it, but I'm sure that will go away once it airs out more. Overall, this is a solid five star from me. It's a great affordable option for your make up brushes and tools. It was packaged nicely and arrived in plenty of time.

Fill shaker with ice (you may want to double or triple this recipe for more than one person).
1 jigger (1.5 oz...the large end of the jigger) vodka
1 jigger Lychee liqueur or syrup
Dash dry vermouth
Shake, pour into a chilled martini glass and garnish with a lychee on a tooth pick.
Enjoy.

I've been diffusing essential oils for almost 30 years, ever since I purchased my first diffuser from Whole Foods back in the 1980s. This diffuser is not representative of the latest generation of diffusers, but it fits nicely within the last generation. The latest generation of diffusers are not waterless, cordless (rechargeable) and portable. I have both types of diffusers in my home and much prefer the latest gen.

This is a nice diffuser but is slightly more expensive than it should be, even with the ceramic appointments. Like all water diffusers you put water in the chamber with a few drops of oil and let it go. The light is nice but doesn't serve much purpose other than to remind you that the unit is on when you cannot see the cold steam. I'm not a fan of the whole thing being lit because it does cause me to take a second look if my eyes slightly open while I'm sleeping. I prefer a thin band of light. Of course on this unit you can turn the light off.

It doesn't come with any oil which is actually good. I find that when an oil is included in with a diffuser it's often the cheapest brand around and smells awful. It might be enough to turn a newbie off of diffusing if they don't know that high quality oils exist. I recommend Plant Therapy.

I don't buy into the claim that this can be used as a humidifier because the output is just not strong enough. After shut-off there is always water still left in the chamber. This is not a good thing because if you want to change oils, you have to diffuse water with vinegar for a couple of run-throughs and then wipe down the inside. Of course there is nothing wrong with left over oil if you don't mind a blend, but sometimes I want one pure smell for a specific purpose.

I put it on morning and night for five days straight, and I always woke up (and spent the day) with itchy eyes. I tried to convince myself that it was something in the air, but when I forgot to use it I was just fine. So I stopped using it and I was just fine.

However, I do believe in the concept. My family in Jamaica swear by putting coconut (or castor) oil on the lashes daily to keep them supple. When they're moisturized they don't fall off as fast, and putting on mascaras certainly aid in drying out the lashes. I try the oil-on-the-lashes thing but I've made the decision to stop using this product.

I haven't been using this item long enough to report on any discernible difference in my face but I can speak to a couple of other interesting tidbits.

I know that these have been in use for generations and they must work because people swear by them. If that weren't proof enough, I use my Clarisonic Uplift daily, and it comes with an attachment that does the exact same thing that this roller does, only with using technology. The instructions on this roller is to use it for 5-10 minutes a day, 2-3 times a day. That's a lot and I don't know of many people who care to carve out time to do this, but if you're sitting quietly watching TV or even reading, you can do it absentmindedly. With the Clarisonic, you're supposed to use it with a moisturizer or a serum but with this, you use it on a dry face. With or without a lotion, the massaging affect is exactly the same.

The jade roller feels cool across the skin (even if mine does squeak a little) and it feels wonderful. I'm not sure it does anything if you're rolling it on your chest, but it feels amazing if done with a bit of pressure. It comes in a nice little Asian-inspired embroidered bag, so it doesn't look bad if you want to leave it on your bedside for easy access. I'm going to continue to use the Uplift each night but this item doesn't require a battery and I can whip it out anytime.

For the price, I have to wonder why this item is not listed under Amazon's "luxury beauty" line. Like many reviewers, I was put off by the sheer amount of packaging that came along with this item. It wouldn't be so bad if they didn't tout how conscious they were of environmental issues, but I've purchased Chanel with less packing, come on!

All of the beauty and skin care products I consume are luxury, at the moment I've been using Dr. Gross's skin care line but until I could get back to Sephora, I've been using Purity cleanser. I was hoping this product would be a suitable replacement but I'm not convinced so let me tell you about the photos.

Each night I cleanse my face with Purity using Clarasonic's Uplift with the Revitalizing brush. I follow this with micellar water (by Borghese) and then a serum and moisturizer. The whole thing takes about 7 minutes (it's therapy, don't judge!).

Upon waking, I swabbed my face with the micellar water and then took a picture of the cotton ball along with an untouched cotton ball for comparison. And by the way for the uninitiated, micellar water is the best skincare product to come out since mascara was invented. I was sure that my $349 Clarasonic erased all traces of dirt no matter the soap, but the micellar water never lies.

On the second morning, first thing, I used the Clarasonic with the Radiance brush and three pumps of LaClaire Foaming Botanical Facial Cleanser. Two pumps did not create a bit of lather. Then using micellar water, I swabbed my face again and there you have the picture of both -- no cleanser and cleanser.

You can see that there is still a lot of dirt left behind after using this cleanser, certainly less than no cleanser at all but there is still some there. There is less dirt left after washing with Purity so I wouldn't call it a miracle cleanser, it's really just "okay."

The texture is interesting - it's less a cream and more like a gel that's almost runny. It absorbs fairly quickly into the skin and doesn't leave behind any kind of greasy residue. It does help with redness and dry patches, and at this point, it doesn't seem to cause breakouts.

I have to say, though, that I was hoping for longer-lasting, even cumulative results, because I apply this at night and right after I rinse my face off the next morning, it's almost like I never used the product at all. review_title: Great for Acne, Fresh And Clean Feel.
review_text:
I received NOTS brand 28 Day Remedy on June 12th as a promotional item from the company. This product is available with Amazon Prime Delivery so it came in about 3 days. This is nice because I don't like being without my skincare for more than a few days.

I have been using 28 Day Remedy twice a day for 10 days now. I have had serious acne problems in the past and usually I would have to use multiple acne care products to keep my skin clear. For me this serum by itself was enough to keep my acne problems away. I did however incorporate this into my normal skincare routine, meaning I used this after my normal toner and followed it with my normal moisturizer.

I really like this serum, it absorbs very well into the skin, which for me is the biggest factor. It does not leave a tacky or sticky film on the skin. Also, a little goes a long way. Before, I have used other Korean brand skincare and serums like Skin&Lab Dr. Color Effect Red Serum and also Zymogen Ferment Houttuniya Cordata Extract Serum. I would choose 28 Day Remedy above both Skin&Lab and Zymogen. 28 Day Remedy is more effective for my skin regeneration and healing than Red Serum without the stickiness. Also it absorbs better and quicker than Zymogen and is more effective against acne on its own.

This product did smooth my skin texture and any breakouts I had starting were gone by the next morning. Overall this is a very good product especially if you have had problems with acne in the past. I am giving it 4 out of 5 stars because the price point is a little high for most people. But this product does do what it promises on the packaging and is a quality product.

-Sonya H.

review_title: It isn't even close to natural bristle
review_text:
I wanted to try a synthetic fiber brush since it is impossible to dry your natural bristle brush sufficiently before packing it up on the day of travel. I was looking for a brush that I can use, shake out and pack within minutes. For use at home, I've had over the years a couple of natural badger brushes of varying quality, ranging from lower grade black only brushes to very fine silvertip. So, trust me, I know how they feel.
This brush is for me virtually unusable.
When i try to lather up, i spray water and soap all over the bathroom. Try as i may, i couldn't prevent the spray. When these synthetic bristles are deflected even only a little, they spring back with a snap. It appears that the spring back force increases linearly with the amount of deflection. And all the fibers move almost in unison.

This is very different in natural bristles where more force bends the hair further, but it isn't like a linear increase in force. During the lather, the bristles conform to your face and the circular action seems to gently bent the hairs in one or the other direction. The brush also spreads a bit, as fibers are pushed and bent a little. Once you lift the natural hair brush off your face, the bristles don't string back all at once. Some fibers may return to their approximate straight form, but the water and soap mixture will clump some of them together.

I want to be clear that I don’t object to a different brush feel. As long as it does the job of lathering up and isn’t so coarse to feel like sandpaper, I’m fine. This synthetic fiber, on the other hand, are best compared to very playable, soft steel springs. Even when I tried to lather up very slowly and gingerly, each fiber literally snapped back to its original position. When you lift the brush off your face, all the bristles are back in place as if you just upacked the brush.

In summary, this brush is far from coming close to the feel of badger bristles. I cant use it without spraying soap all over and I wish I could return it, but it appears I’m stuck with this thing.

Tea tree oil foot scrub (made in the USA)

Tea tree oil foot balm (made in the USA)
This is the star of the show, it's heavenly. Smells refreshingly minty, makes your skin soft. Works on any dry skin, not just feet. I couldn't resist using a lot of this, so even though you get a lot, I have a feeling I'll be buying more fairly soon. I really notice the difference right away. Bag

Overall

review_title: Great product! Detailed review and pics.
review_text:
This product basically asks you to take a three-day vacation from your normal skin-care routine and only use the contents of a total of nine pretty small (0.05 ounce each) foil packets. You follow the three step process each night for three nights then only use a wet cloth to "wash" your face in the morning.

Because this product makes great promises in a VERY short period of time, (and for $20 for a small amount of product, let's be honest!) and because I read reviews before I make purchases, and because I was able to purchase this product at a discount in exchange for evaluation and my HONEST review, I have swallowed my pride (uhm, ego??!!??) and am not only going to share the process for this product but also, several of my "naked face" photos - before, during and after. This way you, my fellow Amazon buyer, may not only read my opinion BUT also decide for yourself how much difference this product made in at least this instance for me.

BASICS- I am a woman, former Marine and (ugh!) a smoker. I will be turning 50 in June 2016 and although I have (so far) not found any actual wrinkles, other than a couple of minor horizontal lines on my forehead (thanks Dad & grandma for the genetics!), I DID have fairly prominent acne from about 13 until after 30 (& even a couple now!) leaving scars mostly on my cheeks and chin. I also was a serious sun worshipper, getting as brown as I possibly could, including tanning beds, outdoor activities, the Marine Corps and beach/pool lounging (anyone my age group remember baby oil and iodine? The worst thing you can do for your skin?? Yep! That was me!). It honestly is a miracle I don't look like a raisin. I do have discoloration & brown patches all over my face. I stopped actively tanning just after my 40th birthday and now always wear sunscreen at least in my facial moisturizer. I do have a pretty good routine now because I want to try to preserve what I have and fight Mother Nature and gravity as much as possible, but my face needs some work.
ALL PHOTOS WERE TAKEN AT APPROX THE SAME TIME, IN THE SAME PLACE WITH CAMERA AT APPROX THE SAME DISTANCE FROM MY FACE (too close!!) AND IN THE SAME LIGHTING. NO FILTERS OR PHOTOSHOP USED.
BEFORE PICTURE- The "before" photo,
(hopefully these will show up in the proper order but in it I am wearing a grey t-shirt with black "squares" and a pony tail) shows the brown spots, scarring and general lack of "glow". This was the night I began the process.

THE PROCESS- Three steps/Three days
STEP ONE "Gentle Prep Cleanser"- The cleanser is a pearly white color (see photograph) The directions say it removes makeup, but as you can tell from my "before" pic, I did remove my makeup with a makeup remover cloth. I did this for two reason: 1- Because I didn't trust that the small amount of cleanser would actually remove makeup and clean enough and 2- Because I wanted naked skin to evaluate the cleanser itself. I need not have worried. The cleanser cleans the skin and prepares it for the "peel" product at step two. The cleanser was very pleasant "clean" smelling and although it foamed very little (see photo of this step) it amazingly did a great job of further cleansing the skin and removing every trace of makeup (I know this because I used a white wash cloth to rinse my face - no I didn't photograph the dirty cloth!). My skin felt quite clean, but not "squeaky/stripped", which is good, IMO.
STEP TWO- "Non-Irritating Pro Peel". This is a clear gel (see pic) which had a slight astringent smell to it. This is applied to the now clean and towel dries skin using fingertips. The directions say to keep it on for 5 minutes, or 2-3 for sensitive skin rinse them pat dry. I felt no tingling or burning at all, just the alcohol smell which is no big deal. This product does not dry like a mask and it doesn't turn white like some chemical peels are supposed to do. In fact, on the second night, I got distracted and left this on for over 10 minutes and still had no discomfort at all. When rinsing, be careful to avoid the eyes. After this step, my skin did feel kind of tight but not in an uncomfortable way at all!
STEP THREE- "Radiance Renewing Deep Moisturizer"- OH MY GOODNESS!!! I absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE this moisturizer!!! I am going to try finding this alone for use as a night cream. As you can see from the photos of the "dots" of moisturizer on my face, there was not a lot of the cream in the packet & I thought it would not be enough (I ALWAYS treat my neck all around and my chest area with the same process as my face!) but - again - I was wrong to be worried. This moisturizer feels so very good! I honestly wanted to use it all over. When I find the moisturizer alone, I will edit this review and add the name of the product! This cream was the perfect way to end the process.

All three steps took less than 15 minutes per night.

The "after" photo was taken this morning because I wanted to allow the third night's process to fully work, so the lighting is a bit different. If anything, the daylight is harsher than the night photos and I took this picture even closer so I could really see.

RESULTS- It is usually difficult to be objective about your own appearance. At least it is for me. I look at this face each day and see all my faults. However, I honestly can say that I have noticed smaller pore appearance and brighter, smoother skin. Putting on my makeup this morning was so much easier and to my great surprise, the makeup actually lasted well the entire day without the blotchy, tired appearance I usually find by the end of the day (the photo of me with makeup shows that my hair has definitely fallen and my eyes look tired but the foundation held up pretty well!). I did do an informal survey of a few friends, texting only the before and after photos for their candid opinions. The feedback was quite good! I am an "average looking" woman, and this product did not make me suddenly a Cover Girl, but in my honest opinion, this product is a clear winner! At the $19.99 price point, I am definitely going to be repeating this "Three-Day Vacation" again... Perhaps up to four times a year!

I do enjoy testing products and sharing my experience, and hope the information I share helps other Amazon customers decide if a product is right for them, so if you find my review at all helpful (either good or bad for the product) please let me know by selecting "yes" in response to the question "was this review helpful?" At the bottom of this review. Also, please feel free to ask me any additional questions you may have. I am happy to help as much as I can!

review_title: "It's fancy, and it IS what it says it IS"...
review_text:
It comes in a nice looking metal can. It says it is a MEDIUM SHINE and a MEDIUM HOLD styling aid and my years of research trying endless styling aids to tame my 80s' bowl do genetics concurs 100%. Seriously though, my hair has like 5% body to it so I shifted to short/shorter hairstyles about 5 years ago which are easier to control. My hair is on the thicker side and very straight

It most definitely looks like a putty with a semi-firm smooth texture and a white color. The SNIFF does seem to have notes of black pepper and pipe tobacco but they are dulled way down likely to avoid being overbearing or offensive. The HOLD is flexible and can be molded/shaped. There is a slight oiliness or greasy "to the touch" feel but that is quite normal when you're talking about "medium" or "high" shine hair products.

I used it on my "mini mini faux hawk" and it allowed me to form it together on top and it held which not all medium/medium products accomplish. I emulsified it in my fingers and applied it to DRY hair. I am very happy with how it works for this style of cut. All in all, a nice product which works splendidly for my favorite style of cut.

review_title: "Sniff's good, work's good, look's good -- it's all good"...
review_text:
My hair is super straight, fairly thick and has about 5% body to it. Without hair product it would form a "bowl do" in 2.2 seconds or less. My typical hair styles that I do myself since the pandemic are a Semper Fi look, a mini mini fauxhawk and a buzz cut since I work in the loss prevention/security field.

The REVIEW:

-- I didn't find it to be too greasy or oily to the touch. If you like the "wet look" there is going to need to be some oil or glycerin so I'm okay with a certain amount of oil or glycerin to get that medium to high shine I prefer.
-- You need to apply it to DRY hair. I emulsify it and apply it to my hair (I built it up in very small amounts to avoid overdoing it) and it covered my hair pretty well and adhered well which is always easier on dry hair. I did need to touch up some spots since I just gave myself a "mini mini fauhawk" and a couple areas were fighting back.
-- COLOR = pearl white and has an airy light look to it like it was aerated or a tiny bit of mousse was added (but it surely wasn't). That mousse look is gone once you dig into the top and begin working with it.
-- SNIFF = light pleasant fragrance but I can't place anything beyond that. Nothing offensive. I wish it had a citrus scent (i.e. grapefruit, orange or lemon) but this is fine.
-- CONTAINER = not cheap looking; nice printing and quality materials with clear directions and ingredient list
-- FIRM HOLD = firm hold but not extreme or super hold thus it allows some give or flexibility in the hair
-- SHINE is MEDIUM = this is true but it leans toward a high shine
-- TEXTURE = firm to the touch but has some flexibility so your hair isn't entirely locked into place; not crisp or crunchy but it is firm
-- For my "mini mini fauxhawk" hairstyle it works quite well and allows me to form my hair at the top and it holds in place. My favorite styling products had high shine and medium hold, but this product is making me re-think my preferences.

SUMMARY:

For my wants and needs it works really well on my preferred "mini mini fauxhawk" style. It really is what it says it is. This is a real gem of a styling aid.

I've been using the Diffuser for a few weeks and I found it to be a great unit. I like that you do not need distilled water to use it. Its the first we've owned that doesn't need distilled water.

The directions state to use only 3 to 5 drops of oil. I found that using 3 drops doesn't do much. Depending what oils I'm adding to the diffuser I can easily drop 5 to 8 drops. For the most part, 5 drops is what we are happy with. It will keep a 200 square foot room diffused with oils as long as the diffuser is running.

The lighting effects work great and we generally run them at night as a night light in the kitchen. At other times we run it for fun. The timers works great but we rarely use that feature. We just turn it on and it runs for several hours (never timed it) until it runs out and shuts off.

I don't like the ending noise alerts. They are loud and at night they will wake us up. I can't complain to much about this because most diffusers have the loud beeping noise.

Tips:

Before adding more drops then the instructions states, follow their suggest usage and see if you like the smell. If its not enough, then add more drops until you get the desired effect during your next few runs.

Don't set it up to close to you or your work space. If its set it up to close, I found that the mist creates is very strong and gives me a headache. For the most part, I only use it when I'm working on the other side of the room. When I need to be near the diffuser, I turn off until I'm done.

review_title: Thick hair, but U-tips are huge for fine hair. Removal breaks natural hair. Please see update!
review_text:
My once beautiful long hair is finally growing back in from chemotherapy for breast cancer. I had had it bonded by my hair salon about 6 months ago with Cinderella bonds that shed like a cat almost immediately and had hair that was split and damaged before I ever even washed it.

I took a chance on ordering 2-18 inch packs of #613 and 2-16 inch packs of #613 of Sunny hair. The hair looked beautiful and was a perfect match for my own color, but there is no way of telling until it's been washed, conditioned and blown out over a few weeks to really know how it will hold up.

My stylist, who specializes in hot fusion bonds, put in 1 pack of the 18 inch Sunny hair (50 U tips) and one pack of Cinderella hair (25 U tips) 5 days ago. I have very fine hair and a tiny head, so more would not have been possible (this amount also equals a full head of hair for me). We are experimenting to see which hair holds up better.

After one wash, conditioning and blow dry yesterday, the high priced Cinderella hair was tangling in the middle, while the Sunny hair stayed tangle-fee, but did shed quite a bit. The Sunny hair has more weight to it than the much more expensive hair though and combed out better.

One star off for how huge the actual keratin U-tip are and the shedding. My stylist tried to cut some of the tip off with great difficulty. This is an FYI for those with fine hair or those who want to be able to pull it back without the bond showing (the more expensive type has much smaller Keratin u-tips).

I will update this review after 4 weeks in, but for now, I'd like to thank other reviewers for their input as it helped me choose Sunny hair. You were all correct in saying the hair is thicker than most online hair, even though each strand is a bit different in strand width, health and quality. As the industry is unregulated, it's hard to know what you're getting and with blonde hair, just how much processing went into coloring the hair (causing damage).

If my Sunny hair holds up well, my stylist, who does at least 10 hot fusion bondings per month on clients, will be ordering directly from Sunny hair instead of the company that charges $125-$150 per pack. We are both hoping this is the case.

I hope others will try this brand and leave reviews on their experiences. Also, if this is your first time with bonds, please remember on length that it's not going from the top of your head. The lower layers will fall much longer - I'm 5'7 with a long neck and the 18 inch lower tiers fall just a few inches above my waist.

UPDATE: please don't buy this hair if you value your natural hair.
It's impossible to remove the bonds without breaking your own hair.
It breaks, frizzes, knots up like crazy if in a warm climate.
I loved those first packs until summertime. Absolutely awful in heat and humidity. I couldn't get a brush through the hair. It would just snap off. The knots were horrific. I had my hairdresser try to remove and this is more like crazy glue on the bond than keratin.

review_title: Not sure what all the fuss is about...
review_text:
I will be the first to admit I hate taking baths; it bores me out of my skull. But because I have chronic pain, I've occasionally taken Epsom salt baths or bubble baths with a fantastic product called Muscle Soak. I found the salts were no longer really helping, so I thought I'd try these magnesium flakes. I take magnesium daily but a boost through the muscles that ache sounds great.

I was floored at how quickly and completely they dissolved. The tub wasn't done filling and they were fully absorbed into the water. With salts, I have to get in and stir repeatedly to get the crystals to dissolve, often in water that's hotter than comfortable. So that was promising.

I got in the tub and lay back, focused on the flower print on the wall....and was ready to get out in 15 minutes, but I wanted to give it the full 30. I wasn't magically relaxed or calmed by the bath as other reviewers are claiming. (You literally can't tell the flakes are there, as the water isn't salty like it is with Epsom salts.) I wasn't whisked away to a lush garden in my mind. I was just lying in a bathtub with pleasantly hot/warm water. While I was in the water and for up to an hour after I got out and showered, I felt a limited, temporary reduction in the tightness in my upper back. I put on a compression shirt to help things along but had 9/10 pain. When I can next score some Muscle Soak, I'll be going back to that. The bubbles are at least something to play with! And it is more effective on achy muscles.

This is not a magic cure for stress or pain. I'll use it to soak my feet when they ache, but don't expect miracles. If Epsom salts don't make a big difference, these flakes probably won't either.

Or, for those who prefer to view all events in a positive light, someone should be promoted. I was fortunate enough - or so I thought - to receive the [[ASIN:B001A0GDQE Philips Norelco Arcitec 1090 Rechargeable Cordless Men's Shaving System]] last year and although it is not a comparison of equals, I now also have the Cool Skin 8040x. The 1090x is Philips/Norelco's flagship razor and this one is more of a middle of the road competitively priced product so any comparison is unfair...for the 1090x. For the last month, I've alternated between this razor and the 1090x, and my impression is without reservation, the 8040x delivers a superior cut. I've finally found a cordless that eliminates the need to keep some manual razors in reserve. Whomever led this product development team is making the top tier team look bad.

Notwithstanding bells and whistles, the primary function of any razor is to offer a smooth, comfortable shave and this rechargeable gets the job done with aplomb, with or without utilization of the moisturizing system, whether employed as a wet or dry shaver. I'm not a real big fan of products that obligate additional expenditures for consumables like the Nivea Conditioner but I realize it is a nice feature for those who may need the conditioner to avoid skin irritation. I would recommend Nivea and Norelco team up to produce a fragrance free version as this product does conflict with other scents the consumer might use. It is not my practice to use the conditioner every time I shave (every other day) but at my present rate, I would anticipate the initial conditioner supply will last at least six months.

Cleaning the shaver is a snap. Just turn it on and wash the heads under hot running water. I wish the upscale model cleaned as efficiently, but then, as I facetiously stated in another review my primary use for that pricey unit is as a display item now.

This razor's tracking system follows facial contours (head in my case) quite efficiently and does not require anywhere near as much pressure to achieve a close cut on stubble as has been my experience with the top of the line model. Additionally, the relatively compact size and shape is easier to manipulate. The 8040x also has a detachable trim head that can be used for close grooming and you can actually see what you're doing, another advantage over the premium model. Just pull off the tracker head and lightly press on the trimmer attachment.

Charge time for a full charge is about four hours for 40 minutes of shave time. There is a 9 minute quick charge capability that provides enough power for a three minute shave. The charging stand has a reasonably small footprint although for convenience and my take on durability, the charging cord has to be unplugged but remain attached to the base. The inexpensive plastic retainer does not look as though it would withstand multiple rotations. The travel locking feature is a nice touch but the travel case is a joke.

Yet, for nearly $150 less than the top of the line model and superior shaving capability, I'll figure out how to securely pack it.

The curling iron heats up very quickly and you can read the temperature as it is rising. The barrels do not have clamps. I had to use some heat spray and hold on my daughter's hair and it did not stick to the barrels. I accidentally put it down next to a plastic bag. The bag melted on the barrel but was easily wiped off with a tissue. There is a straightening brush attachment that you can use as well.
The barrels are easy to fit into the handle: just line up the pins, push down and turn to lock them in place. Where you push them in does not get hot so you can change out your barrels while you're doing your styling.
The cord on this unit is 6' long.
Great value for multi use curling wands.

review_title: It actually works!  This is pretty amazing on my curly hair!
review_text:
I am always sceptical when I see advertisements on TV for products that seem 'AMAAAAZZZZING! MUST BUY NOW!!'
I wasn't too sure what to expect with this. I thought it was gimmicky, but I am happy to be proven wrong.
This is so much easier to use than a flat iron.
I like that it has a digital LCD that shows you what temperature the brush is heating up to. It gives the heat range that your hair styling should be at depending on thickness, etc. I set mine to 230, the hottest setting and it worked great for my thick, curly hair.
It heats up very quickly and the hand grip is comfortable. The cord rotates from the end and the grip on the back of the wand feels nice in the hand.
The rubbery nubs on the ends of the bristles offer some flexibility, but they are not as flexible as your hairbrush. They are also shorter, too.
The way that you do this is to start with clean, well brushed hair. As the bristles are short, they will not detangle for you. Have your hair prepped and ready. If you use a smoothing serum, it would be perfect to add it before you start with this.
You simply brush it over your hair like you would a hairbrush. You can brush from underneath or on top to make sure that all the hair gets close to the heated plate of the brush.
You can spend more time on areas that you want straightened more but I found that my doing my hair in pieces (held up with an alligator clip) worked best for me.
In order to get to the roots at the scalp, it was very easy. The brush is easy to angle towards the scalp and it gets about 1/2" away from the scalp easily and starts straightening from there.
If you hair is damp, you will see some steam, but you'd expect that with a curling iron or flatiron, too.
This actually worked so well, my kids wanted to try it out and they loved it!
The only concern that I had was that if you hair is the type to come out when you brush it, it will come out when you use this, too. The issue was removing the hair from the straightener. It is HOT. I had to work quickly to sweep the excess hair from the brush to toss. I will keep a wide tooth comb by this the next time I use it so I can run it over the bristles and remove the hair.
All in all: I give this a strong thumbs up!
I can't speak about the others on the market, but this one really does what it says it will do. It is way better than a flat iron. It covers more ground and feels more comfortable in the hand. Its a natural movement to brush your hair and this is no different.
Excellent new beauty tool! Very happy that this does what it claims to do! Part of my daily hair regime now!

I was looking for a manicure device for natural nails. According to other reviewers, this doesn’t work well on acrylic or gel, which I’ve never used, so I thought I would give it a try on my natural nails. It was a good decision! It was also a good price, which was helpful since I have never used one and only heard of “nail drills” when I searched for emery boards. I couldn’t figure out who would want to drill their nails! It sounded like a torture device! It turned out to be easy and painless.

This is a great little manicure kit. I got it yesterday, charged it, and tried it today. It’s very easy to use. The instruction manual told me everything I needed to know to use it, including that it shuts off after two minutes, but you can simply turn it back on. For me, that’s not a problem. It is not faulty if it shuts off after two minutes. It’s supposed to do that. The device has two speeds, and it can reverse directions.

I was concerned about vibration, but this didn’t vibrate noticeably to me. I really dislike using an emery board or other manual file because it feels uncomfortable. Filing with this little machine was so much better. It even has a light that shines on the work area. I also used the fine sander to smooth my nails, and then polish them. It was very easy, and the shine is amazing.

It is rechargeable through USB. It comes with a cord that has a special end to plug into the manicure tool. The other end plugs into a USB wall charger which is not supplied. Again, for me that was not a problem as I have quite a few of those in the house.

The kit comes with 1 grinder to file nails, 2 coarse sandpaper disks, 2 fine nail file boards (look similar to sandpaper disks, but much finer), and 2 EVA polish rollers. It also has a small bag of 10 extra assorted sticker, of the types I just mentioned. I am not sure how long each one lasts or how to order more if I need them. I couldn’t find the information in the Amazon description or in the manual that came with the kit. I’ll keep looking.

I charged this in the bedroom overnight. When charging, the device has a light that flashes during charging, but stops flashing and remains on once charged. It’s pretty bright on a nightstand in a dark bedroom. I’ll probably charge it during the day! The first charge took about three hours.

I hope this continues working as well as it did on my first try. As of now, I highly recommend this MiroPure kit. If that changes for any reason, I will update this post.

review_title: Works well overall - but "bristles" vary in length year to year, become brittle and break off too easily.
review_text:
It is difficult to find a large barreled curling iron/brush. HELEN OF TROY offers a broad range of assorted sizes, and they work well. This is my third or fourth purchase of this same model in about 10 years. Even though I purchase the same model, I find that the hard plastic "bristles" vary in height from year to year. The short "bristles" sometimes place the hot barrel too close to my skin, especially when the "bristles" break off (which is fairly easy and common, possibly due to overexposure to heat). The models that arrived with longer "bristles" are more suited for longer hair, however they sometimes "tangle" in the hair -- and THEY, too break off all too easily. (I have recommended to the manufacturer that they add something slightly more flexible to the "bristles" to keep them from getting brittle and breaking, or perhaps design the barrels so that new sets of bristles can be installed, however -- why would they take my suggestion when consumers can simply replace the entire unit with a new one?) The heating elements in these units have never failed; only the "bristles" are problematic.

Overall, I like this model, but I find that I need to replace it after about 12-18 months of use due to loss of "bristles".

review_title: The silver bullet for small breed teeth problems.
review_text:
We have a lot of dogs and they’re chihuahuas. They are known for having notoriously bad teeth as a breed even when you do everything right. Our littlest has been losing teeth left and right and is at the age where cleanings are too scary with her size. She would realistically need a cleaning much more often than yearly because the plaque builds up so fast.

I bought this as a shot in the dark, as we have burned hundreds on every product known to man. I mixed the product parts together in the large bottle and sprayed 4 of our dogs’ teeth as instructed. After a SINGLE application, our girl with the bad teeth had a 25% reduction in plaque. Our other three had a reduction of 40%, 60%, and 90%. I am not joking - this stuff has carbolic acid in it and it WORKS. The two components mixed causes some type of fizzy reaction and really works between the plaque and teeth/gums and between teeth. I tasted it first myself to be sure it wouldn’t be traumatizing to our pups and it tastes like flavorless alcohol free mouthwash.

Since, I continue to spray once or twice a day as I remember to and the plaque keeps disappearing. I did check with my dental tools to be sure it wasn’t just bleaching the plaque and it is not- it’s physically breaking off their teeth. I don’t know how we will get larger bottles of the stuff with the number of dogs we have but it’s true, it works. I paid my actual money and used it on my real dogs. This is not a paid or discounted review. Please give this a shot on your Littles!

review_title: Best value in $/oz for a true believer
review_text:
I bought this giant pack after trying the 16oz tea tree oil cleansing conditioner and did some crazy calculation on the total/average cost of different ways of purchasing this really expensive hair cleansing product from multiple sources.

Obviously, you can tell I'm quite convinced by this product, or else I wouldn't invest so much work/resources into getting it. Because these things take a while to use, I will be updating my review as I finish each flavor included in this set. I will not be using the Sweet Almond Mint, which is too oily for me and I'm sure you can find plenty of review on other package sizes.

* Overall Impression *

1. Great reduction in hair loss
2. Great increase in manageability
3. Quite expensive for regular use

A lot of people say "this product changed my life!" I don't want to exaggerate my excitement. I think to be very fair this product made me discover something I never experienced with other commercial shampoos - "near zero hair loss after wash".

I was a heavy shedder and I was used to losing a lot of hair everyday. With this product, I hardly lose any piece of hair at all during the day, with everything else being the same as my old-shampoo days. I have to say I don't know how it will compare to shampoo during hair wash with an equal comparison (i.e. same washing technique). WEN requires you to comb your hair during washing, which causes hair to shed when I wash my hair. I did not comb my hair while I was using shampoos so I didn't know if combing in wash would be the same. All else being the same, I lose about the same amount of hair during washing using shampoo or WEN. The no hair loss during the day is amazing though. I might have been allergic to the commercial shampoos and never knew it. My hair now feels significantly thicker when putting into a pony tail.

Another great discovery is that WEN makes my hair very smooth, light but not necessarily shiny. It dries faster after wash. It also feels easier to manage - my hair now stays in the right shape - this is especially true after the 24 hours. My hair would have started to feel lumpy and oily if I had used shampoo, but WEN keeps my scalp evenly moist a little longer. With these two improvements, I no longer use styling products or a blow dryer.

* Impression on the Flavors I Have Tried *

Tea Tree 5 of 5
Fig 5 of 5
Cucumber Aloe 3 of 5

Very short, I would recommend people with oily/combination skin type stay away from the Cucumber Aloe. Somehow it feels more water-based I had to use more to wash each time. At the same time, even though I make sure to wash it off completely, my scalp/hair started to feel oily sooner than when I use tea tree and fig versions. Both Tea Tree and Fig are great for oily/combination type. They make my hair feel clean and refreshed. Fig makes my hair feels extra smooth and it is the richest/densest of the three.

* How Long Does a 32oz Bottle Last? *

When the WEN TV infomercial says the 12oz starter version is a "30-day" supply, you need to understand that it is for people with very short, thin, or little hair. For someone like me with long, very thick Asian hair going to mid back, the 16oz tea tree bottle survived barely one month with washing at least every other day.

Two other things to keep in mind:
The 32oz pump holds more than a 16oz pump, but less than twice the amount.
Each flavor varies in its moisture strength. As mentioned earlier, I had to use more Cucumber Aloe to achieve the same effect I can do with Tea Tree and Fig.

I made a chart documenting my process of finishing up the 32oz Cucumber Aloe bottle. In total there were about 250 pumps, which lasted me 50 days with 30 washes, average 8 pumps per wash.

* How Much Should You Use For Each Wash? *

I definitely recommend strictly following the WEN instructions when you begin. That is, use the large amount as instructed by WEN, follow the steps to rinse, massage, comb, leave in, rinse off. This will help you see how the proper use can really change your hair as they've claimed. However, this is an expensive product so we all want to use it efficiently. Once you have formed the proper washing habit, start reducing the pump number little by little until you find your optimal dose. I found my optimal to be about 1/2 of the recommended amount for my hair length. Given the amount of hair I have, I'm sure many people can save more once you've started using it.

On average I use:
Tea Tree 16oz - 15 pumps per wash (haven't started the 32oz bottle yet)
Cucumber Aloe 32oz - 8-9 pumps per wash
Fig 32oz - 7 pumps per wash

A couple of tips for application: make sure you place the squared end at the tip of your nail; the rounded end sits on the nail bed (and this will prevent accidental lifting). Additionally, USE THE ALCOHOL PAD that is supplied to ensure all oils are off your nails before application. This will help the adhesive adhere much better and stay on longer.

Once again, these are beautiful and the pictures don't do them justice. My fiancé wishes she could get her gel nails in flat black now. The textured silver nails were a bonus. Not sure how she's going to live without something similar now. The extra adhesive pads (as seen in the pics) will allow her to use these multiple times as well. Highly recommend them if you're looking for something easy for a quick night out, without having to find time to run to the manicurist, or if you just don't want something permanent.

review_title: 6 sticks, each with their own blender brush
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:9d6b73448b9c4669051332c7b4e0f4e9]] I was actually shopping for another cream eyeshadow stick by Julep that I really liked and found these instead with a blender BRUSH instead of a foam pad. I loved the one I had of the other brand, but the sponge blender kind of burned when I used it. It was just too rough for the eye area (mine, anyway).

At first I thought this set was just one eyeshadow stick and I was trying to figure out how to choose which color or purple I wanted. Then I saw that it was SIX STICKS and each color had its own blender brush. OMG! This makes it an amazing deal! There's not a single shade of these that I won't wear and I usually wear about 3 colors from the set at once.

These colors are really pretty as well as very soft and flattering. I used the video to show the colors on my light skin since a lot of times I'm wondering how something will look on me. These are frosty shades of purple, meaning they are sparkly. A lot of them are kind of a brownish purple, which I was happy to see.

Each end has a cap. The brush end is where you twist to raise and lower the stick. The brush is very soft, like a regular makeup brush. You can put the cap from the colored end over the brush cap and it stays on. Totally handy!

I was wish each cap on the color end was the color of the eyeshadow, but then I realized the color is written on the side in the color of the shade. Now I can find the one I want much faster. The cream eyeshadow glides on wonderfully without dragging your eyelid. It blends easily and looks so nice. If you're looking for waterproof all-day color, this isn't it. Otherwise, this is a great set that you'll have so much fun with. I prefer cream makeup now that I"m older and these are probably the best eyeshadow sticks I've had.

The best things about these sticks (aside from the gorgeous purple colors)? That each stick has it's own blending brush. You don't have to worry about mixing colors on your brush or even using your own brushes. The brush on the end is what sold me and I'm just so thrilled they are as soft as they are. Couldn't be happier.

This is the best little set and I'll buy it again when I use it up. I'd love it if they came out with a burgundy set and I'd also buy a smoky set (hint, hint, hint). A smoky set would be wow. I specifically bought this brand because customer reviews said they didn't smell strongly. I have asthma and strong smells give me an asthma attack, but it's nice to have a smell-good in the shower. I've used bath bombs, but shower bombs had never occurred to me until I saw them on amazon. What a nice treat! They came nicely packed and none of the bombs were broken.

As soon as they came, I jumped in the shower to try one out. Let me just say that I take super looooong showers. Like until the hot water runs out lol. The bomb lasted my whole shower and didn't leave a trace when it was all gone. I couldn't even tell where it was, so it didn't mark or stain my shower at all.

Other reviewers complained about the scent being too weak, but I thought the strength of the scent was just right. If it were any stronger, I'd have had an asthma attack and that would've sucked. It was enough scent that I felt like I was treating myself, but not strong enough to bother my lungs. Even an hour later, I could still smell the scent of the shower bomb in the bathroom. Beats the heck out of the usual Hints de Kitty Litter lol

Anyway, I think these shower bombs are lovely and I have no problem recommending them to my friends. Even my asthmatic friends lol

review_title: Rich lotion with an ingredient that I'm not a fan of.
review_text:
It's me again. That Irish girl with the picky skin :)
This time we are trying Clia Natural Facial Moisturizer.
I like when a product has an easy to read ingredients panel, either on their product, or the accompanying box. If not, at least have on their product page a complete list of ingredients so I know what's in it, so I can make an informed decision if this is a product for me and my sensitive skin.
The box I received this product in was a simple, plain cardboard box.
The writing on the label is miniscule at best.
I blew up the attached images so I could read what it actually said. One of the first 5 ingredients is Palm Oil. I'm not a fan of Palm Oil for environmental reasons. The growth and harvest of palm oil is not kind to our planet. That's my personal feelings on the matter.

The cream itself is very rich and smooth without a chemical smell, more like your typical face cream.
I did the back of my hand test first to check for a reaction. There was none, so the next morning I applied the cream to one half of my face for the "face" test.
This cream is VERY rich. Just lightly tap your fingers on the open jar, and you'll get just the right amount. A little goes a long way.
I applied it to my forehead, cheek and neck. It absorbed fairly quickly with no greasy residue.
DId it pass the no breakout, no hives test? Yes it did, and my skin felt softer throughout the day without drying out or leaving any dry patches.
Overall, it's a good, luxurious feeling lotion, but with that Palm Oil in there, i'm not 100% on board, so, I'm really at 3.75 stars on this product
Disclosure: I received this product at a discount for my honest review.

TL; DR: I can't recommend this dry facial brush enough.

Beurer Foot Bath Massager, Water Tempering, Relaxing Vibration Massage and Bubble Massage Functions for Tired Feet, Includes 3 Pedicure Attachments, FB21 by Beurer North America. Of course, our feet play an important role throughout our lives as they have to bear our full weight: and each foot has 26 bones, 22 joints and 107 ligaments that may all need care. Beurer North America says that this foot bath will be a simple and convenient solution for sore and tired feet. The bath has three setting functions (water heating, vibration and bubble massage), an integrated water heater. The infrared light points will support the soothing effect of the foot massage. The three exchangeable pedicure tip can deliver a cleansing foot care treatment. The massage-assisted foot bed, Beurer states, will stimulate the feet; the detachable roller attachments will give a soothing foot reflexology massage; the double-walled housing ensures better thermal insulation. It includes a removable splash protection guard, convenient draining outlet, infrared light points to support the soothing effect of the foot massage.

I expect Beurer North America is a branch of a German company, and I am as awed by German engineering and technology as anyone else. But Beurer’s claims that this device can deliver a professional quality luxury spa experience are, frankly, silly. The item is more of a novelty than anything else. To begin with, I know nothing about German bathrooms, but in this country, any electrical outlets in bathrooms seem inevitably to be near the sink. The cord provided is not long enough to allow the item’s use in the tub without an extension cord, which, considering the well-known risks of mixing electricity and water, adds an unnecessary element of risk. So you will probably end up sitting on the toilet seat, or may have to bring in a chair. And the gadget is messy; you’d better put it on a towel. That being said, it did make my feet feel marginally better after a long tough day. Will you find it useful? That depends on how much you’re willing to spend on it, and whether you have room for one more bathroom gadget of limited utility.

I long since stopped shaving my underarms because the stubble grows in faster than a man's 5 o'clock shadow and is painful and this kind of hair removal solves that problem. review_title: Takes some practice to get right
review_text:
I've seen these type of curlers around for a while now and had been curious to try them out. However, upon opening them, I was disappointed by the size. If you have long hair and a lot of it, one pack will definitely not be enough, as is the case for me.
I was confused as to how to put them on. However, luckily for me, my sister knew how to do it since she had seen someone else try out this same style of curlers, but from another brand. Since she knew how to apply them, I told her to try them out for me and let me know, because I knew I'd end up frustrated.
Here's her take on them: They are tricky to apply at first and it takes a while to apply them, so make sure you have something else to keep you busy while you do this. However, once you know what you are doing, they're no longer tricky, but they are still time consuming. It takes time to section out the hair, put the curler in, roll it up, and repeat. Also, it is best if you do this at night if you are someone who has a sensitive head and is prone to headaches from wearing certain hairstyles. I put these on at around 3 p.m. and wore them for the rest of the day. After applying them, I was lounging around and watching a movie. Since I was laying down, I didn't notice any discomfort. However, once I was sitting up, it wasn't long before I felt a tension headache coming on. So, I would say that these are not good for someone who is sensitive to pressure from hairstyles. They don't look heavy, but there is a certain weight to having your hair "pulled" into the curler which can cause discomfort. I decided to sleep with them on, and was able to sleep just fine, since I didn't have any of the curlers directly on the back of my head. Upon taking them out, I had some nice curls, but I also had some wonky ones. I don't know the exact cause of that (rolled wrong, hair not pulled in correctly, moved during sleep, etc). However, I still liked the results and the curls held up for me, despite not having using any curling cream, gel, or anything.
All in all, they're a good product to try out and they allow you to get some curls without heat styling, but they can be tricky to use.

review_title: Right now it is tied as my favorite retinol product. It beat ROC products for me.
review_text:
I received a complimentary bottle of this serum to review on my blog. I really love it. I had finished my old retinol serum, which I liked and was ready to purchase another bottle until I was asked to review this serum on my blog. I like that this product is light. It has the same lightness as OZ Natural's hyaluronic serum. A little goes a long way. Two pumps of the serum is the most you will need. The serum absorbs quickly into the skin. Allow a full minute to go by before you apply another product over it. That initial absorption you see is just ti drying faster on the top layer of skin. It takes about a minute for serums to absorb deeper into the skin. Allowing this time prevent the pilling when you a moisturizer too soon.

Give this product about four weeks to see any real results. Retinol products take months of use to see any impact on deeper issue like lines and wrinkles. Initially you will feel a surface difference where skin my feel smoother or even softer. A couple of weeks later you may see some lighter scars fading. If you are battle crow feet apply a little of this serum at the corners of your eyes (don't get the product in eyes though) before you apply your eye cream. The two working together will give you better results.

I have the T770 model depicted above, so I've been a happy user for nearly two years. In his review, Reuben gives good tips on the use of this trimmer: take your time when you use it and clean it out after every use. The first results in even trimming; the second allows the vacuum to work best. Yes, a few hairs will show up in the sink, but with one swipe with a damp tissue they're gone. The adjustable comb trims beard, mustache, goatee, etc., to any length a user might want. In addition to the trimmer, the mustache and sideburn clipper gives a precise and neat edge; to use it, just remove the comb.

Taking the T770 apart to clean the blades is easy; getting it back together properly requires careful assembly in good lighting and some patience. I have generally straight hair, but it tends to get frizzy and wavy especially in high humidity or after working out. The Professional Hair Straightener Brush Best for Beauty 40W Digital Electric Straightening Comb by Magnifeko will be a great tool to bring on my upcoming vacation to the Caribbean! Now after using it for a good 6 months I would definitely recommend DND base and top coat for most clients.

I'm a licensed Instructor and nail tech, I've been doing nails for almost 20 years, I do gel polish by leaving the base coat on. (basically by doing a fill every 2 weeks, not a new set.) I only remove the gel polish color and prep the re-growth and apply base coat to the new growth. That said, the only issue Ive had on a couple clients is the base coat can get a little soft after several months if my client's hand are in water and/or chemicals a lot. So I need to remove the entire base coat and start all over every few months. This isn't the end of the world but to avoid having to do this, I use a different base coat on clients who are hairdressers or for those who have their hands in water a lot.
That is the base coat only and on just a few clients. I haven't had any issue like that with the top coat. I have since re-purchased this duo several times. I will continue to do so. :0)

review_title: Glides on smoothly and does a decent job on my skin.
review_text: I have really oily skin, especially in my T-zone region. I normally rely on blotting paper but sometimes, I feel like it smudges my makeup or requires me to go through a couple of sheets before it gets the job done. I decided to give this product a try. I have seen an ad for something like this before from Revlon and have been meaning to get my hands on it. This set comes with 2 volcanic balls, a holder, drying mat and drawstring bag. The volcanic ball did a decent job of removing excess oil without ruining my makeup. It took a couple of tries in some areas versus others. I felt a slight cooling effect while using this. This glides smoothly on to the skin. It is very compact so you can take it wherever you go and it can be washed and reused.

review_title: Stencils are one time use only...
review_text: This eyebrow kit includes an air cushion eyebrow stamp, 24 sticker stencils, and 4 eyebrow brushes. The stencils come in a variety of different shapes and are really easy to use, unfortunately you can only use them one time. The stamp provided a fairly natural color and washed off with just water so I'm kind of skeptical about the smudgeproof/waterproof claim. This is great if you have to do your makeup in a hurry. It would have been better if the stencils were reusable.

review_title: Natural beige is still pretty light
review_text: This is a concealer in a cushion powder form. It comes in a compact with a magnetic closure and included sponge. It only comes in 2 colors: light beige and natural beige. I got the natural beige which is still on the lighter side and is best for fair to light complexions. This provides good coverage and blends easily. It applies like a liquid but dries like a powder.

review_title: Requires some effort for application but stays on pretty well.....
review_text: This is a pack of 2 mechanical brow liners in the color brown. These are dual ended pencils so one end has a brow brush while the other end has the eyebrow product. The pencils have a beautiful gold casing that is slim and comfortable to grasp. I think the formula is a little dry so I had to apply some pressure for the desired color payout. The fine tip allows you to draw in precise brow hairs. The staying power is great and held up well throughout my 8+ hour work day. I wanted to test out the waterproof claim so I did shower without washing my face and the color didn't really budge if left untouched. It came off easily using a makeup wipe.

review_title: Dissolves easily, smells great, and provides a good lather....
review_text: This set contains 3 packs of soap sheets with the following scents/fragrances: Lavender & Aloe, Bergamot & Ylang Ylang, Jasmine & Patchouli. There are 80 sheets in each pack. The sheets are thin and dissolve easily with water. It provides a good amount of lather and smells wonderful. I used the Jasmine & Patchouli scent today and it's pretty long lasting. My hands felt clean, soft, and moisturized afterwards. This set comes with a storage tin so it's perfect for traveling or camping.

This combo set comes with 3 different “spa” treats: a set of eye patches, feet masks and lip mask. It has a you need to pamper you’re self from head to toe. Here are my 2 cents on each:

Lip mask - it’s big and easily for around my entire mouth. Felt nice and moisturizing on my lips. Leaves you unable to talk for at least 20 min

Feet mask - smells like eucalyptus… nice and cooling on my feet… there are tabs on the side to hold them in place. Feet felt so soft and moisturized after removal. There was no dry spot in sight. I rubbed the rest of the serum all over my legs.

Eye patch - cool and soothing on my face… stays in place even with me moving around freely.

This is a great set of 6 bright, pastel colored gel polishes. Each bottle has a sticker on top to mark the color, which is 100% accurate. The polish is on the thicker side so you only need 1-2 coats for opacity. These will be my go to all summer long!

Oh what luxury! When I opened this package I was delighted by the scent, if you're a fan of peppermint mochas (or even if you're not) it smells amazing, both comforting and refreshing.  I scooped out about 2 tablespoons and applied it on my upper arms and elbows and immediately knew I loved it. I've had two experiences with body scrubs, ones that contain oils and ones that do not. I find the ones that contain oil work better because they exfoliate the skin as advertised but do so without creating redness and irritation, plus they moisturize so the end result is soft smooth skin, almost to the effect of those in-shower body moisturizers that are popular these days. Body scrubs that don't contain oil can't feel like a sandpaper and make you wonder if they're even worth using. After using this one I quickly realized it just HAD to contain oils, my skin felt SOOO moisturized! Sure enough I looked at the ingredients and it did contain various oils. Once I experienced the results I scooped out another handful and went to town on my knees and shins. I love this stuff! It creates the ultimate spa-like shower experience, plus the peppermint oil combined with the hot steam from the shower helped me breathe better which I liked...it almost felt therapeutic. My one critique is that the bag made it a bit tricky to use in the shower, so afterwards I filled a travel container with the scrub to keep in the shower, problem solved. Overall, this is a phenomenal skincare product I highly recommend. I purchased this with a discount so I could test and review, but my opinion is how I honestly feel about the product.

review_text:
I know it says "Men's" on there, but I am a woman, and I use this razor. I just happen to have very coarse hair on my legs. Lady shavers don't do it for me. In fact, I've always had to use 2 razors, a men's for the legs and a women's for the underarms. I know, more information than you wanted, but it's relevant.

This razor is the only one I have ever had that works for everything. Oh, I had some really nasty razor burn before I got the hang of it, but since then, it's been great! No cleaning and maintaining 2 razors any more.

I have found with this razor, that putting pressure on it is a big no-no. If I do that, it will tear up my skin big time. I have to just sort of guide/glide it over the area, no pressure on it, and it does a beautiful job without the razor burn. Now, I honestly don't know how that would go for a guy and his face, but that's how it works for me on ALL parts I shave.

This razor only needs charged about every two to three weeks. There is no indicator system on this razor, and when it needs charged, it just quits. If you keep playing with the on/off button, it will run for 2 or 3 more minutes, but that's it. It takes one hour (about) to recharge, much better than any razor I ever had before.

This razor is easy to clean, just run the head under the sink, shake the water off, and let it dry out. I do that once a week. Easy peasy.

Like I said, I've no idea how my experience might translate for a guy. I gave it 4 stars because of the lack of a recharge indicator. Other that, it is wonderful for me.

I applied the base coat and found that it was a bit thicker than expected. I have used some other brands of gel base coats and the consistency is generally thinner. Most of the polishes are light but not to the point of being watery. It's the same consistency as non gel polishes which I prefer. However, some of the glittered polishes that have confetti included are pretty thick and almost chunky. I'm not sure that it will last long based off the consistency at first use. I hope they do last because those are some of the prettiest colors. I love that unlike other brands of gel polishes that I've used, this brand's glitter polishes are not opaque. It's both shiny and the color is dense. I put on the color A708 first cured it then topped it with A707 while leaving some of the color A708 visible. I then layered it with the color A712 on a diagonal so that some of the color A708 would still be visible. I know the colors are hard to make out from the photo. I realized after the fact that I probably should've started with the color A707 or A712 first. I used number A707 and A708 alternating on the remaining toes. I finished it by putting a gloss top coat and cured it with the UV light. I set it to 60 seconds for three rounds just to make sure the polish dried fully. It has been two days and so far so good. The photo of my toenails were taken on day two.
Overall, I love the color selections. They're very pretty hence why I chose to use 3 colors at once. I can't wait to use the rest of the colors. I really love this set. I like to paint my toes colors that are compatible with the current season so these color selections are perfect for my seasonal needs. I wish the bottle sizes were a bit larger but I guess they make up for that by offering a lot of color selections. Also, you don't need to cake on the polish. A little goes a long way. The only drawback is that the base coat seemed a bit too thick so it may not last, but it could be an isolated case with this set. I was so excited to try the poly gel and thought it would be so easy but it wasn't that simple. You receive a set of 8 colors. The tubes are small so I'm not sure how many uses you'll get out of it. I think you'll get about 2 full uses per tube maybe 3. I had a hard time with this poly gel. I squeezed a small amount onto the nail former and smoothed it out evenly. I put a thin layer of base coat on my nail and cured it. Then I put the nail former filled with the poly gel onto my nail but it wouldn't stay in place. The former kept lifting from my nail. I tried putting more and putting less to see if it'll help the former stay in place but it didn't work. I cured it for 120 seconds twice and even then the center of my nail where the former lifted from didn't turn solid. I even have a couple bubble pockets. Also while curing, the poly gel flowed to the right side of the former and created a thick dried buildup underneath the nail. I think the shape of the former is what caused this and because the former needs to be lighter. I came to this conclusion because I have used another poly gel brand where the former was feather light and less curvy and was able to cure the gel completely and the former stayed in place until cured. I didn't have any buildup underneath my nail either and got it on the first try. Otherwise, the poly gel was very easy to shape after being cured. I used the clear and I love how natural it looks but it feels like I have an acrylic nail. I might use it in combination with the nail extention in the future. Hopefully that will stop the buildup from happening. It also comes with a free gift of glitter. Overall, the set it okay. May be better suited for more advanced users.

review_title: A fairly basic 'stache wax with good hold and tackiness
review_text:
I'm the proud owner of a rather glorious handlebar moustache (though I say so myself). So when a 'stache wax or grooming product comes available on Vine I'll usually request it if it's anything in the neighborhood of what I usually like.

I like firm or strong hold waxes with significant tackiness. I won't even consider a wax unless it either states a strong hold or a tacky hold or both. As a reference my other favorite common varieties of moustache wax include (in order of preference descending):
Firehouse Moustache Wax - Tacky (Wacky Tacky)
The Vintage Grooming Company - Death Grip
Can You Handlebar - Primary

All of these are either exceptionally tacky or very strong in hold or both. I have tried many other waxes by various brands over the last several years but the ones above are my favorites and the ones that I feel are most worth mentioning in comparison to this product.

I would rate this wax as slightly less tacky than the Firehouse Moustache wax Tacky and slightly less stiffness than the Can You Handlebar Primary wax. Death Grip has it's own unique and weird properties (and I don't love the way it smells) so it is hard to direct compare :-)

As far as my general ranking I'd put this solidly in the top 5 waxes I've ever tried though, probably just under the three above and maaaybe 5th place after maybe Fisticuffs Strong Hold (which also has some pine resin for stickiness).

Unscented is good! Nothing worse than a cloying scent right up under your nose holes all day long!

Anyway, it has a strong hold for shaping if you like a strong curl as I do, combined with a tacky hold if you get a lot of stray and fly away hairs as I do. While my "go to" product is still Firehouse Tacky, and this has not replaced that, this is a worthy offering. The tree embossment on the wax is cute and I kinda dig that they give you the recipe.

The price point at the time of this writing is very fair. If you're in need of a good strong hold tacky wax I'd say give this product a shot!
